entries.original: Ampacity is the maximum current, in amps, that a conductor can carry under stated conditions without overheating. This calculator starts with NEC Table 310.16, applies NEC Table 310.15(B)(1) ambient correction and NEC Table 310.15(C)(1) conductor adjustment, then applies NEC 110.14(C) and 240.4(D) limits.
entries.translation: La ampacidad es la corriente máxima, en amperios, que un conductor puede transportar en las condiciones indicadas sin sobrecalentarse. Esta calculadora comienza con NEC Table 310.16, aplica la corrección ambiental de NEC Table 310.15(B)(1) y el ajuste de conductores de NEC Table 310.15(C)(1), y después aplica los límites de NEC 110.14(C) y 240.4(D).
entries.backTranslation: Ampacity is the maximum current, in amperes, that a conductor can carry under the stated conditions without overheating. This calculator starts with NEC Table 310.16, applies the ambient correction from NEC Table 310.15(B)(1) and the conductor adjustment from NEC Table 310.15(C)(1), and then applies the limits of NEC 110.14(C) and 240.4(D).

entries.backTranslation: Start with the insulation column, correct for heat and bundled conductors, and see exactly which safety limit controls.

entries.original: This U.S. edition uses the verified NEC Table 310.16 base ampacities, Table 310.15(B)(1) ambient factors, Table 310.15(C)(1) conductor factors, 110.14(C) termination limits, and 240.4(D) small-conductor caps. It never interpolates a missing value.
entries.translation: Esta edición de Estados Unidos usa las ampacidades base verificadas de NEC Table 310.16, los factores ambientales de Table 310.15(B)(1), los factores de conductores de Table 310.15(C)(1), los límites de terminación de 110.14(C) y los límites para conductores pequeños de 240.4(D). Nunca interpola un valor faltante.
entries.backTranslation: This United States edition uses the verified base ampacities from NEC Table 310.16, the ambient factors from Table 310.15(B)(1), the conductor factors from Table 310.15(C)(1), the termination limits of 110.14(C), and the small conductor limits of 240.4(D). It never interpolates a missing value.

entries.original: Use the insulation rating for the starting ampacity column, then separately choose the termination rating. THHN is normally a 90°C insulation, while marked equipment commonly limits the final result to the 75°C column. NM-B and unmarked equipment use the 60°C termination limit.
entries.translation: Use la temperatura nominal del aislamiento para la ampacidad inicial y luego elija por separado la temperatura nominal de la terminación. THHN normalmente tiene aislamiento de 90°C, mientras que los equipos marcados suelen limitar el resultado final a la columna de 75°C. NM-B y los equipos sin marcar usan el límite de terminación de 60°C.
entries.backTranslation: Use the insulation temperature rating for the initial ampacity and then separately choose the termination temperature rating. THHN normally has 90°C insulation, while marked equipment usually limits the final result to the 75°C column. NM-B and unlabeled equipment use the 60°C termination limit.

entries.original: All the grounds together count as one wire's worth of space (that's the code rule — not one each).
entries.translation: Todos los conductores de puesta a tierra juntos ocupan el espacio de un conductor; esa es la regla, no uno por cada conductor.
entries.backTranslation: All grounding conductors together occupy the space of one conductor; that is the rule, not one for each conductor.

entries.original: Canadian rule: every pair of insulated wire connectors counts as one conductor's worth of space. This aggregate input uses the largest conductor listed above.
entries.translation: Regla canadiense: cada par de conectores aislados cuenta como un volumen de conductor. Esta entrada conjunta usa el conductor más grande indicado arriba.
entries.backTranslation: Canadian rule: each pair of insulated wire connectors counts as one conductor allowance. This aggregate input uses the largest conductor listed above.

entries.original: Clamps built inside the box count as one conductor's allowance, using the largest conductor listed above. Connectors that stay outside the box don't count.
entries.translation: Las abrazaderas internas cuentan como un volumen del conductor más grande indicado arriba. Los conectores fuera de la caja no cuentan.
entries.backTranslation: Internal clamps count as one allowance of the largest conductor listed above. Connectors outside the box do not count.

entries.original: Count every hot and neutral that enters the box — including any that pass straight through unbroken (those count too). Don't count ground wires here (next question), and don't count pigtails that start and end inside the box.
entries.translation: Cuente cada conductor de fase y neutro que entra en la caja, incluidos los que la atraviesan sin cortarse. No cuente aquí los conductores de puesta a tierra ni las colas de conexión que comienzan y terminan dentro de la caja.
entries.backTranslation: Count each phase and neutral conductor that enters the box, including those that pass through it uncut. Do not count grounding conductors here or pigtails that begin and end inside the box.

entries.original: Cram too many wires into a box and connections get stressed, insulation gets nicked, and heat builds up — a classic cause of failed inspections and flickering circuits. The U.S. electrical code (NEC 314.16) assigns every wire a space allowance based on its size, and the box must have at least that much room.
entries.translation: Una caja sobrecargada fuerza las conexiones, daña el aislamiento y acumula calor. Es una causa habitual de inspecciones fallidas y circuitos intermitentes. NEC 314.16 asigna a cada calibre del conductor un volumen mínimo, y la caja debe ofrecer al menos ese espacio.
entries.backTranslation: An overloaded box strains connections, damages insulation, and accumulates heat. It is a common cause of failed inspections and intermittent circuits. NEC 314.16 assigns each conductor gauge a minimum volume, and the box must provide at least that space.

entries.original: Do pass-through wires count toward box fill?
entries.translation: ¿Los conductores que atraviesan la caja cuentan para el llenado de caja?
entries.backTranslation: Do conductors that pass through the box count toward box fill?

entries.original: Each hot or neutral entering the box = 1 count — including wires that pass straight through unbroken (those count once too). Each device (switch/outlet) = 2 counts. All ground wires together = 1 count (with more than four grounds, each extra adds a ¼ count under the 2020 rules). Built-in cable clamps = 1 count. Pigtails that live entirely inside the box are free. Multiply the counts by your wire size's space allowance and compare to the box volume — we do exactly that, and show the math.
entries.translation: Cada conductor de fase o neutro que entra en la caja = 1, incluidos los que la atraviesan sin cortarse. Cada dispositivo (interruptor o tomacorriente) = 2. Todos los conductores de puesta a tierra juntos = 1; si hay más de cuatro, cada conductor adicional suma ¼ según las reglas de 2020. Las abrazaderas internas = 1. Las colas de conexión que permanecen dentro de la caja no cuentan. Multiplicamos el total por el volumen correspondiente al calibre del conductor y lo comparamos con el volumen de la caja.
entries.backTranslation: Each phase or neutral conductor that enters the box = 1, including those that pass through it uncut. Each device (switch or receptacle) = 2. All grounding conductors together = 1; if there are more than four, each additional conductor adds ¼ under the 2020 rules. Internal clamps = 1. Pigtails that remain inside the box do not count. We multiply the total by the volume corresponding to the conductor gauge and compare it with the box volume.

entries.original: Is your junction or device box big enough? Count what's in it, get a clear fits / doesn't-fit answer.
entries.translation: ¿Tiene su caja de conexiones o dispositivos el tamaño suficiente? Cuente su contenido y obtenga una respuesta clara.
entries.backTranslation: Is your junction or device box large enough? Count its contents and get a clear answer.

entries.original: Add one row for each conductor size. Most homes use 14 AWG (15 A circuits) or 12 AWG (20 A circuits).
entries.translation: Agregue una fila por cada calibre del conductor. La mayoría de las viviendas usa 14 AWG (circuitos de 15 A) o 12 AWG (circuitos de 20 A).
entries.backTranslation: Add one row for each conductor size. Most homes use 14 AWG (15 A circuits) or 12 AWG (20 A circuits).

entries.original: NEC 314.16 assigns each wire size a volume allowance (for example 2.25 cubic inches for 12 AWG). Count each hot or neutral entering the box as one, each device such as a switch or receptacle as two, all ground wires together as one, and internal cable clamps as one — the total times the allowance must not exceed the box volume.
entries.translation: NEC 314.16 asigna un volumen a cada calibre del conductor; por ejemplo, 2.25 pulgadas cúbicas para 12 AWG. Cuente una vez cada conductor de fase o neutro, dos veces cada dispositivo, una vez todos los conductores de puesta a tierra juntos y una vez las abrazaderas internas. El total multiplicado por el volumen asignado no debe superar el volumen de la caja.
entries.backTranslation: NEC 314.16 assigns a volume to each conductor gauge; for example, 2.25 cubic inches for 12 AWG. Count each phase or neutral conductor once, each device twice, all grounding conductors together once, and internal clamps once. The total multiplied by the assigned volume must not exceed the box volume.

entries.original: Under NEC Chapter 9, one wire may fill 53% of a conduit's internal area, two wires 31%, and three or more wires 40%. The calculation uses the official cross-section areas for the wire type and the conduit type.
entries.translation: Según NEC Chapter 9, un conductor puede ocupar 53% del área interior del tubo conduit; dos conductores, 31%; y tres o más, 40%. El cálculo usa las áreas transversales oficiales del conductor y del tipo de tubo conduit.
entries.backTranslation: According to NEC Chapter 9, one conductor may occupy 53% of the conduit's interior area; two conductors, 31%; and three or more, 40%. The calculation uses the official cross-sectional areas for the conductor and conduit type.

entries.original: Wires need free space in a conduit — jam it full and you can't pull them through, and they can overheat. The standard U.S. limits (NEC Chapter 9): one wire may fill

entries.backTranslation: Conductors need free space inside the conduit. If it is overfilled, you will not be able to pull them and they may overheat. Standard U.S. limits (NEC Chapter 9): one conductor may occupy

entries.original: Almost always one of two things: some tools want round-trip wire length where others want one-way distance (VoltDrop always uses one-way and doubles it internally), and some use slightly different resistance values for the wire. VoltDrop shows its full calculation so you can check its numbers against any other tool.
entries.translation: Casi siempre se debe a una de dos cosas: algunos calculadores piden el recorrido de ida y vuelta y otros piden la distancia en un solo sentido (VoltDrop siempre usa la distancia en un solo sentido y la duplica internamente); otros usan valores de resistencia ligeramente distintos. VoltDrop muestra el cálculo completo para que pueda compararlo.
entries.backTranslation: It is almost always due to one of two things: some calculators ask for the round-trip run and others ask for the one-way distance (VoltDrop always uses the one-way distance and doubles it internally); others use slightly different resistance values. VoltDrop shows the complete calculation so you can compare it.

entries.original: This result sizes the conductor for ampacity (heat) and voltage drop (distance). It does not size the whole circuit.
entries.translation: Este resultado dimensiona el conductor por ampacidad (calor) y caída de tensión (distancia). No dimensiona el circuito completo.
entries.backTranslation: This result sizes the conductor by ampacity (heat) and voltage drop (distance). It does not size the complete circuit.

entries.original: The yes/no choice treats the entire entered load as continuous or noncontinuous. It does not model a mix of the two.
entries.translation: La opción sí/no trata toda la carga ingresada como continua o no continua. No modela una combinación de ambas.
entries.backTranslation: The yes/no option treats the entire entered load as continuous or noncontinuous. It does not model a combination of both.

entries.original: The widely used rule of thumb (based on a recommendation in the U.S. National Electrical Code): keep the drop on a branch circuit at or under 3%, and the total from your panel to the device at or under 5%. These are guidelines for good performance, not laws — low-voltage systems like 12 V solar are often even stricter, because 3% of 12 V hurts a lot more than 3% of 240 V.
entries.translation: La recomendación ampliamente usada del U.S. National Electrical Code es mantener la caída de tensión de un circuito derivado en 3% o menos, y el total desde el tablero hasta el dispositivo en 5% o menos. Son recomendaciones de buen funcionamiento, no requisitos legales generales. Los sistemas de baja tensión, como el solar de 12 V, suelen necesitar un objetivo más estricto porque 3% de 12 V afecta mucho más que 3% de 240 V.
entries.backTranslation: The widely used recommendation of the U.S. National Electrical Code is to keep the voltage drop of a branch circuit at 3% or less, and the total from the panel to the device at 5% or less. These are good-performance recommendations, not general legal requirements. Low-voltage systems, such as 12 V solar, often need a stricter target because 3% of 12 V has a much greater effect than 3% of 240 V.

entries.original: Wire has resistance, so some voltage is lost as heat before reaching the device. The widely used rule of thumb, based on a recommendation in the U.S. National Electrical Code, is to keep the drop on a branch circuit at or under 3% and the total from panel to device at or under 5%. These are performance guidelines, not laws — low-voltage systems like 12 V solar are often stricter.
entries.translation: El conductor tiene resistencia, por lo que parte de la tensión se pierde como calor. Las notas informativas del U.S. National Electrical Code recomiendan un máximo de 3% para el circuito derivado y 5% en total. Son recomendaciones de funcionamiento, no requisitos legales generales. Los sistemas de baja tensión, como el solar de 12 V, suelen ser más estrictos.
entries.backTranslation: The conductor has resistance, so part of the voltage is lost as heat. The informational notes of the U.S. National Electrical Code recommend a maximum of 3% for the branch circuit and 5% total. These are performance recommendations, not general legal requirements. Low-voltage systems, such as 12 V solar, are often stricter.

But Romex (NM-B cable) must use the 60°C column no matter what's printed on the conductors, and #8 NM-B is only good for 40 A — so Romex needs #6. entries.original: CEC Tables 2 and 4 are numerically identical to NEC 310.16 in the 60/75/90°C columns at every shared size. The old “14 AWG copper is 20 A in Canada” difference was real in the 2012 edition. It was harmonized away around 2015–2018. Anyone repeating it is a decade out of date. But the free-air tables still differ. The harmonization is not total.
entries.translation: CEC Tables 2 and 4 son numéricamente idénticas a NEC 310.16 en las columnas de 60/75/90°C para todos los calibres compartidos. Pero las tablas al aire libre todavía difieren. La armonización no es total.
entries.backTranslation: CEC Tables 2 and 4 are numerically identical to NEC 310.16 in the 60/75/90°C columns for all shared wire sizes. The old difference that “14 AWG copper is rated for 20 A in Canada” was real in the 2012 edition. It was harmonized around 2015–2018. Anyone repeating it is a decade out of date. entries.original: Canadian RW90 is unjacketed cross-linked polyethylene. American THHN has a nylon jacket and is thinner for the same copper. RW90 is roughly 14–43% larger in cross-section, depending on size. Canadian EMT is also slightly smaller inside than its US counterpart. The two differences compound.
entries.translation: El RW90 canadiense es polietileno reticulado sin cubierta. El THHN estadounidense tiene una cubierta de nylon y es más delgado para la misma cantidad de cobre. El RW90 tiene aproximadamente 14–43% más sección transversal, según el calibre. El EMT canadiense también es ligeramente más pequeño por dentro que su equivalente estadounidense. Las dos diferencias se acumulan.
entries.backTranslation: Canadian RW90 is unjacketed cross-linked polyethylene. U.S. THHN has a nylon jacket and is thinner for the same amount of copper. RW90 has approximately 14–43% more cross-sectional area, depending on the wire size. Canadian EMT is also slightly smaller inside than its U.S. equivalent. The two differences add up.

entries.original: Nearly every online source we found cites Canadian colour rules as “Rule 4-038.” In the current 26th edition there is no Rule 4-038. entries.translation: Casi todas las fuentes en línea que encontramos citan las reglas canadienses de color como “Rule 4-038”. En la 26th edición actual no existe Rule 4-038. entries.backTranslation: Almost every online source we found cites the Canadian colour rules as “Rule 4-038.” Rule 4-038 does not exist in the current 26th edition. entries.original: We shipped a Canadian conduit-fill calculator that used American conductor dimensions. It gave answers about 50% too permissive. We found it, fixed it, and went looking for what else differs. This is what we found.
entries.translation: Publicamos una calculadora canadiense de llenado de tubo conduit que usaba dimensiones de conductores estadounidenses. Daba respuestas aproximadamente 50% demasiado permisivas. Lo encontramos, lo corregimos y buscamos qué más cambia. Esto fue lo que encontramos.
entries.backTranslation: We published a Canadian conduit-fill calculator that used U.S. conductor dimensions. It gave answers that were approximately 50% too permissive. We found it, corrected it, and looked for what else changes. This is what we found.

entries.backTranslation: A verified map of the differences between the NEC and the Canadian Electrical Code that change real answers.

entries.backTranslation: Nylon T90, by contrast, is within about 2% of THHN. It is the Canadian equivalent of THHN. Conductor type matters more than country.

entries.original: The 3% and 5% figures live in NEC Informational Notes. They are not requirements. In Canada, Rule 8-102 makes voltage drop mandatory. The physics is the same. The legal status is completely different. This is the marquee difference on this list.
entries.translation: Las cifras de 3% y 5% aparecen en las Notas Informativas del NEC. No son requisitos. En Canadá, Rule 8-102 hace obligatoria la caída de tensión. La física es la misma. La condición legal es completamente distinta. Esta es la diferencia principal de la lista.
entries.backTranslation: The 3% and 5% figures appear in the NEC Informational Notes. They are not requirements. In Canada, Rule 8-102 makes voltage drop mandatory. The physics is the same. The legal status is completely different. This is the main difference on the list.

entries.original: 5. Voltage drop: a suggestion in one country, a rule in the other
entries.translation: 5. Caída de tensión: sugerencia en un país, regla en el otro
entries.backTranslation: 5. Voltage drop: a suggestion in one country, a rule in the other

entries.original: The equipment grounding conductor is sized from the feeder breaker per NEC Table 250.122 — for example #8 copper for a 100 A feeder — and must be upsized proportionally if you upsize the hot conductors for voltage drop.
entries.translation: El conductor de puesta a tierra de equipos se dimensiona a partir del interruptor automático del alimentador según NEC Table 250.122 — por ejemplo #8 de cobre para un alimentador de 100 A — y debe aumentarse proporcionalmente si aumentas el calibre de los conductores vivos por caída de tensión.
entries.backTranslation: The equipment grounding conductor is sized from the feeder breaker per NEC Table 250.122 — for example #8 copper for a 100 A feeder — and must be increased proportionally if you increase the size of the live conductors for voltage drop.

entries.backTranslation: About 46 feet one-way at 120 V with a full 20 A load, staying within the 3% voltage-drop planning target (about 91 feet at 240 V). Lighter real loads reach proportionally farther.

entries.translation: ¿Calculas con los 20 A del interruptor automático o con los amperios de la carga real? Los foros se dividen 50/50 en esto. Nuestra tabla usa la capacidad nominal del interruptor automático (el peor caso, seguro para planear); si conoces la carga real, úsala en la
entries.backTranslation: Do you calculate with the breaker's 20 A or with the amps of the actual load? The forums split 50/50 on this. Our table uses the breaker's rated capacity (the worst case, safe for planning); if you know the actual load, use it in the

entries.original: The circuit still works but delivers lower voltage at the far end: motors start hard and overheat, LEDs flicker, chargers and heaters underperform, and energy is wasted as heat in the wire. Fix it with thicker wire, a shorter route, or a higher voltage.
entries.translation: El circuito sigue funcionando, pero entrega menos tensión en el extremo lejano: los motores arrancan forzados y se sobrecalientan, los LED parpadean, los cargadores y los calefactores rinden menos, y se desperdicia energía en forma de calor en el conductor. Corrígelo con un conductor más grueso, una ruta más corta o una tensión más alta.
entries.backTranslation: The circuit still works, but it delivers less voltage at the far end: motors start under strain and overheat, LEDs flicker, chargers and heaters perform worse, and energy is wasted as heat in the conductor. Fix it with a thicker conductor, a shorter route, or a higher voltage.

entries.original: Diagram: measure the one-way distance from panel to load; current travels out on one wire and back on the other
entries.translation: Diagrama: mide la distancia en un solo sentido del tablero a la carga; la corriente va por un conductor y regresa por el otro
entries.backTranslation: Diagram: measure the one-way distance from the panel to the load; the current goes out on one conductor and returns on the other

entries.original: Do I measure wire distance one-way or round trip for voltage drop?
entries.translation: ¿Mido la distancia del conductor en un solo sentido o el recorrido de ida y vuelta para la caída de tensión?
entries.backTranslation: Do I measure the wire distance one-way or the round trip for voltage drop?

entries.original: Increase the wire size (each AWG step cuts drop about 21%), raise the system voltage (240 V vs 120 V is a 4x improvement for the same watts), shorten the run, or use a step-up transformer for very long distances.
entries.translation: Aumenta el calibre del conductor (cada paso de AWG reduce la caída cerca de 21%), sube la tensión del sistema (240 V frente a 120 V es una mejora de 4x con los mismos watts), acorta el tramo, o usa un transformador elevador para distancias muy largas.
entries.backTranslation: Increase the wire size (each AWG step reduces the drop by about 21%), raise the system voltage (240 V versus 120 V is a 4x improvement at the same watts), shorten the run, or use a step-up transformer for very long distances.

entries.original: is the round trip — current flows out and back, so measure your distance
entries.translation: es el recorrido de ida y vuelta — la corriente va y regresa, así que mide tu distancia
entries.backTranslation: is the round trip — the current goes out and comes back, so measure your distance

entries.original: Measure one-way, from the source to the load. The standard formula's factor of 2 accounts for the round trip. Entering round-trip length into a one-way calculator doubles your error — the most common cause of disagreeing results.
entries.translation: Mide en un solo sentido, de la fuente a la carga. El factor 2 de la fórmula estándar ya toma en cuenta el recorrido de ida y vuelta. Meter la longitud de ida y vuelta en una calculadora de un solo sentido duplica tu error — la causa más común de resultados que no coinciden.
entries.backTranslation: Measure one-way, from the source to the load. The factor of 2 in the standard formula already accounts for the round trip. Putting the round-trip length into a one-way calculator doubles your error — the most common cause of results that don't match.

entries.original: measure THIS: one-way distance (the formula doubles it)
entries.translation: mide ESTO: distancia en un solo sentido (la fórmula la duplica)
entries.backTranslation: measure THIS: one-way distance (the formula doubles it)

entries.original: Mostly it's a performance problem — dim lights, hot motors, slow chargers — but chronically undervolted motors can overheat and fail, and the lost energy becomes heat in the wiring. Severe drop is a sign the circuit needs redesign.
entries.translation: En general es un problema de desempeño — luces tenues, motores calientes, cargadores lentos — pero los motores con tensión crónicamente baja pueden sobrecalentarse y fallar, y la energía perdida se convierte en calor en el cableado. Una caída severa es señal de que el circuito necesita rediseñarse.
entries.backTranslation: Generally it is a performance problem — dim lights, hot motors, slow chargers — but motors with chronically low voltage can overheat and fail, and the lost energy turns into heat in the wiring. Severe drop is a sign the circuit needs to be redesigned.

entries.original: shorten the route
entries.translation: acorta la ruta
entries.backTranslation: shorten the route

entries.original: . Too much — go to #10 or shorten the run.
entries.translation: . Demasiado — sube a #10 o acorta el tramo.
entries.backTranslation: . Too much — go up to #10 or shorten the run.

entries.original: A 32 A continuous charger produces a 40 A sizing load: 32 A × 1.25 = 40 A. The charger must be set and listed for that circuit, and the conductor still has to pass the installation's ampacity and distance checks.
entries.translation: Un cargador continuo de 32 A produce una carga de dimensionamiento de 40 A: 32 A × 1.25 = 40 A. El cargador debe estar configurado y certificado para ese circuito, y el conductor todavía tiene que pasar las verificaciones de ampacidad y distancia de la instalación.
entries.backTranslation: A continuous 32 A charger produces a sizing load of 40 A: 32 A × 1.25 = 40 A. The charger must be configured and certified for that circuit, and the conductor still has to pass the installation's ampacity and distance checks.

entries.original: A range is the classic 40 A circuit. A 32 A continuous EV load also lands on a 40 A circuit because 32 A × 1.25 = 40 A; confirm the charger's setting and installation instructions.
entries.translation: Una estufa es el circuito clásico de 40 A. Una carga continua de 32 A de un cargador de vehículo eléctrico también cae en un circuito de 40 A porque 32 A × 1.25 = 40 A; confirma la configuración del cargador y las instrucciones de instalación.
entries.backTranslation: A stove is the classic 40 A circuit. A continuous 32 A load from an electric vehicle charger also falls on a 40 A circuit because 32 A × 1.25 = 40 A; confirm the charger's configuration and the installation instructions.

entries.original: The verified ampacity table gives #8 copper 40 A in the 60°C column and 50 A in the 75°C column. That makes #8 the minimum at ordinary conditions in either case, but the available headroom is different.
entries.translation: La tabla de ampacidad verificada le da al #8 de cobre 40 A en la columna de 60°C y 50 A en la columna de 75°C. Eso hace que el #8 sea el mínimo en condiciones ordinarias en cualquiera de los dos casos, pero el margen disponible es distinto.
entries.backTranslation: The verified ampacity table gives #8 copper 40 A in the 60°C column and 50 A in the 75°C column. That makes #8 the minimum under ordinary conditions in either case, but the available margin is different.

entries.original: Our verified calculator selects #6 copper (26,240 circular mils): 2 × 12.9 × 40 × 150 ÷ 26,240 = 5.90 V, or 2.46% of 240 V. #8 passes ampacity but does not meet the 3% drop target at this distance.
entries.translation: Nuestra calculadora verificada selecciona #6 de cobre (26,240 cmil): 2 × 12.9 × 40 × 150 ÷ 26,240 = 5.90 V, o 2.46% de 240 V. El #8 pasa la ampacidad, pero no cumple el objetivo de caída del 3% a esta distancia.
entries.backTranslation: Our verified calculator selects #6 copper (26,240 cmil): 2 × 12.9 × 40 × 150 ÷ 26,240 = 5.90 V, or 2.46% of 240 V. #8 passes ampacity, but does not meet the 3% drop target at this distance.

entries.original: Yes, under ordinary conditions when the wiring method and termination rating support the applicable ampacity column. Heat, bundled conductors, and long distance can require a larger conductor.
entries.translation: Sí, en condiciones ordinarias cuando el método de cableado y la clasificación de terminación respaldan la columna de ampacidad aplicable. El calor, los conductores agrupados y la distancia larga pueden exigir un conductor más grueso.
entries.backTranslation: Yes, under ordinary conditions when the wiring method and the termination rating support the applicable ampacity column. Heat, bundled conductors, and long distance can demand a thicker conductor.

entries.original: This table starts with the NEC 310.12 dwelling-service minimum, then raises the conductor when needed to keep calculated drop at or under the 3% planning target. It uses 240 V, the full 100 A rating, and one-way distance.
entries.translation: Esta tabla parte del mínimo de acometida residencial del NEC 310.12, y luego sube el calibre del conductor cuando es necesario para mantener la caída calculada en 3% o menos como objetivo de planeación. Usa 240 V, la capacidad completa de 100 A y distancia en un solo sentido.
entries.backTranslation: This table starts from the NEC 310.12 residential service minimum, and then upsizes the conductor gauge when necessary to keep the calculated drop at 3% or less as a planning target. It uses 240 V, the full 100 A capacity, and one-way distance.

entries.original: 100 A × 83% = 83 A → 4 AWG copper (85 A at 75 °C); 2 AWG aluminum (90 A at 75 °C).
entries.translation: 100 A × 83% = 83 A → 4 AWG de cobre (85 A a 75 °C); 2 AWG de aluminio (90 A a 75 °C).
entries.backTranslation: 100 A × 83% = 83 A → 4 AWG copper (85 A at 75 °C); 2 AWG aluminum (90 A at 75 °C).

entries.original: No ampacity adjustment or correction factors can be required.
entries.translation: No se puede requerir ningún ajuste de ampacidad ni factor de corrección.
entries.backTranslation: No ampacity adjustment or correction factor can be required.

entries.original: No. NM/Romex is treated as a 60 °C assembly, while this dwelling-service allowance requires conductors rated 75 °C or better.
entries.translation: No. El NM/Romex se trata como un conjunto de 60 °C, mientras que esta reducción de acometida residencial exige conductores clasificados a 75 °C o más.
entries.backTranslation: No. NM/Romex is treated as a 60 °C assembly, while this residential service reduction demands conductors rated at 75 °C or more.

entries.original: Yes for a qualifying 100 A dwelling service: the 83% calculation requires 83 A, and 4 AWG copper is rated 85 A in the verified 75 °C table. Otherwise, check the actual method in the Ampacity Check tool.
entries.translation: Sí, para una acometida residencial de 100 A que califique: el cálculo del 83% exige 83 A, y el 4 AWG de cobre está clasificado en 85 A en la tabla verificada de 75 °C. De lo contrario, revisa el método real en la herramienta Verificación de ampacidad.
entries.backTranslation: Yes, for a qualifying 100 A residential service: the 83% calculation demands 83 A, and 4 AWG copper is rated at 85 A in the verified 75 °C table. Otherwise, check the actual method in the Ampacity Check tool.

entries.original: The service or feeder rating must be from 100 A through 400 A.
entries.translation: La capacidad de la acometida o el alimentador debe estar en el rango de 100 A a 400 A, inclusive.
entries.backTranslation: The capacity of the service or the feeder must be in the range of 100 A to 400 A, inclusive.

entries.original: A 100 A dwelling service that meets NEC 310.12 can use 4 AWG copper or 2 AWG aluminum. That is a service answer, not a general 100 A feeder answer.
entries.translation: Una acometida residencial de 100 A que cumple el NEC 310.12 puede usar 4 AWG de cobre o 2 AWG de aluminio. Esa es una respuesta para acometida, no una respuesta general para un alimentador de 100 A.
entries.backTranslation: A 100 A residential service that meets NEC 310.12 can use 4 AWG copper or 2 AWG aluminum. That is an answer for a service, not a general answer for a 100 A feeder.

entries.original: Plain 75 °C table: 100 A → 3 AWG copper (100 A) or 1 AWG aluminum (100 A).
entries.translation: Tabla simple a 75 °C: 100 A → 3 AWG de cobre (100 A) o 1 AWG de aluminio (100 A).
entries.backTranslation: Simple table at 75 °C: 100 A → 3 AWG copper (100 A) or 1 AWG aluminum (100 A).

entries.original: Without the dwelling-service allowance, use the ordinary ampacity table and the temperature method the installation permits. This includes non-dwelling work and any installation where derating applies. At 75 °C, the verified table selects 3 AWG copper or 1 AWG aluminum. A 60 °C method needs its own lookup and cannot borrow the 75 °C result.
entries.translation: Sin la reducción de acometida residencial, usa la tabla de ampacidad ordinaria y el método de temperatura que permita la instalación. Esto incluye trabajos que no son de vivienda y cualquier instalación donde aplique una reducción de ampacidad. A 75 °C, la tabla verificada selecciona 3 AWG de cobre o 1 AWG de aluminio. Un método de 60 °C necesita su propia consulta y no puede tomar prestado el resultado de 75 °C.
entries.backTranslation: Without the residential service reduction, use the ordinary ampacity table and the temperature method that the installation permits. This includes non-dwelling work and any installation where an ampacity reduction applies. At 75 °C, the verified table selects 3 AWG copper or 1 AWG aluminum. A 60 °C method needs its own lookup and cannot borrow the 75 °C result.

entries.original: Conductors must be rated 75 °C or better. NM/Romex is a 60 °C assembly, so it is out.
entries.translation: Los conductores deben estar clasificados a 75 °C o más. El NM/Romex es un conjunto de 60 °C, así que queda descartado.
entries.backTranslation: The conductors must be rated at 75 °C or more. NM/Romex is a 60 °C assembly, so it is ruled out.

entries.original: Dwelling service or a feeder carrying the entire dwelling load only — never a branch circuit or a non-dwelling installation.
entries.translation: Solo una acometida residencial o un alimentador que lleve toda la carga de la vivienda — nunca un circuito derivado ni una instalación que no sea de vivienda.
entries.backTranslation: Only a residential service or a feeder that carries the dwelling's entire load — never a branch circuit nor a non-dwelling installation.

entries.original: A 48 A continuous charger produces a 60 A sizing load: 48 A × 1.25 = 60 A. Confirm the charger's permitted setting, wiring method, terminal ratings, and local requirements.
entries.translation: Un cargador continuo de 48 A produce una carga de dimensionamiento de 60 A: 48 A × 1.25 = 60 A. Confirma la configuración permitida del cargador, el método de cableado, la clasificación de las terminales y los requisitos locales.
entries.backTranslation: A continuous 48 A charger produces a sizing load of 60 A: 48 A × 1.25 = 60 A. Confirm the charger's permitted configuration, the wiring method, the terminal rating, and local requirements.

entries.original: A 48 A continuous EV charger produces a 60 A sizing load: 48 A × 1.25 = 60 A. Other common jobs include sub-panel feeds and larger heat-pump or mini-split circuits; follow the equipment nameplate.
entries.translation: Un cargador continuo de vehículo eléctrico de 48 A produce una carga de dimensionamiento de 60 A: 48 A × 1.25 = 60 A. Otros trabajos comunes incluyen alimentadores de subtablero y circuitos más grandes de bomba de calor o minisplit; sigue la placa del equipo.
entries.backTranslation: A continuous 48 A electric vehicle charger produces a sizing load of 60 A: 48 A × 1.25 = 60 A. Other common jobs include subpanel feeders and larger heat pump or mini-split circuits; follow the equipment nameplate.

entries.original: The copper answer splits by temperature column: #6 at 75°C, but #4 at 60°C. Check the cable type and terminal markings before choosing between them.
entries.translation: La respuesta en cobre se divide según la columna de temperatura: #6 a 75°C, pero #4 a 60°C. Revisa el tipo de cable y las marcas de las terminales antes de elegir entre ellos.
entries.backTranslation: The copper answer splits according to the temperature column: #6 at 75°C, but #4 at 60°C. Check the cable type and the terminal markings before choosing between them.

entries.original: The verified 75°C column gives #6 copper 65 A, so it passes 60 A. The verified 60°C column gives #6 copper only 55 A, so that method selects #4 copper at 70 A. This page does not use a next-size-up exception to make #6 pass at 60°C.
entries.translation: La columna verificada de 75°C le da al #6 de cobre 65 A, así que pasa los 60 A. La columna verificada de 60°C le da al #6 de cobre solo 55 A, así que ese método selecciona #4 de cobre a 70 A. Esta página no usa una excepción de subir un calibre para hacer que el #6 pase a 60°C.
entries.backTranslation: The verified 75°C column gives #6 copper 65 A, so it passes 60 A. The verified 60°C column gives #6 copper only 55 A, so that method selects #4 copper at 70 A. This page does not use a next-size-up exception to make #6 pass at 60°C.

entries.original: Our verified calculator selects #4 copper (41,740 circular mils): 2 × 12.9 × 60 × 150 ÷ 41,740 = 5.56 V, or 2.32% of 240 V. Distance now governs over the #6 copper 75°C ampacity floor.
entries.translation: Nuestra calculadora verificada selecciona #4 de cobre (41,740 cmil): 2 × 12.9 × 60 × 150 ÷ 41,740 = 5.56 V, o 2.32% de 240 V. Ahora la distancia manda por encima del piso de ampacidad del #6 de cobre a 75°C.
entries.backTranslation: Our verified calculator selects #4 copper (41,740 cmil): 2 × 12.9 × 60 × 150 ÷ 41,740 = 5.56 V, or 2.32% of 240 V. Now the distance governs above the ampacity floor of #6 copper at 75°C.

entries.original: A TT-30 RV receptacle is 120 V. Start with 10 AWG copper at ordinary distances, then use the 120 V table or calculator for the actual one-way run.
entries.translation: Un receptáculo TT-30 para casa rodante es de 120 V. Empieza con 10 AWG de cobre en distancias comunes, y luego usa la tabla de 120 V o la calculadora para el tramo real en un solo sentido.
entries.backTranslation: A TT-30 receptacle for a motorhome is 120 V. Start with 10 AWG copper at common distances, and then use the 120 V table or the calculator for the actual one-way run.

entries.original: The verified ampacity table supports #8 aluminum at 30 A under ordinary 75°C termination conditions, so aluminum is included. Confirm the conductor type, terminals, and equipment listing before using it.
entries.translation: La tabla de ampacidad verificada respalda el #8 de aluminio a 30 A en condiciones ordinarias de terminación a 75°C, así que el aluminio está incluido. Confirma el tipo de conductor, las terminales y la certificación del equipo antes de usarlo.
entries.backTranslation: The verified ampacity table supports #8 aluminum at 30 A under ordinary conditions with 75°C termination, so aluminum is included. Confirm the conductor type, the terminals, and the equipment certification before using it.

entries.original: No. NEC 240.4(D) caps 12 AWG copper at 20 A for ordinary circuits, so it does not pass a 30 A ampacity check.
entries.translation: No. El NEC 240.4(D) limita el 12 AWG de cobre a 20 A en circuitos comunes, así que no pasa una verificación de ampacidad de 30 A.
entries.backTranslation: No. NEC 240.4(D) limits 12 AWG copper to 20 A on common circuits, so it does not pass a 30 A ampacity check.

entries.original: Start with 10 AWG copper for an ordinary 30 A circuit. A TT-30 RV receptacle is 120 V, while a typical dryer or water-heater circuit is 240 V; that voltage difference changes long-run sizing.
entries.translation: Empieza con 10 AWG de cobre para un circuito común de 30 A. Un receptáculo TT-30 para casa rodante (RV) es de 120 V, mientras que un circuito típico de secadora o calentador de agua es de 240 V; esa diferencia de tensión cambia el dimensionamiento en tramos largos.
entries.backTranslation: Start with 10 AWG copper for a common 30 A circuit. A TT-30 receptacle for a motorhome (RV) is 120 V, while a typical dryer or water heater circuit is 240 V; that voltage difference changes the sizing on long runs.

entries.original: At 120 V, our verified calculator selects #6 copper (26,240 circular mils): 2 × 12.9 × 30 × 100 ÷ 26,240 = 2.95 V, or 2.46%. The 240 V table is smaller because the same volts lost are half the percentage.
entries.translation: A 120 V, nuestra calculadora verificada selecciona #6 de cobre (26,240 cmil): 2 × 12.9 × 30 × 100 ÷ 26,240 = 2.95 V, o 2.46%. La tabla de 240 V es más pequeña porque los mismos volts perdidos son la mitad del porcentaje.
entries.backTranslation: At 120 V, our verified calculator selects #6 copper (26,240 cmil): 2 × 12.9 × 30 × 100 ÷ 26,240 = 2.95 V, or 2.46%. The 240 V table is smaller because the same volts lost are half the percentage.

entries.original: Use 12 AWG copper for an ordinary 20 A branch circuit. NEC 240.4(D) caps 14 AWG copper at 15 A, so it cannot be protected by a 20 A breaker for this ordinary use.
entries.translation: Usa 12 AWG de cobre para un circuito derivado común de 20 A. El NEC 240.4(D) limita el 14 AWG de cobre a 15 A, así que no puede protegerse con un interruptor automático de 20 A para este uso común.
entries.backTranslation: Use 12 AWG copper for a common 20 A branch circuit. NEC 240.4(D) limits 14 AWG copper to 15 A, so it cannot be protected with a 20 A circuit breaker for this common use.

entries.original: NEC 240.4(D) caps 14 AWG copper at 15 A and 12 AWG copper at 20 A for ordinary circuits. A larger raw ampacity in another temperature column does not erase that cap.
entries.translation: El NEC 240.4(D) limita el 14 AWG de cobre a 15 A y el 12 AWG de cobre a 20 A en circuitos comunes. Una ampacidad bruta mayor en otra columna de temperatura no elimina ese límite.
entries.backTranslation: NEC 240.4(D) limits 14 AWG copper to 15 A and 12 AWG copper to 20 A on common circuits. A higher raw ampacity in another temperature column does not remove that limit.

entries.original: Our verified calculator selects #8 copper (16,510 circular mils): 2 × 12.9 × 20 × 100 ÷ 16,510 = 3.13 V, or 2.6% of 120 V. It passes both the ampacity check and the 3% drop target.
entries.translation: Nuestra calculadora verificada selecciona #8 de cobre (16,510 cmil): 2 × 12.9 × 20 × 100 ÷ 16,510 = 3.13 V, o 2.6% de 120 V. Pasa tanto la verificación de ampacidad como el objetivo de caída del 3%.
entries.backTranslation: Our verified calculator selects #8 copper (16,510 cmil): 2 × 12.9 × 20 × 100 ÷ 16,510 = 3.13 V, or 2.6% of 120 V. It passes both the ampacity check and the 3% drop target.

entries.original: This table begins with the NEC 310.12 dwelling-service minimum, then raises the conductor when the calculated drop would exceed the 3% planning target. It uses 240 V, the full 200 A rating, and one-way distance.
entries.translation: Esta tabla parte del mínimo de acometida residencial del NEC 310.12, y luego sube el calibre del conductor cuando la caída calculada superaría el objetivo de planeación del 3%. Usa 240 V, la capacidad completa de 200 A y distancia en un solo sentido.
entries.backTranslation: This table starts from the NEC 310.12 residential service minimum, and then increases the conductor size when the calculated drop would exceed the 3% planning target. It uses 240 V, the full 200 A capacity, and one-way distance.

entries.original: 200 A × 83% = 166 A → 2/0 AWG copper (175 A at 75 °C); 4/0 AWG aluminum (180 A at 75 °C).
entries.translation: 200 A × 83% = 166 A → 2/0 AWG de cobre (175 A a 75 °C); 4/0 AWG de aluminio (180 A a 75 °C).
entries.backTranslation: 200 A × 83% = 166 A → 2/0 AWG copper (175 A at 75 °C); 4/0 AWG aluminum (180 A at 75 °C).

entries.original: For a qualifying dwelling service, use 4/0 aluminum. Without the allowance, the verified 75 °C table requires 250 kcmil aluminum for 200 A.
entries.translation: Para una acometida residencial que califique, usa 4/0 de aluminio. Sin la reducción, la tabla verificada a 75 °C exige 250 kcmil de aluminio para 200 A.
entries.backTranslation: For a residential service that qualifies, use 4/0 aluminum. Without the reduction, the verified 75 °C table requires 250 kcmil aluminum for 200 A.

entries.original: No ampacity adjustment or correction factors can be required.
entries.translation: No se puede requerir ningún ajuste de ampacidad ni factor de corrección.
entries.backTranslation: No ampacity adjustment or correction factor may be required.

entries.original: No. NM/Romex is a 60 °C assembly, and the dwelling-service allowance requires conductors rated 75 °C or better.
entries.translation: No. El NM/Romex es un conjunto de 60 °C, y la reducción de acometida residencial exige conductores clasificados a 75 °C o más.
entries.backTranslation: No. NM/Romex is a 60 °C assembly, and the residential service reduction requires conductors rated 75 °C or higher.

entries.original: The service or feeder rating must be from 100 A through 400 A.
entries.translation: La capacidad de la acometida o el alimentador debe estar en el rango de 100 A a 400 A, inclusive.
entries.backTranslation: The service or feeder capacity must be in the range of 100 A to 400 A, inclusive.

entries.original: Plain 75 °C table: 200 A → 3/0 AWG copper (200 A) or 250 kcmil aluminum (205 A).
entries.translation: Tabla simple a 75 °C: 200 A → 3/0 AWG de cobre (200 A) o 250 kcmil de aluminio (205 A).
entries.backTranslation: Plain table at 75 °C: 200 A → 3/0 AWG copper (200 A) or 250 kcmil aluminum (205 A).

entries.original: 250 kcmil
entries.translation: 250 kcmil
entries.backTranslation: 250 kcmil

entries.original: 300 kcmil
entries.translation: 300 kcmil
entries.backTranslation: 300 kcmil

entries.original: 400 kcmil
entries.translation: 400 kcmil
entries.backTranslation: 400 kcmil

entries.original: Conductors must be rated 75 °C or better. NM/Romex is a 60 °C assembly, so it is out.
entries.translation: Los conductores deben estar clasificados a 75 °C o más. El NM/Romex es un conjunto de 60 °C, así que queda descartado.
entries.backTranslation: The conductors must be rated 75 °C or higher. NM/Romex is a 60 °C assembly, so it is ruled out.

entries.original: 2/0 AWG copper is the NEC 310.12 dwelling-service answer. 3/0 AWG copper is the plain 310.16 answer at 75 °C when that allowance does not apply. 4/0 AWG aluminum is the dwelling-service aluminum answer; the plain 75 °C table instead selects 250 kcmil aluminum.
entries.translation: 2/0 AWG de cobre es la respuesta de acometida residencial del NEC 310.12. 3/0 AWG de cobre es la respuesta simple del 310.16 a 75 °C cuando esa reducción no aplica. 4/0 AWG de aluminio es la respuesta de acometida residencial en aluminio; la tabla simple a 75 °C selecciona en cambio 250 kcmil de aluminio.
entries.backTranslation: 2/0 AWG copper is the NEC 310.12 residential service answer. 3/0 AWG copper is the plain 310.16 answer at 75 °C when that reduction does not apply. 4/0 AWG aluminum is the residential service answer in aluminum; the plain 75 °C table instead selects 250 kcmil aluminum.

entries.original: Use 2/0 copper for a dwelling service or whole-dwelling feeder that meets every NEC 310.12 condition. Use 3/0 copper for the plain 75 °C Table 310.16 method when the allowance does not apply.
entries.translation: Usa 2/0 de cobre para una acometida residencial o un alimentador de toda la vivienda que cumpla todas las condiciones del NEC 310.12. Usa 3/0 de cobre para el método simple de la Tabla 310.16 a 75 °C cuando la reducción no aplica.
entries.backTranslation: Use 2/0 copper for a residential service or a whole-dwelling feeder that meets all the conditions of NEC 310.12. Use 3/0 copper for the plain Table 310.16 method at 75 °C when the reduction does not apply.

entries.original: Yes, when the 200 A installation qualifies for NEC 310.12 and the conductors and equipment are suitable for aluminum. The 83% requirement is 166 A, and 4/0 aluminum is rated 180 A at 75 °C.
entries.translation: Sí, cuando la instalación de 200 A califica para el NEC 310.12 y los conductores y el equipo son aptos para aluminio. El requisito del 83% es 166 A, y el 4/0 de aluminio está clasificado en 180 A a 75 °C.
entries.backTranslation: Yes, when the 200 A installation qualifies for NEC 310.12 and the conductors and equipment are suitable for aluminum. The 83% requirement is 166 A, and 4/0 aluminum is rated at 180 A at 75 °C.

entries.original: Dwelling service or a feeder carrying the entire dwelling load only — never a branch circuit or a non-dwelling installation.
entries.translation: Solo una acometida residencial o un alimentador que lleve toda la carga de la vivienda — nunca un circuito derivado ni una instalación que no sea de vivienda.
entries.backTranslation: Only a residential service or a feeder that carries the entire dwelling load — never a branch circuit or a non-dwelling installation.

entries.original: After a table passes, we take a fingerprint of it and store that fingerprint in the repository. From then on, if a single digit in that table changes, the verification suite stops before the browser checks and reports the mismatch. Re-verifying the data and deliberately updating the fingerprint are separate human steps, not something the seal can enforce by itself.
entries.translation: Después de que una tabla pasa la revisión, calculamos su huella digital y la guardamos en el repositorio. A partir de entonces, si cambia un solo dígito de esa tabla, el conjunto de verificaciones se detiene antes de las pruebas en el navegador e informa la discrepancia. Volver a verificar los datos y actualizar deliberadamente la huella son pasos humanos separados; el sello no puede imponerlos por sí solo.
entries.backTranslation: After a table passes review, we calculate its digital fingerprint and store it in the repository. From then on, if a single digit in that table changes, the verification suite stops before the browser tests and reports the discrepancy. Rechecking the data and deliberately updating the fingerprint are separate human steps; the seal cannot enforce them on its own.

entries.original: Back-translation catches missing warnings and mangled meaning. It is a screen, not proof.
entries.translation: La traducción inversa detecta advertencias ausentes y significados deformados. Es un filtro, no una prueba definitiva.
entries.backTranslation: Back translation detects missing warnings and distorted meanings. It is a filter, not definitive proof.

entries.original: The seal proves a number hasn't changed without somebody noticing. It doesn't prove the original was right. That's what the multi-source check is for. They're separate protections and they do separate jobs.
entries.translation: El sello demuestra que un número no cambió sin que alguien lo notara. No demuestra que el original fuera correcto. Para eso sirve la comprobación con múltiples fuentes. Son protecciones distintas y cumplen funciones distintas.
entries.backTranslation: The seal proves that a number did not change without someone noticing. It does not prove that the original was correct. That is what cross-checking with multiple sources is for. They are different protections and serve different functions.

entries.original: Codes are adopted locally and amended locally. The edition in force where you're standing may not be the one a table came from.
entries.translation: Los códigos se adoptan y modifican localmente. La edición vigente donde usted está puede no ser la edición de la que provino una tabla.
entries.backTranslation: Codes are adopted and amended locally. The edition currently in effect where you are may not be the edition from which a table came.

entries.original: US ampacity data reflects NEC Table 310.16 and the 310.15(B)(1) correction factors as published in the 2023 edition (NFPA 70). Small-conductor caps come from 240.4(D), conduit fill from Chapter 9 Tables 4 and 5, and box fill from 314.16. These particular tables have been stable across editions. That is why a slightly different adopted edition usually does not change the answer. State and municipal adoption varies; confirm the edition adopted locally.
entries.translation: Los datos de ampacidad de US reflejan NEC Table 310.16 y los factores de corrección de 310.15(B)(1) publicados en la edición de 2023 (NFPA 70). Los límites para conductores pequeños provienen de 240.4(D), el llenado de tubo conduit de Chapter 9 Tables 4 y 5, y el llenado de caja de 314.16. Estas tablas en particular se han mantenido estables entre ediciones. Por eso, una edición adoptada un poco distinta normalmente no cambia la respuesta. La adopción estatal y municipal varía; confirme la edición adoptada localmente.
entries.backTranslation: US ampacity data reflects NEC Table 310.16 and the correction factors in 310.15(B)(1) published in the 2023 edition (NFPA 70). Small conductor limits come from 240.4(D), conduit fill from Chapter 9 Tables 4 and 5, and box fill from 314.16. These particular tables have remained stable between editions. Therefore, a slightly different adopted edition normally does not change the answer. State and municipal adoption varies; confirm the locally adopted edition.

entries.original: Every calculator is driven in all six editions, not just English, and the answer is checked against an expected value — hand-worked for the core voltage-drop cases, and derived from the sealed tables for the rest. We learned this one the hard way: a test run that drove only English once reported a clean pass while the main calculator was dead in four other editions.
entries.translation: Cada calculadora se prueba en las seis ediciones, no solo en inglés, y la respuesta se compara con un valor esperado: calculado a mano para los casos principales de caída de tensión y derivado de las tablas selladas para los demás. Lo aprendimos por las malas: una ejecución que solo probó la edición en inglés dio un resultado limpio mientras la calculadora principal no funcionaba en otras cuatro ediciones.
entries.backTranslation: Each calculator is tested in all six editions, not just in English, and the answer is compared with an expected value: calculated by hand for the main voltage drop cases and derived from the sealed tables for the others. We learned this the hard way: a run that tested only the English edition produced a clean result while the main calculator did not work in four other editions.

entries.original: The numeric-parity check covers the translated guides, the Terms page, and three newer pages, including this one. On those pages, every visible number is compared with its English twin, except for a value explicitly marked as a legitimate locale-specific difference.
entries.translation: La comprobación de paridad numérica cubre las guías traducidas, la página de Términos y tres páginas más recientes, incluida esta. En esas páginas, cada número visible se compara con su equivalente en inglés, salvo los valores marcados expresamente como diferencias legítimas propias del idioma o la región.
entries.backTranslation: The numerical parity check covers the translated guides, the Terms page, and three more recent pages, including this one. On those pages, every visible number is compared with its English equivalent, except for values expressly marked as legitimate language-specific or regional differences.

entries.original: So read the labels rather than assuming. Where the data behind a result hasn't passed for your country, the page tells you so in plain language instead of quietly presenting it as a verified answer.
entries.translation: Así que lea las etiquetas en lugar de dar nada por sentado. Cuando los datos que sustentan un resultado no han pasado la revisión para su país, la página se lo dice con claridad en vez de presentarlo discretamente como una respuesta verificada.
entries.backTranslation: So read the labels instead of taking anything for granted. When the data supporting a result has not passed review for your country, the page tells you clearly instead of quietly presenting it as a verified answer.

entries.original: Your local inspector (AHJ) decides, not us. Confirm the result against the rules actually adopted in your area before you install anything.
entries.translation: La decisión corresponde a su inspector local (AHJ), no a nosotros. Antes de instalar, confirme el resultado con las reglas realmente adoptadas en su zona.
entries.backTranslation: The decision belongs to your local inspector (AHJ), not to us. Before installing, confirm the result against the rules actually adopted in your area.

entries.original: No licensed electrician reviews or approves VoltDrop. Nobody here is holding a licence over this work. If a page ever claims otherwise, it's wrong — tell us.
entries.translation: Ningún electricista con licencia revisa ni avala VoltDrop. Nadie aquí respalda este trabajo con una licencia profesional. Si alguna página afirma lo contrario, está equivocada: avísenos.
entries.backTranslation: No licensed electrician reviews or endorses VoltDrop. No one here backs this work with a professional license. If any page claims otherwise, it is wrong: let us know.

entries.original: VoltDrop is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or approved by NFPA. No calculator is “NEC certified,” including this one. That isn't a thing.
entries.translation: VoltDrop no está afiliado, respaldado ni aprobado por NFPA. Ninguna calculadora tiene una “certificación NEC”, incluida esta. Esa certificación no existe.
entries.backTranslation: VoltDrop is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or approved by NFPA. No calculator has an “NEC certification,” including this one. That certification does not exist.

entries.original: The Canadian conduit-fill page shows what happens when a gap closes. It used to carry a warning because its Canadian conductor and conduit tables had not passed the multi-source check. CSA C22.1:24 Tables 6A/6K and 9A–9H have now passed, so the warning is gone and the page computes from sealed Canadian data. We would rather leave a visible gap than fill it early, and remove the warning only when the evidence changes.
entries.translation: La página canadiense de llenado de conduit muestra qué ocurre cuando se cierra una brecha. Antes llevaba una advertencia porque sus tablas canadienses de conductores y tubos conduit no habían pasado la comprobación con múltiples fuentes. CSA C22.1:24 Tables 6A/6K y 9A–9H ya la han pasado, así que la advertencia desapareció y la página calcula con datos canadienses sellados. Preferimos dejar una brecha visible antes que llenarla demasiado pronto, y quitar la advertencia solo cuando cambian las pruebas.
entries.backTranslation: The Canadian conduit fill page shows what happens when a gap is closed. It previously carried a warning because its Canadian conductor and conduit tables had not passed the multiple-source check. CSA C22.1:24 Tables 6A/6K and 9A–9H have now passed it, so the warning disappeared and the page calculates with sealed Canadian data. We prefer to leave a gap visible rather than fill it too soon, and remove the warning only when the evidence changes.

entries.original: Results are planning estimates using simplified, normal-conditions methods. Real installations have conditions our inputs don't ask about.
entries.translation: Los resultados son estimaciones de planificación que usan métodos simplificados para condiciones normales. Las instalaciones reales tienen condiciones que nuestras entradas no preguntan.
entries.backTranslation: The results are planning estimates that use simplified methods for normal conditions. Actual installations have conditions that our inputs do not ask about.

entries.original: Terms that must never be translated — code names, wire types, and units — are checked for survival in every language.
entries.translation: En todos los idiomas comprobamos que sobrevivan los términos que nunca deben traducirse: nombres de códigos, tipos de conductor y unidades.
entries.backTranslation: In every language, we check that terms which must never be translated remain intact: code names, conductor types, and units.

entries.original: The easiest thing in the world would be to fill every gap with a plausible-looking number and say nothing about it. When a country-specific table has not passed, we label the boundary or refuse the answer in the place you would be about to rely on it.
entries.translation: Lo más fácil del mundo sería llenar cada vacío con un número que pareciera plausible y no decir nada al respecto. Cuando una tabla específica de un país no ha pasado la comprobación, señalamos ese límite o rechazamos la respuesta justo donde usted estaría a punto de basarse en ella.
entries.backTranslation: The easiest thing in the world would be to fill every gap with a number that seemed plausible and say nothing about it. When a country-specific table has not passed the check, we indicate that limit or refuse the answer right where you would be about to rely on it.

entries.original: The English pages are compared byte-for-byte against the previous build, so nothing changes by accident.
entries.translation: Las páginas en inglés se comparan byte por byte con la generación anterior para que nada cambie por accidente.
entries.backTranslation: The English pages are compared byte for byte with the previous generation so that nothing changes accidentally.

entries.original: This is not theatre. One draft ampacity value in an early build disagreed between sources. The check caught it, the value was corrected before it shipped, and that is the whole reason the step exists.
entries.translation: Esto no es teatro. En una versión inicial, un valor provisional de ampacidad no coincidía entre las fuentes. La comprobación lo detectó, el valor se corrigió antes de publicarse y esa es la razón de que exista este paso.
entries.backTranslation: This is not theater. In an early version, a provisional ampacity value did not match across sources. The check caught it, the value was corrected before publication, and that is why this step exists.

entries.original: VoltDrop doesn't type numbers in from memory. Every electrical table built into these calculators is compared against at least two independently produced reproductions of the published table before it goes live, row by row. They all have to agree, on every cell, or it doesn't ship.
entries.translation: VoltDrop no escribe números de memoria. Antes de publicarse, cada tabla eléctrica incluida en estas calculadoras se compara, celda por celda, con al menos dos reproducciones de la tabla publicada elaboradas de manera independiente. Todas deben coincidir en cada celda o no se publica.
entries.backTranslation: VoltDrop does not enter numbers from memory. Before publication, every electrical table included in these calculators is compared, cell by cell, with at least two independently produced reproductions of the published table. They must all match in every cell or it is not published.

entries.original: VoltDrop ships in six editions across four languages. A safety warning that quietly loses its meaning in translation is a real hazard, so we screen for it: the translated text is turned back into English on its own, without the original in view, and the result is compared against what we actually meant.
entries.translation: VoltDrop se publica en seis ediciones y cuatro idiomas. Una advertencia de seguridad que pierde su significado en la traducción es un peligro real. Por eso la filtramos: el texto traducido se convierte de nuevo al inglés por sí solo, sin tener a la vista el original, y el resultado se compara con lo que realmente queríamos decir.
entries.backTranslation: VoltDrop is published in six editions and four languages. A safety warning that loses its meaning in translation is a real danger. That is why we screen for it: the translated text is converted back into English independently, without the original in view, and the result is compared with what we actually meant.

entries.original: We also watch the screen itself. An early version of this check reported almost everything as perfect because the English original had leaked into the process and was simply being echoed back. That run was thrown out. The check was rebuilt so the source is sealed out of it. Runs that show signs of leakage are rejected rather than trusted.
entries.translation: También vigilamos el propio proceso. Una primera versión de esta comprobación indicó que casi todo era perfecto porque el original en inglés se había filtrado al proceso y simplemente se repetía. Esa ejecución se descartó. La comprobación se reconstruyó para mantener la fuente fuera de ella. Las ejecuciones con señales de filtración se rechazan en vez de darse por buenas.
entries.backTranslation: We also monitor the process itself. An early version of this check reported that almost everything was perfect because the English original had leaked into the process and was simply repeated. That run was discarded. The check was rebuilt to keep the source out of it. Runs showing signs of leakage are rejected rather than accepted.

entries.original: We've tested that the seal fires on a one-digit edit.
entries.translation: Comprobamos que el sello se active al editar un solo dígito.
entries.backTranslation: We check that the seal is triggered when a single digit is edited.

entries.original: You're about to size a conductor from a number on a screen. Here's exactly where that number came from, and what we do to stop it being wrong.
entries.translation: Está a punto de dimensionar un conductor a partir de un número en una pantalla. Aquí explicamos exactamente de dónde salió y qué hacemos para evitar que sea incorrecto.
entries.backTranslation: You are about to size a conductor based on a number on a screen. Here we explain exactly where it came from and what we do to prevent it from being incorrect.

entries.original: Ohm's law describes a circuit; it does not size a conductor. Wire size depends on ampacity (heat) and voltage drop (distance), neither of which is in this equation. For those, use
entries.translation: La ley de Ohm describe un circuito; no dimensiona un conductor. El calibre depende de la ampacidad (calor) y de la caída de tensión (distancia), y ninguna está en esta ecuación. Para eso, use
entries.backTranslation: Ohm’s law describes a circuit; it does not size a conductor. The gauge depends on ampacity (heat) and voltage drop (distance), and neither is in this equation. For that, use

entries.original: Ask for ohms on a three-phase circuit and this calculator declines, on purpose. A single resistance figure depends on whether the load is wye or delta connected, and that changes the answer. This form does not ask, and many people wiring a motor do not know off the top of their head. Printing a number anyway would be a guess dressed up as a result.
entries.translation: Si pide ohmios para un circuito trifásico, esta calculadora se niega a propósito. Un único valor de resistencia depende de si la carga está conectada en estrella o en triángulo, y eso cambia la respuesta. Este formulario no lo pregunta, y muchas personas que cablean un motor no lo saben de memoria. Mostrar un número de todos modos sería una suposición disfrazada de resultado.
entries.backTranslation: If you request ohms for a three-phase circuit, this calculator deliberately refuses. A single resistance value depends on whether the load is connected in star or delta, and that changes the answer. This form does not ask, and many people wiring a motor do not know it from memory. Showing a number anyway would be a guess disguised as a result.

entries.original: Free NEC ampacity derating calculator for ambient temperature, current-carrying conductors, termination limits, 240.4(D), and separate continuous-load sizing.
entries.translation: Calculadora gratuita de reducción de ampacidad NEC para temperatura ambiente, conductores portadores de corriente, límites de terminación, 240.4(D) y dimensionamiento separado de cargas continuas.
entries.backTranslation: Free NEC ampacity derating calculator for ambient temperature, current-carrying conductors, termination limits, 240.4(D), and separate sizing of continuous loads.

entries.original: VoltDrop Ampacity Derating Check
entries.translation: Verificación de reducción de ampacidad VoltDrop
entries.backTranslation: VoltDrop ampacity derating check

entries.original: Ampacity Derating Calculator — NEC 310.15 | VoltDrop
entries.translation: Calculadora de reducción de ampacidad — NEC 310.15 | VoltDrop
entries.backTranslation: Ampacity Derating Calculator — NEC 310.15 | VoltDrop

entries.original: Free NEC 314.16 box fill calculator: count wires, devices, grounds and clamps, get a clear fits/too-full verdict with the cubic-inch math shown. No signup.
entries.translation: Calculadora gratuita de llenado de caja según NEC 314.16: cuente conductores, dispositivos, tierras y abrazaderas para obtener una evaluación clara con el cálculo de volumen.
entries.backTranslation: Free box-fill calculator according to NEC 314.16: count conductors, devices, grounds, and clamps to obtain a clear assessment with the volume calculation.

entries.original: Free conduit fill calculator: THHN wire count and size in, smallest legal EMT or PVC Schedule 40 conduit out — using the official NEC Chapter 9 tables and 53/31/40% fill limits.

entries.backTranslation: Ten verified differences between the NEC and the Canadian Electrical Code: ampacity, adjustment, continuous loads, voltage drop, conduit fill, colours, and the high leg.

entries.original: Free max wire run calculator: enter wire size, amps, and voltage to get the longest one-way distance that stays under 3% or 5% voltage drop. Copper and aluminum, DC and AC, no signup.

entries.backTranslation: Free maximum-length calculator: enter conductor gauge, amperes, and voltage to obtain the greatest one-way distance that keeps the drop below 3% or 5%.

entries.original: How far can your wire run before voltage drop becomes a problem? Get the maximum one-way distance for any wire size and load.
entries.translation: ¿Qué distancia puede recorrer el conductor antes de que la caída de tensión sea un problema? Obtenga la distancia máxima en un solo sentido para cualquier calibre y carga.
entries.backTranslation: How far can the conductor run before voltage drop becomes a problem? Get the maximum one-way distance for any gauge and load.

entries.original: Free NEC conductor size calculator for ampacity and voltage drop. See the heat-driven minimum, distance-driven minimum, governing AWG, and separate margins.
entries.translation: Calculadora gratuita NEC de calibre del conductor por ampacidad y caída de tensión. Muestra el mínimo por calor, el mínimo por distancia, el AWG gobernante y márgenes separados.
entries.backTranslation: Free NEC conductor size calculator for ampacity and voltage drop. Shows the minimum for heat, the minimum for distance, the governing AWG, and separate margins.

entries.original: Ohms modes are unavailable for three-phase. The answer changes depending on whether the load is wye or delta connected, and this calculator does not ask for that.
entries.translation: Los modos con ohmios no están disponibles para sistemas trifásicos. La respuesta cambia según la carga esté conectada en estrella o en triángulo, y esta calculadora no solicita ese dato.
entries.backTranslation: Ohms modes are not available for three-phase systems. The answer changes depending on whether the load is connected in star or delta, and this calculator does not ask for that information.

entries.original: Watts (kW) measure real usable power, while kVA measures the apparent power the wiring must carry. For heaters and simple loads they are equal; for motors and electronics kVA can be higher, and the ratio between them is the power factor.
entries.translation: Los vatios (kW) miden la potencia real utilizable, mientras que kVA mide la potencia aparente que el cableado debe transportar. En calefactores y cargas simples son iguales; en motores y equipos electrónicos, kVA puede ser mayor. La relación entre ambas es el factor de potencia.
entries.backTranslation: Watts (kW) measure real usable power, while kVA measures the apparent power that the wiring must carry. For heaters and simple loads they are equal; for motors and electronic equipment, kVA may be higher. The relationship between them is the power factor.

entries.backTranslation: The calculators run entirely in your browser: the numbers you enter never leave your device. We do not require an account, we do not sell data, and the only personal information we retain is what you give us if you choose to sign in and leave a comment.

entries.original: Canadian counting (Rule 12-3034): each insulated wire entering the box counts once at its own size. Bare bond wires are NOT counted. Each device counts twice. Every PAIR of insulated wire connectors (marrettes) counts once. Devices and marrette pairs use the largest listed conductor. Cable clamps get NO allowance in Canada. Pigtails that live entirely inside the box are free.
entries.translation: Conteo canadiense (Rule 12-3034): cada conductor aislado que entra en la caja cuenta una vez según su propio calibre. Los conductores de continuidad de masa desnudos NO cuentan. Cada dispositivo cuenta dos veces. Cada PAR de conectores aislados (marrettes) cuenta una vez. Los dispositivos y pares de marrettes usan el conductor más grande indicado. Las abrazaderas NO reciben volumen en Canadá. Las colas de conexión internas no cuentan.
entries.backTranslation: Canadian counting (Rule 12-3034): each insulated conductor entering the box counts once at its own size. Bare bonding conductors do NOT count. Each device counts twice. Each PAIR of insulated connectors (marrettes) counts once. Devices and marrette pairs use the largest listed conductor. Clamps receive NO volume in Canada. Internal pigtails do not count.

entries.original: Canadian fine print: bare bond wires and cable clamps get no allowance (unlike the US); marrettes count one allowance per pair, sized by the largest wire in them (we use your selected size — pick the largest present to be safe); devices deeper than 2.54 cm need an extra deduction of 32 mL per cm of depth, which this simple check doesn't include.
entries.translation: Detalle canadiense: los conductores de continuidad de masa desnudos y las abrazaderas no reciben volumen; cada par de marrettes recibe un volumen según el conductor más grande conectado (usamos el calibre que seleccionó; para mayor seguridad, seleccione el conductor de mayor tamaño presente). Los dispositivos con más de 2.54 cm de profundidad necesitan una deducción adicional de 32 mL por cm de profundidad, que esta verificación sencilla no incluye.
entries.backTranslation: Canadian detail: bare bonding conductors and clamps receive no volume; each pair of marrettes receives one volume based on the largest conductor connected (we use the gauge you selected; for greater safety, select the largest conductor size present). Devices more than 2.54 cm deep need an additional deduction of 32 mL per cm of depth, which this simple check does not include.

entries.original: Cram too many wires into a box and connections get stressed, insulation gets nicked, and heat builds up — a classic cause of failed inspections and flickering circuits. The U.S. electrical code (NEC 314.16) assigns every wire a space allowance based on its size, and the box must have at least that much room.
entries.translation: Una caja sobrecargada fuerza las conexiones, daña el aislamiento y acumula calor. Es una causa habitual de inspecciones fallidas y circuitos intermitentes. NEC 314.16 asigna un volumen a cada calibre del conductor, y la caja debe ofrecer al menos ese espacio.
entries.backTranslation: An overloaded box strains connections, damages insulation, and accumulates heat. It is a common cause of failed inspections and intermittent circuits. NEC 314.16 assigns a volume to each conductor gauge, and the box must provide at least that space.

entries.original: Cram too many wires into a box and connections get stressed, insulation gets nicked, and heat builds up — a classic cause of failed inspections. The Canadian Electrical Code (Rule 12-3034 with Table 22) assigns every insulated wire a space allowance in millilitres, and the box must have at least that much room.
entries.translation: Una caja sobrecargada fuerza las conexiones, daña el aislamiento y acumula calor. Es una causa habitual de inspecciones fallidas. Canadian Electrical Code (Rule 12-3034 con Table 22) asigna a cada conductor aislado un volumen en mililitros, y la caja debe ofrecer al menos ese espacio.
entries.backTranslation: An overloaded box strains connections, damages insulation, and accumulates heat. It is a common cause of failed inspections. Canadian Electrical Code (Rule 12-3034 with Table 22) assigns each insulated conductor a volume in millilitres, and the box must provide at least that space.
