entries.original: Each hot or neutral entering the box counts at its own size — including wires that pass straight through unbroken. Each device (switch/outlet) counts twice at the allowance of its largest connected conductor. All ground wires together count once at the largest ground size. Built-in cable clamps count once at the largest conductor in the box. Pigtails that live entirely inside the box are free.
entries.translation: Cada conductor de fase o neutro que entra en la caja cuenta según su propio calibre, incluidos los que la atraviesan sin cortarse. Cada dispositivo cuenta dos veces según el volumen de su conductor conectado más grande. Todos los conductores de puesta a tierra juntos cuentan una vez según el mayor. Las abrazaderas internas cuentan una vez según el conductor más grande de la caja. Las colas de conexión internas no cuentan.
entries.backTranslation: Each hot or neutral conductor entering the box counts at its own size, including conductors that pass through unbroken. Each device counts twice using the volume of its largest connected conductor. All grounds together count once using the largest ground. Internal clamps count once using the largest conductor in the box. Internal pigtails do not count.

entries.original: Fine print: pigtails that stay entirely inside the box don't count, but a wire passing through unbroken DOES count once — include it above. If more than four ground wires enter the box, each one beyond four adds a ¼ count (2020 code rule) — add roughly one extra wire to be safe. Mixed wire sizes deserve the full by-size calculation (coming soon); until then, picking your largest size is the safe way to use this tool.
entries.translation: Detalle: las colas de conexión que permanecen dentro de la caja no cuentan, pero un conductor que la atraviesa sin cortarse SÍ cuenta una vez. Si entran más de cuatro conductores de puesta a tierra, cada uno después del cuarto suma ¼ según las reglas de 2020. Si hay varios calibres, use el más grande para mantener un margen seguro.
entries.backTranslation: Detail: pigtails that remain inside the box do not count, but a conductor that passes through it uncut DOES count once. If more than four grounding conductors enter, each one after the fourth adds ¼ under the 2020 rules. If there are multiple gauges, use the largest to maintain a safe margin.

entries.original: Over the limit. Use a deeper box, a box extension, or fewer conductors — overfilled boxes are a common inspection failure and a heat risk.

entries.backTranslation: Exceeds the limit. Use a deeper box, an extension, or fewer conductors. Overloaded boxes often fail inspection and present a heat risk.

entries.backTranslation: {count} × {size}: {count} × {wireArea} = {rowArea} sq in

entries.original:
Each row uses the conductor cross-section from NEC Chapter 9, Table 5.

{breakdown} TOTAL = {needed} sq in {conduitSize} {conduit} inside area = {conduitArea} sq in (NEC Chapter 9, Table 4) Allowed for {count} conductors: {conduitArea} × {percent}% = {allowed} sq in {needed} ≤ {allowed} → fits at {actualPercent}% fill
entries.translation:
Cada fila usa la sección transversal del conductor de NEC Chapter 9, Table 5.

{breakdown} TOTAL = {needed} sq in Área interior de {conduitSize} {conduit} = {conduitArea} sq in (NEC Chapter 9, Table 4) Permitido para {count} conductores: {conduitArea} × {percent}% = {allowed} sq in {needed} ≤ {allowed} → llenado real de {actualPercent}%
entries.backTranslation: Each row uses the conductor cross-sectional area from NEC Chapter 9, Table 5. TOTAL = {needed} sq in. The inside area of {conduitSize} {conduit} is {conduitArea} sq in from NEC Chapter 9, Table 4. Allowed for {count} conductors: {conduitArea} × {percent}% = {allowed} sq in. {needed} ≤ {allowed}, giving actual fill of {actualPercent}%.

entries.translation: menor {conduit} para {count} conductores
entries.backTranslation: smallest {conduit} for {count} conductors

entries.translation: El área combinada de los conductores es {area} sq in, lo que supera el límite de llenado de {percent}% incluso en un {conduit} de 4".
entries.backTranslation: The combined conductor area is {area} sq in, which exceeds the {percent}% fill limit even in a 4-inch {conduit}.

Ampacity-driven minimum: {size}

Base ampacity ({insulation}°C insulation): {base} A → Ambient correction ({ambient}°C; row {ambientRow}): × {ambientFactor} = {ambientAdjusted} A → {conductors} current-carrying conductors: × {adjustmentFactor} = {adjusted} A → Termination limit ({termination}°C): {terminationLimit} A → Small-conductor cap: {smallCap} = Final permitted ampacity: {permitted} A

{continuousRule}
entries.translation:
Mínimo por ampacidad: {size}

Ampacidad base (aislamiento de {insulation}°C): {base} A → Corrección ambiental ({ambient}°C; fila {ambientRow}): × {ambientFactor} = {ambientAdjusted} A → {conductors} conductores portadores de corriente: × {adjustmentFactor} = {adjusted} A → Límite de terminales ({termination}°C): {terminationLimit} A → Límite para conductores pequeños: {smallCap} = Ampacidad final permitida: {permitted} A

Límite vinculante: {binding}.

{continuousRule}
entries.backTranslation:
Minimum by ampacity: {size}

Base ampacity ({insulation}°C insulation): {base} A → Ambient correction ({ambient}°C; row {ambientRow}): × {ambientFactor} = {ambientAdjusted} A → {conductors} current-carrying conductors: × {adjustmentFactor} = {adjusted} A → Terminal limit ({termination}°C): {terminationLimit} A → Small-conductor limit: {smallCap} = Final permitted ampacity: {permitted} A

Binding limit: {binding}.

{continuousRule}

entries.original: Different table ranges: Voltage drop alone allows {dropSize}, but the ampacity table starts at {floorSize} for {material}. {dropSize} is not treated as passing ampacity.
entries.translation: Rangos de tabla distintos: La caída de tensión por sí sola permite {dropSize}, pero la tabla de ampacidad comienza en {floorSize} para {material}. {dropSize} no se trata como aprobado por ampacidad.
entries.backTranslation: Different table ranges: Voltage drop alone permits {dropSize}, but the ampacity table starts at {floorSize} for {material}. {dropSize} is not treated as approved by ampacity.

entries.original: Smallest-size proof: {size} passes and is the smallest size this ampacity table supports for {material}. The engine makes no claim about smaller sizes.
entries.translation: Prueba del calibre mínimo: {size} aprueba y es el calibre más pequeño que esta tabla de ampacidad admite para {material}. El motor no afirma nada sobre calibres menores.
entries.backTranslation: Minimum-size proof: {size} passes and is the smallest size this ampacity table supports for {material}. The engine makes no claim about smaller sizes.

entries.original: Distance did not raise the conductor — zero listed sizes. Ampacity raised it from the distance-only {dropSize} to {finalSize}.
entries.translation: La distancia no aumentó el conductor: cero calibres listados. La ampacidad lo aumentó desde {dropSize}, permitido solo por distancia, hasta {finalSize}.
entries.backTranslation: Distance did not increase the conductor: zero listed sizes. Ampacity increased it from {dropSize}, permitted by distance alone, to {finalSize}.

entries.original: Smallest-size proof: {size} passes. The next smaller supported size, {smallerSize}, fails the entered {load} A under the applied load rule.
entries.translation: Prueba del calibre mínimo: {size} aprueba. El siguiente calibre menor admitido, {smallerSize}, no aprueba la carga ingresada de {load} A bajo la regla de carga aplicada.
entries.backTranslation: Minimum-size proof: {size} passes. The next smaller supported size, {smallerSize}, does not pass the entered load of {load} A under the applied load rule.

entries.original: Distance did not raise the conductor beyond ampacity — zero listed sizes. Both constraints select {finalSize}; this is a normal tie.
entries.translation: La distancia no aumentó el conductor más allá de la ampacidad: cero calibres listados. Ambas restricciones seleccionan {finalSize}; es un empate normal.
entries.backTranslation: Distance did not increase the conductor beyond ampacity: zero listed sizes. Both constraints select {finalSize}; this is a normal tie.

entries.original:
Continuous-load step

Entered load: {load} A × {factor}% = {after} A required ampacity {after} A ≤ {permitted} A permitted ampacity → passes

The switch treats the entire entered load as continuous; it does not model a mixed load.
entries.translation:
Paso de carga continua

Carga ingresada: {load} A × {factor}% = {after} A de ampacidad requerida {after} A ≤ {permitted} A de ampacidad permitida → aprueba

El interruptor trata toda la carga ingresada como continua; no modela una carga mixta.
entries.backTranslation:
Continuous-load step

Entered load: {load} A × {factor}% = {after} A required ampacity {after} A ≤ {permitted} A permitted ampacity → pass

The switch treats the entire entered load as continuous; it does not model a mixed load.

entries.original: NEC continuous load: 125% of the load. Before: {load} A entered load. After: {load} A × {factor}% = {after} A required ampacity. The switch treats the entire entered load as continuous; it does not model a mixed load.
entries.translation: Carga continua NEC: 125% de la carga. Antes: carga ingresada de {load} A. Después: {load} A × {factor}% = {after} A de ampacidad requerida. El interruptor trata toda la carga ingresada como continua; no modela una carga mixta.
entries.backTranslation: NEC continuous load: 125% of the load. Before: entered load of {load} A. After: {load} A × {factor}% = {after} A required ampacity. The switch treats the entire entered load as continuous; it does not model a mixed load.

entries.original: At exactly this distance you hit {percent}% drop. Stay shorter for margin. And remember: the wire must also be rated for {amps} A (ampacity) regardless of distance.
entries.translation: A esta distancia exacta se alcanza una caída de {percent}%. Mantenga el recorrido más corto para conservar margen. Recuerde también que el conductor debe tener capacidad nominal para {amps} A (ampacidad), sin importar la distancia.
entries.backTranslation: At this exact distance the drop reaches {percent}%. Use a shorter run to keep margin. The conductor must also be rated for {amps} A (ampacity), regardless of distance.

entries.original:
We rearranged the formula to solve for distance, with your limit of {percent}% ({maxDrop} V):

Max one-way feet = {maxDrop} V × {cm} cmil ÷ ({mult} × {factor} × {amps} A) = {feet} ft
entries.translation:
Reordenamos la fórmula para calcular la distancia, con su límite de {percent}% ({maxDrop} V):

Máximo de pies en un solo sentido = {maxDrop} V × {cm} cmil ÷ ({mult} × {factor} × {amps} A) = {feet} ft
entries.backTranslation:
We rearrange the formula to calculate distance using your {percent}% limit ({maxDrop} V):

Maximum one-way feet = {maxDrop} V × {cm} cmil ÷ ({mult} × {factor} × {amps} A) = {feet} ft

entries.original: no listed size keeps you under {percent}%
entries.translation: ningún calibre indicado mantiene la caída por debajo de {percent}%
entries.backTranslation: no listed gauge keeps the drop below {percent}%

entries.original: Even {size} {material} drops more than {percent}% over {feet} one-way feet at {amps} A.
entries.translation: Incluso un conductor de {material} {size} tiene una caída superior a {percent}% en {feet} pies de distancia en un solo sentido con {amps} A.
entries.backTranslation: Even a {size} {material} conductor drops more than {percent}% over {feet} one-way feet at {amps} A.

entries.original: The published ambient table marks {ambient}°C with {insulation}°C insulation as “—” or outside the supported rows. No correction factor is substituted and no conductor size is returned.
entries.translation: La tabla de temperatura ambiente publicada marca {ambient}°C con aislamiento de {insulation}°C como “—” o fuera de las filas admitidas. No se sustituye ningún factor de corrección ni se devuelve ningún calibre de conductor.
entries.backTranslation: The published ambient-temperature table marks {ambient}°C with {insulation}°C insulation as “—” or outside the supported rows. No correction factor is substituted and no conductor size is returned.

entries.original: Refusal: {constraint} did not produce a passing listed size. The largest listed conductor is not returned as a recommendation.
entries.translation: Rechazo: {constraint} no produjo un calibre listado aprobado. El conductor listado más grande no se devuelve como recomendación.
entries.backTranslation: Rejection: {constraint} did not produce an approved listed size. The largest listed conductor is not returned as a recommendation.

entries.original: No listed conductor passes both checks. The voltage-drop search found {dropStatus}; the ampacity search found {ampacityStatus}. Change the design or have a qualified electrician evaluate conductors or arrangements outside this tool.
entries.translation: Ningún conductor listado aprueba ambas verificaciones. La búsqueda por caída de tensión encontró {dropStatus}; la búsqueda por ampacidad encontró {ampacityStatus}. Cambie el diseño o pida a un electricista calificado que evalúe conductores o disposiciones fuera de esta herramienta.
entries.backTranslation: No listed conductor passes both checks. The voltage-drop search found {dropStatus}; the ampacity search found {ampacityStatus}. Change the design or ask a qualified electrician to evaluate conductors or arrangements outside this tool.

entries.original:
We tested each size, smallest first, until one kept the drop under your {percent}% limit ({maxDrop} V):

{size} ({cm} cmil): {mult} × {factor} × {amps} A × {feet} ft ÷ {cm} = {dropped} V = {actualPercent}% ✓ under your limit
entries.translation:
Probamos cada calibre, empezando por el menor, hasta encontrar uno que mantuviera la caída por debajo de su límite de {percent}% ({maxDrop} V):

{size} ({cm} cmil): {mult} × {factor} × {amps} A × {feet} ft ÷ {cm} = {dropped} V = {actualPercent}% ✓ por debajo de su límite
entries.backTranslation:
Starting with the smallest, each gauge was tested until one stayed below your {percent}% limit ({maxDrop} V):

{size} ({cm} cmil): {mult} × {factor} × {amps} A × {feet} ft ÷ {cm} = {dropped} V = {actualPercent}% ✓ below your limit

entries.original: smallest {material} wire that stays under {percent}%
entries.translation: menor conductor de {material} que mantiene la caída por debajo de {percent}%
entries.backTranslation: smallest {material} conductor that remains below {percent}%

entries.original: This sizes wire for voltage drop. The conductor also has to be rated to carry the current without overheating, which is a different calculation with different tables. Outdoors, in conduit, and in sunlight, derating matters. Check it:
entries.translation: Esto dimensiona el conductor por caída de tensión. El conductor también debe estar autorizado para transportar la corriente sin sobrecalentarse, lo cual es otro cálculo con tablas distintas. A la intemperie, dentro de un tubo conduit y bajo el sol, los ajustes importan. Compruébelo:
entries.backTranslation: This sizes the conductor by voltage drop. The conductor must also be permitted to carry the current without overheating, which is another calculation using different tables. Outdoors, inside a conduit, and in the sun, adjustments matter. Check it:

entries.original: The drop targets this tool uses are starting points from common solar practice, not code requirements. There is no code rule that says 2%. Your equipment manufacturer may specify something tighter, and their number wins. The tool shows the target it used so you can change it knowingly rather than inherit it silently.
entries.translation: Los objetivos de caída que usa esta herramienta son puntos de partida de la práctica solar habitual, no requisitos normativos. No existe una regla normativa que diga 2%. El fabricante del equipo puede indicar un valor más estricto, y ese valor prevalece. La herramienta muestra el objetivo utilizado para que pueda cambiarlo conscientemente en vez de heredarlo sin saberlo.
entries.backTranslation: The voltage-drop targets used by this tool are starting points from common solar practice, not code requirements. There is no code rule that says 2%. The equipment manufacturer may specify a stricter value, and that value takes precedence. The tool shows the target used so that you can change it knowingly instead of inheriting it without realizing it.

entries.original: Always verify calculations independently, follow your local electrical code and permit requirements, and hire a licensed professional where required by law or common sense.
entries.translation: Verifique siempre los cálculos de forma independiente, cumpla el código eléctrico y los permisos locales, y contrate a un profesional autorizado cuando la ley o la prudencia lo exijan.
entries.backTranslation: Always verify calculations independently, comply with local electrical code and permits, and hire a licensed professional when the law or prudence requires it.

entries.original: Don't attack, overload, scrape at abusive rates, reverse-engineer for the purpose of harming, or otherwise interfere with the Service, and don't use it in violation of any law.
entries.translation: No ataque, sobrecargue ni extraiga contenido a un ritmo abusivo; no aplique ingeniería inversa con el fin de causar daños ni interfiera de otra forma con el Servicio. Tampoco lo use para infringir la ley.
entries.backTranslation: Do not attack, overload, or extract content at an abusive rate; do not reverse engineer for the purpose of causing harm or otherwise interfere with the Service. Also do not use it to break the law.

entries.original: Electrical work can injure or kill, and mistakes can cause fires.
entries.translation: El trabajo eléctrico puede causar lesiones o la muerte, y los errores pueden provocar incendios.
entries.backTranslation: Electrical work can cause injury or death, and mistakes can cause fires.

entries.original: For Canadian code-based calculations, VoltDrop implements CSA C22.1:24 — Canadian Electrical Code, Part I, 26th edition (2024): Tables 2, 4, 5A, 5C, and 22, and Rules 4-004, 4-006, 8-102, 8-104, 12-3034, and 14-104.
entries.translation: Para los cálculos basados en códigos canadienses, VoltDrop implementa CSA C22.1:24 — Canadian Electrical Code, Part I, 26th edition (2024): Tables 2, 4, 5A, 5C y 22, y Rules 4-004, 4-006, 8-102, 8-104, 12-3034 y 14-104.
entries.backTranslation: For calculations based on Canadian codes, VoltDrop implements CSA C22.1:24 — Canadian Electrical Code, Part I, 26th edition (2024): Tables 2, 4, 5A, 5C, and 22, and Rules 4-004, 4-006, 8-102, 8-104, 12-3034, and 14-104.

entries.original: For U.S. code-based calculations, VoltDrop implements the 2023 edition of NFPA 70 — National Electrical Code (NEC): Table 310.16, Tables 310.15(B)(1) and 310.15(C)(1), 240.4(D), and 110.14(C). Its conduit-fill and box-fill tools also use NEC Chapter 9 Tables 4 and 5 and NEC 314.16, including Tables 314.16(A) and 314.16(B).
entries.translation: Para los cálculos basados en códigos de EE. UU., VoltDrop implementa la edición de 2023 de NFPA 70 — National Electrical Code (NEC): Table 310.16, Tables 310.15(B)(1) y 310.15(C)(1), 240.4(D) y 110.14(C). Sus herramientas de llenado de conduit y de cajas también usan NEC Chapter 9 Tables 4 y 5 y NEC 314.16, incluidos Tables 314.16(A) y 314.16(B).
entries.backTranslation: For calculations based on U.S. codes, VoltDrop implements the 2023 edition of NFPA 70 — National Electrical Code (NEC): Table 310.16, Tables 310.15(B)(1) and 310.15(C)(1), 240.4(D), and 110.14(C). Its conduit-fill and box-fill tools also use NEC Chapter 9 Tables 4 and 5 and NEC 314.16, including Tables 314.16(A) and 314.16(B).

entries.original: . If you don't agree, please don't use the Service.
entries.translation: . Si no está de acuerdo, no use el Servicio.
entries.backTranslation: . If you do not agree, do not use the Service.

entries.original: Results are simplified estimates for normal conditions. They do not account for every real-world factor (temperature, bundling, derating, continuous loads, local code amendments, equipment listings, and more). The Service is not a substitute for a licensed electrician or professional engineer, and using it does not create any professional relationship.
entries.translation: Los resultados son estimaciones simplificadas para condiciones normales. No consideran todos los factores reales (temperatura, agrupamiento, reducción de ampacidad, cargas continuas, cambios locales al código, certificaciones de equipos y otros). El Servicio no sustituye a un electricista autorizado ni a un ingeniero profesional, y su uso no crea una relación profesional.
entries.backTranslation: The results are simplified estimates for normal conditions. They do not account for all real-world factors (temperature, grouping, ampacity derating, continuous loads, local code changes, equipment certifications, and others). The Service is not a substitute for a licensed electrician or professional engineer, and its use does not create a professional relationship.

entries.original: States, provinces, and municipalities adopt codes on different schedules and may add local amendments. A result that is correct under the edition VoltDrop implements can be wrong where an earlier edition or local amendment applies. You must confirm the edition adopted by your own authority.
entries.translation: Los estados, las provincias y los municipios adoptan los códigos en fechas distintas y pueden añadir modificaciones locales. Un resultado correcto conforme a la edición que implementa VoltDrop puede ser incorrecto donde se aplique una edición anterior o una modificación local. Debe confirmar la edición adoptada por su propia autoridad competente.
entries.backTranslation: States, provinces, and municipalities adopt codes on different dates and may add local amendments. A result that is correct under the edition implemented by VoltDrop may be incorrect where an earlier edition or a local amendment is applied. You must confirm the edition adopted by your own competent authority.

entries.backTranslation: To the fullest extent permitted by law, VoltDrop and its operator are not liable for damages arising from use of or inability to use the Service, including property damage, personal injury, lost profits, or the cost of redoing electrical work, whether under warranty, contract, tort, or another theory. If liability cannot be fully excluded, our total liability is limited to $50 (USD). Some jurisdictions do not allow certain exclusions, so some parts may not apply to you.

entries.original: Translations are provided for convenience. If a translated version is inconsistent with the English version, the English version governs.
entries.translation: Las traducciones se proporcionan por comodidad. Si una versión traducida no coincide con la versión en inglés, prevalece la versión en inglés.
entries.backTranslation: Translations are provided for convenience. If a translated version does not match the English version, the English version prevails.

entries.original: VoltDrop sometimes uses a simplified or conservative method. For example, CEC Rule 4-006 limits the termination-temperature requirement to the first 1.2 m of conductor and permits a compliant transition beyond it. VoltDrop does not model that split; it applies the lower of the conductor and termination temperature ratings to the entire run. This is conservative, but it is not the full Code procedure.
entries.translation: VoltDrop a veces emplea un método simplificado o conservador. Por ejemplo, CEC Rule 4-006 limita el requisito de temperatura de las terminaciones a los primeros 1.2 m del conductor y permite una transición conforme al código después de ese tramo. VoltDrop no modela esa división; aplica la menor de las temperaturas nominales del conductor y de la terminación a todo el recorrido. Este método es conservador, pero no es el procedimiento completo del código.
entries.backTranslation: VoltDrop sometimes uses a simplified or conservative method. For example, CEC Rule 4-006 limits the termination-temperature requirement to the first 1.2 m of the conductor and permits a code-compliant transition after that section. VoltDrop does not model that division; it applies the lower of the conductor and termination temperature ratings to the entire run. This method is conservative, but it is not the code’s full procedure.

entries.original: Where a Code does not expressly answer an implementation detail, VoltDrop may make a conservative choice that your local inspector or authority may not share. For example, CEC Rule 4-004 does not expressly address installed spare power or lighting conductors; VoltDrop counts them toward Table 5C.
entries.translation: Cuando un código no resuelve expresamente un detalle de implementación, VoltDrop puede tomar una decisión conservadora que su inspector o autoridad local quizá no comparta. Por ejemplo, CEC Rule 4-004 no aborda expresamente los conductores de reserva instalados para potencia o iluminación; VoltDrop los cuenta para Table 5C.
entries.backTranslation: When a code does not expressly resolve an implementation detail, VoltDrop may make a conservative decision that your local inspector or authority may not share. For example, CEC Rule 4-004 does not expressly address installed spare conductors for power or lighting; VoltDrop counts them for Table 5C.

Usted conserva la propiedad de lo que escribe, pero nos concede una licencia mundial y libre de regalías para mostrarlo en el Servicio. entries.backTranslation: You may sign in with Google or Facebook to leave comments. You retain ownership of what you write, but grant us a worldwide, royalty-free license to display it in the Service. Do not post illegal, hateful, harassing, deceptive, or spam content; nor links, third parties' personal information, or impersonations. entries.original: Green, green with yellow stripes, or bare, under NEC 250.119.
entries.translation: Verde, verde con franjas amarillas o desnudo, según NEC 250.119.
entries.backTranslation: Green, green with yellow stripes, or bare, in accordance with NEC 250.119.

entries.original: Use green, green with yellow stripes, or bare. Conductors 4 AWG and larger may be permanently reidentified at accessible points.
entries.translation: Use verde, verde con franjas amarillas o conductor desnudo. Los conductores 4 AWG y mayores pueden volver a identificarse permanentemente en los puntos accesibles.
entries.backTranslation: Use green, green with yellow stripes, or a bare conductor. Conductors 4 AWG and larger may be permanently reidentified at accessible points.

entries.original: On a standard three-phase panelboard, circuits 1 and 2 are phase A, 3 and 4 are B, 5 and 6 are C, then the pattern repeats.
entries.translation: En un tablero trifásico estándar, los circuitos 1 y 2 son fase A, 3 y 4 son B, 5 y 6 son C, y después se repite el patrón.
entries.backTranslation: In a standard three-phase panel, circuits 1 and 2 are phase A, 3 and 4 are B, 5 and 6 are C, and then the pattern repeats.

entries.original: Use this for new work; the actual bus is a meter question. Verify with a meter before touching anything.
entries.translation: Use esto para trabajo nuevo; la barra real se determina con un medidor. Verifique con un medidor antes de tocar cualquier conductor.
entries.backTranslation: Use this for new work; the actual bus is determined with a meter. Verify with a meter before touching any conductor.

entries.original: NEC 200.6 controls neutral identification and 250.119 controls equipment grounding. For ordinary ungrounded phases, the NEC prohibits reserved colours but does not mandate black/red/blue or brown/orange/yellow; those are trade convention and job-spec choices.
entries.translation: NEC 200.6 controla la identificación del neutro y 250.119 la puesta a tierra de equipos. Para las fases no puestas a tierra ordinarias, el NEC prohíbe los colores reservados, pero no exige negro/rojo/azul ni marrón/naranja/amarillo; son decisiones de práctica y especificación.
entries.backTranslation: NEC 200.6 governs neutral identification, and 250.119 governs equipment grounding. For ordinary ungrounded phase conductors, the NEC prohibits reserved colors but does not require black/red/blue or brown/orange/yellow; these are trade-practice and specification choices.

entries.original: The NEC reserves white, grey and green but does not assign colours to ordinary ungrounded phases. The phase colours shown here are trade convention; the job spec or local practice wins.
entries.translation: El NEC reserva blanco, gris y verde, pero no asigna colores a las fases no puestas a tierra ordinarias. Los colores de fase mostrados son práctica del oficio; prevalecen la especificación del trabajo o la práctica local.
entries.backTranslation: The NEC reserves white, gray, and green but does not assign colors to ordinary ungrounded phase conductors. The phase colors shown are trade practice; the job specification or local practice takes precedence.

entries.original: No. Colour tells you what should be installed; it does not prove what an existing conductor is.
entries.translation: No. El color indica qué se debería instalar; no demuestra qué es un conductor existente.
entries.backTranslation: No. Color indicates what should be installed; it does not prove what an existing conductor is.

entries.original: The NEC puts the high leg on phase B, the centre bus. It is orange or identified by another effective means. Canada puts it on phase A.
entries.translation: El NEC coloca la pata alta en la fase B, la barra central. Es naranja o se identifica por otro medio eficaz. Canadá la coloca en la fase A.
entries.backTranslation: The NEC places the high leg on phase B, the center bus. It is orange or identified by another effective means. Canada places it on phase A.

entries.original: In a U.S. 4-wire delta panel, the high leg terminates on phase B and is orange, or identified by another effective means. Canada puts the high leg on phase A.
entries.translation: En un tablero delta estadounidense de 4 conductores, la pata alta termina en la fase B y es naranja, o se identifica por otro medio eficaz. Canadá coloca la pata alta en la fase A.
entries.backTranslation: In a U.S. 4-wire delta panel, the high leg terminates on phase B and is orange or identified by another effective means. Canada places the high leg on phase A.

entries.original: The high leg is on phase B and uses orange, or another effective means of identification.
entries.translation: La pata alta está en la fase B y usa naranja u otro medio eficaz de identificación.
entries.backTranslation: The high leg is on phase B and uses orange or another effective means of identification.

entries.original: This tool answers what to install on new work. Legacy wiring, faded insulation and earlier mistakes make colour unreliable as an identification method.
entries.translation: Esta herramienta responde qué instalar en trabajo nuevo. El cableado antiguo, el aislamiento desteñido y los errores anteriores hacen que el color no sea fiable para identificar.
entries.backTranslation: This tool tells you what to install in new work. Old wiring, faded insulation, and past errors make color unreliable for identification.

entries.original: Enter a whole circuit number of 1 or higher.

entries.original: White or grey, or three continuous white or grey stripes, under NEC 200.6.
entries.translation: Blanco o gris, o tres franjas continuas blancas o grises, según NEC 200.6.

entries.original: White or grey is required; three continuous white or grey stripes are another permitted identification.
entries.translation: Se exige blanco o gris; tres franjas continuas blancas o grises son otra identificación permitida.
entries.backTranslation: White or gray is required; three continuous white or gray stripes are another permitted means of identification.

entries.original: A standard three-phase panelboard runs A, B, C from left to right or top to bottom. Circuit rows follow that bus order. In a 4-wire delta panel, NEC 408.3(E) puts the high leg on B, the centre bus.
entries.translation: Un tablero trifásico estándar sigue A, B, C de izquierda a derecha o de arriba hacia abajo. Las filas de circuitos siguen ese orden de barras. En un tablero delta de 4 conductores, NEC 408.3(E) coloca la pata alta en B, la barra central.
entries.backTranslation: A standard three-phase panel follows A, B, C from left to right or top to bottom. Circuit rows follow that bus order. In a 4-wire delta panel, NEC 408.3(E) places the high leg on B, the center bus.

entries.original: The NEC assigns no phase colour. Follow the job specification or established local practice.

entries.backTranslation: The NEC does not assign a phase color. Follow the job specification or established local practice.

entries.original: Ampacity is the maximum current, in amps, that a conductor can carry under stated conditions without overheating. This calculator starts with NEC Table 310.16, applies NEC Table 310.15(B)(1) ambient correction and NEC Table 310.15(C)(1) conductor adjustment, then applies NEC 110.14(C) and 240.4(D) limits.
entries.translation: 载流量是导体在规定条件下不过热时可承载的最大电流（安培）。本计算器从NEC Table 310.16开始，应用NEC Table 310.15(B)(1)的环境温度校正和NEC Table 310.15(C)(1)的导体调整，然后应用NEC 110.14(C)和240.4(D)限值。
entries.backTranslation: Ampacity is the maximum current (amperes) that a conductor can carry under specified conditions without overheating. This calculator starts with NEC Table 310.16, applies the ambient temperature correction from NEC Table 310.15(B)(1) and the conductor adjustment from NEC Table 310.15(C)(1), and then applies the limits of NEC 110.14(C) and 240.4(D).

entries.original: Start with the insulation column, correct for heat and bundled conductors, then see exactly which safety limit controls.
entries.translation: 先采用绝缘温度栏，再按高温和成束导体校正，并明确显示哪项安全限值起决定作用。
entries.backTranslation: It first uses the insulation temperature column, then applies corrections for high temperature and bundled conductors, and clearly shows which safety limit is controlling.

entries.original: Continuous-load sizing and conductor derating answer different questions. The 125% rule sizes the circuit for a long-running load; it is not multiplied into the conductor derating factors.
entries.translation: 连续负载选型与导体降容解决不同问题。125%规则用于为长时间运行的负载选择电路容量；它不会与导体降容系数相乘。
entries.backTranslation: Continuous load sizing and conductor derating solve different problems. The 125% rule is used to size circuit capacity for long-running loads; it is not multiplied with the conductor derating factors.

entries.original: Count ungrounded conductors and any neutral carrying current under normal conditions, including neutrals carrying harmonics from non-linear loads. entries.backTranslation: Count ungrounded conductors, as well as any neutral that normally carries current, including neutrals carrying harmonics from nonlinear loads. entries.original: This U.S. edition uses the verified NEC Table 310.16 base ampacities, Table 310.15(B)(1) ambient factors, Table 310.15(C)(1) conductor factors, 110.14(C) termination limits, and 240.4(D) small-conductor caps. It never interpolates a missing value.
entries.translation: 美国版本使用经核验的NEC Table 310.16基础载流量、Table 310.15(B)(1)环境系数、Table 310.15(C)(1)导体系数、110.14(C)端子限值和240.4(D)小导体上限。绝不会对缺失值进行插值。
entries.backTranslation: The U.S. version uses verified NEC Table 310.16 base ampacities, Table 310.15(B)(1) ambient factors, Table 310.15(C)(1) conductor factors, 110.14(C) terminal limits, and 240.4(D) small conductor limits. It never interpolates missing values.

entries.original: What this checks
entries.translation: 本工具检查什么
entries.backTranslation: What this tool checks

entries.original: Use the insulation rating for the starting ampacity column, then separately choose the termination rating. THHN is normally a 90°C insulation, while marked equipment commonly limits the final result to the 75°C column. NM-B and unmarked equipment use the 60°C termination limit.
entries.translation: 起始载流量采用绝缘温度额定值，然后单独选择端子温度额定值。THHN绝缘通常为90°C，而有标记的设备通常会使最终结果受75°C栏限制。NM-B和无标记设备使用60°C端子限值。
entries.backTranslation: The starting ampacity uses the insulation temperature rating, then the terminal temperature rating is selected separately. THHN insulation is typically rated 90°C, while marked equipment often causes the final result to be limited by the 75°C column. NM-B and unlabeled equipment use the 60°C terminal limit.

entries.original: Canadian rule: every pair of insulated wire connectors counts as one conductor's worth of space. This aggregate input uses the largest conductor listed above.
entries.translation: 加拿大规则：每对绝缘导线连接器计一个导线容积。此合并输入按上方列出的最大导线计算。
entries.backTranslation: Canadian rule: each pair of insulated wire connectors counts as one conductor allowance. This aggregate input uses the largest conductor listed above.

entries.original: Clamps built inside the box count as one conductor's allowance, using the largest conductor listed above. Connectors that stay outside the box don't count.
entries.translation: 接线盒内部的电缆夹按上方列出的最大导线计一个容积。接线盒外的连接器不计。
entries.backTranslation: Internal clamps count as one allowance of the largest conductor listed above. Connectors outside the box do not count.

entries.original: Count every hot and neutral that enters the box — including any that pass straight through unbroken (those count too). Don't count ground wires here (next question), and don't count pigtails that start and end inside the box.
entries.translation: 请计算进入接线盒的每根相线和中性线，包括未断开而穿过接线盒的导线。此处不要计算接地导体，也不要计算始终留在盒内的引出短线。
entries.backTranslation: Count every phase conductor and neutral conductor entering the junction box, including conductors that pass through the box without being cut. Do not count grounding conductors here, and do not count pigtails that remain entirely inside the box.

entries.original: Cram too many wires into a box and connections get stressed, insulation gets nicked, and heat builds up — a classic cause of failed inspections and flickering circuits. The U.S. electrical code (NEC 314.16) assigns every wire a space allowance based on its size, and the box must have at least that much room.
entries.translation: 接线盒过满会使连接点受力、损伤绝缘层并积聚热量，常导致检查不合格和电路闪断。NEC 314.16按导线规格（线规）规定所需空间，接线盒必须至少提供该容积。
entries.backTranslation: An overfilled junction box puts stress on connections, damages insulation, and accumulates heat, often causing failed inspections and intermittent circuit interruptions. NEC 314.16 specifies the required space by conductor size (wire gauge), and the junction box must provide at least that volume.

entries.original: Do pass-through wires count toward box fill?
entries.translation: 未断开而穿过接线盒的导线是否计入接线盒填充？
entries.backTranslation: Do conductors that pass through the junction box uncut count toward junction-box fill?

entries.original: Each hot or neutral entering the box = 1 count — including wires that pass straight through unbroken (those count once too). Each device (switch/outlet) = 2 counts. All ground wires together = 1 count (with more than four grounds, each extra adds a ¼ count under the 2020 rules). Built-in cable clamps = 1 count. Pigtails that live entirely inside the box are free. Multiply the counts by your wire size's space allowance and compare to the box volume — we do exactly that, and show the math.
entries.translation: 进入接线盒的每根相线或中性线 = 1，包括未断开而穿过盒体的导线。每个器件（开关或插座）= 2。所有接地导体合计 = 1；超过四根后，根据2020规则，每增加一根加¼。内部电缆夹 = 1。始终留在盒内的引出短线不计。总数乘以相应导线规格（线规）的空间，再与接线盒容积比较。
entries.backTranslation: Each phase or neutral conductor entering the junction box = 1, including conductors that pass through the box uncut. Each device (switch or receptacle) = 2. All grounding conductors together = 1; after more than four, each additional conductor adds ¼ under the 2020 rules. Internal cable clamps = 1. Pigtails that remain entirely inside the box do not count. Multiply the total by the space for the corresponding conductor size (wire gauge), then compare it with the junction-box volume.

entries.original: Is your junction or device box big enough? Count what's in it, get a clear fits / doesn't-fit answer.
entries.translation: 接线盒或器件盒是否足够大？请计算盒内项目，即可获得明确结果。
entries.backTranslation: Is the junction box or device box large enough? Count the items in the box to obtain a clear result.

entries.original: Add one row for each conductor size. Most homes use 14 AWG (15 A circuits) or 12 AWG (20 A circuits).
entries.translation: 每种导线规格（线规）使用一行。住宅中最常见的是14 AWG（15 A电路）或12 AWG（20 A电路）。
entries.backTranslation: Add one row for each conductor size. Most homes use 14 AWG (15 A circuits) or 12 AWG (20 A circuits).

entries.original: NEC 314.16 assigns each wire size a volume allowance (for example 2.25 cubic inches for 12 AWG). Count each hot or neutral entering the box as one, each device such as a switch or receptacle as two, all ground wires together as one, and internal cable clamps as one — the total times the allowance must not exceed the box volume.
entries.translation: NEC 314.16为每种导线规格（线规）规定容积，例如12 AWG为2.25立方英寸。每根相线或中性线计一次，每个器件计两次，所有接地导体合计一次，内部电缆夹计一次。总数乘以规定容积后不得超过接线盒容积。
entries.backTranslation: NEC 314.16 specifies a volume for each conductor size (wire gauge), for example 2.25 cubic inches for 12 AWG. Count each phase or neutral conductor once, each device twice, all grounding conductors together once, and internal cable clamps once. The total multiplied by the specified volume must not exceed the junction-box volume.

entries.translation: 请计算导管内的每根绝缘导线，包括中性线和绝缘接地导线。每种规格单独使用一行。
entries.backTranslation: Count every insulated conductor in the conduit, including the neutral and any insulated grounding conductor. Use a separate row for each size.

entries.translation: 您的导线需要多大的导管？请输入要穿入的导线，即可获得最小合规规格。
entries.backTranslation: What size conduit do your wires need? Enter the wires to be pulled through it to obtain the smallest compliant size.

entries.original: long runs with lots of bends are easier with a size bigger than the legal minimum — many electricians upsize on purpose.
entries.translation: 线路较长或弯头较多时，使用比合规最小值大一档的导管更容易穿线；许多电工会主动增大规格。
entries.backTranslation: Long runs with many bends are easier to pull through a size larger than the permitted minimum; many electricians intentionally upsize.

entries.original: Under NEC Chapter 9, one wire may fill 53% of a conduit's internal area, two wires 31%, and three or more wires 40%. The calculation uses the official cross-section areas for the wire type and the conduit type.
entries.translation: 根据NEC Chapter 9，一根导线最多可占导管内部面积的53%，两根导线为31%，三根或更多导线为40%。计算采用相应导线和导管类型的官方横截面积。
entries.backTranslation: According to NEC Chapter 9, one wire may occupy at most 53% of the conduit's interior area, two wires 31%, and three or more wires 40%. The calculation uses the official cross-sectional areas for the corresponding wire and conduit type.

entries.original: Wires need free space in a conduit — jam it full and you can't pull them through, and they can overheat. The standard U.S. limits (NEC Chapter 9): one wire may fill
entries.translation: 导管内必须留有空间。填得太满会导致无法穿线，导线也可能过热。美国标准限值（NEC Chapter 9）：一根导线可占
entries.backTranslation: Space must be left inside the conduit. Filling it too full can make it impossible to pull the wires, and the wires may also overheat. U.S. standard limits (NEC Chapter 9): one wire may occupy

VoltDrop shows its full calculation so you can check its numbers against any other tool.
entries.translation: 通常有两个原因：有些计算器要求输入往返距离，另一些要求输入单程距离（仅去程）。VoltDrop 始终使用单程距离（仅去程），并在内部自动加倍。不同计算器也可能采用略有不同的导线电阻值。VoltDrop 会显示完整计算过程，便于核对。
entries.backTranslation: There are usually two reasons: some calculators require a round-trip distance, while others require a one-way distance (outbound only). VoltDrop always uses the one-way distance (outbound only) and automatically doubles it internally. Different calculators may also use slightly different wire-resistance values. VoltDrop displays the complete calculation process for easy checking.

entries.translation: 请选择端子的实际额定温度

entries.original: This result sizes the conductor for ampacity (heat) and voltage drop (distance). It does not size the whole circuit.
entries.translation: 本结果仅按载流量（热量）和电压降（距离）确定导线规格，并不确定整个电路的规格。
entries.backTranslation: This result sizes the conductor only by ampacity (heat) and voltage drop (distance). It does not size the complete circuit.

entries.original: The yes/no choice treats the entire entered load as continuous or noncontinuous. It does not model a mix of the two.
entries.translation: 此是/否选项会把全部输入负载视为连续或非连续负载，不会计算两者混合的情况。
entries.backTranslation: This yes/no option treats the entire entered load as continuous or noncontinuous. It does not calculate a combination of both.

entries.original: The widely used rule of thumb (based on a recommendation in the U.S. National Electrical Code): keep the drop on a branch circuit at or under 3%, and the total from your panel to the device at or under 5%. These are guidelines for good performance, not laws — low-voltage systems like 12 V solar are often even stricter, because 3% of 12 V hurts a lot more than 3% of 240 V.
entries.translation: U.S. National Electrical Code 的信息性说明建议：分支电路的电压降不高于3%，从配电盘到设备的总电压降不高于5%。这些是良好性能建议，并非普遍可执行的法律要求。12 V 太阳能等低压系统通常需要更严格的目标，因为12 V的3%比240 V的3%影响大得多。
entries.backTranslation: The informational notes of the U.S. National Electrical Code recommend that the voltage drop of a branch circuit be no higher than 3%, and that total voltage drop from the panel to the device be no higher than 5%. These are good-performance recommendations, not generally enforceable legal requirements. Low-voltage systems such as 12 V solar usually need a stricter target because 3% of 12 V has a much greater effect than 3% of 240 V.

entries.original: Conduit fill counts every conductor in the raceway, including the neutral and bond, and also needs the conduit type. That is a different count from current-carrying conductors.
entries.translation: 导管填充必须计算管道中的每一根导体，包括中性线和接地跨接导体，并且还需要导管类型。这与载流导体数量是不同的计数。
entries.backTranslation: Conduit fill must count every conductor in the raceway, including the neutral and bonding conductor, and also requires the conduit type. This is a different count from the number of current-carrying conductors.

entries.original: Wire has resistance, so some voltage is lost as heat before reaching the device. The widely used rule of thumb, based on a recommendation in the U.S. National Electrical Code, is to keep the drop on a branch circuit at or under 3% and the total from panel to device at or under 5%. These are performance guidelines, not laws — low-voltage systems like 12 V solar are often stricter.
entries.translation: 导线具有电阻，因此一部分电压会以热量形式损失。U.S. National Electrical Code的信息性说明建议分支电路最大3%、总路径最大5%。这些是性能建议，并非普遍可执行的法律要求。12 V等低压系统通常采用更严格的目标。
entries.backTranslation: A conductor has resistance, so part of the voltage is lost in the form of heat. The informational notes of the U.S. National Electrical Code recommend a maximum of 3% for a branch circuit and a maximum of 5% for the total path. These are performance recommendations, not generally enforceable legal requirements. Low-voltage systems such as 12 V usually use stricter targets.

entries.original: All results are planning estimates from standard published formulas and tables — not professional advice. Always follow your local electrical code, and when in doubt, ask a licensed electrician. Details in the
entries.translation: 所有结果均为依据公开公式和表格得出的规划估算，不构成专业建议。请始终遵守当地电气规范；如有疑问，请咨询持证电工。
entries.backTranslation: All results are planning estimates derived from published formulas and tables and do not constitute professional advice. Always comply with local electrical codes; if in doubt, consult a licensed electrician.

entries.original: Normal conditions only: hot environments, more than three current-carrying conductors bundled together, and continuous loads (3+ hours → 80% rule) all reduce these numbers. A derating upgrade to our Ampacity tool is on the roadmap.
entries.translation: 仅限常规条件：高温环境、超过三根载流导体成束敷设，以及连续负载（3 小时以上 → 80% 规则），都会让这些数字变小。给我们的载流量工具加上降容功能已列入计划。
entries.backTranslation: Normal conditions only: high-temperature environments, bundling more than three current-carrying conductors, and continuous loads (over 3 hours → the 80% rule) all make these numbers smaller. Adding derating to our ampacity tool is on the plan.

entries.original: a hardwired charger on a 50 A breaker may deliver at most 40 A continuously (the code requires 125% headroom for loads running 3+ hours), so the conductors must be rated for the 50 A breaker — #6 NM-B or #8 THHN, same as above; check your charger's settings.
entries.translation: 接在 50 A 断路器上的硬接线充电桩最多只能连续输出 40 A（规范要求运行 3 小时以上的负载留 125% 余量），所以导体必须额定适用于这个 50 A 断路器——#6 NM-B 或 #8 THHN，跟上面一样；记得看一下充电桩的设置。
entries.backTranslation: A hardwired charger on a 50 A breaker can only deliver 40 A continuously at most (the code requires a 125% margin for loads running more than 3 hours), so the conductors must be rated for that 50 A breaker — #6 NM-B or #8 THHN, same as above; remember to check the charger's settings.

entries.original: Diagram: Romex NM-B cable must use the 60 degree column so 50 amps needs number 6; THHN in conduit may use the 75 degree column so number 8 suffices
entries.translation: 示意图：Romex NM-B 电缆必须用 60 度那一栏，所以 50 安培需要 6 号线；导管内的 THHN 可以用 75 度那一栏，所以 8 号线就够了
entries.backTranslation: Diagram: Romex NM-B cable must use the 60-degree column, so 50 amps needs 6 gauge wire; THHN in conduit can use the 75-degree column, so 8 gauge is enough

entries.translation: 240 V 下按 50 A 选线、把电压降控制在 3% 以内的最小规格，单程距离（仅去程）：
entries.backTranslation: Minimum size for 50 A at 240 V keeping voltage drop within 3%, one-way distance (outbound leg only):

entries.original: #6 copper for Romex/NM-B cable, #8 copper THHN in conduit with 75°C terminations, or #6 aluminum — for a 240 V circuit at ordinary distances. Over about 100 feet, upsize for voltage drop.
entries.translation: Romex/NM-B 电缆用 #6 铜线，导管内的 THHN 配 75°C 端子用 #8 铜线，或者用 #6 铝线——这是 240 V 电路在常规距离下的答案。超过大约 100 英尺，就要为电压降加大线径。
entries.backTranslation: #6 copper for Romex/NM-B cable, #8 copper for THHN in conduit with 75°C terminals, or #6 aluminum — that is the answer for a 240 V circuit at ordinary distances. Past about 100 feet, go up in size for voltage drop.

entries.original: #6 copper is the standard answer, run as a 4-wire circuit with GFCI protection and a disconnect within sight of the tub. Long runs from the panel should be checked for voltage drop.
entries.translation: #6 铜线是标准答案，按 4 线电路敷设，带 GFCI 保护，并在浴缸可见范围内设一个隔离开关。从配电盘拉的长线路应核算电压降。
entries.backTranslation: #6 copper is the standard answer, run as a 4-wire circuit, GFCI protected, with a disconnect within sight of the tub. Long runs from the panel should be checked for voltage drop.

entries.original: #6 copper or #4 aluminum keeps voltage drop under the 3% planning target at 240 V and 50 A over 100 one-way feet.
entries.translation: 在 240 V、50 A、单程 100 英尺的条件下，#6 铜线或 #4 铝线能把电压降控制在 3% 的规划目标以内。
entries.backTranslation: At 240 V, 50 A, and 100 feet one-way, #6 copper or #4 aluminum keeps the voltage drop within the 3% planning target.

entries.original: . The code assigns every wire an amp rating by its insulation temperature column. #8 copper is rated exactly 50 A in the 75°C column — fine for THHN in conduit landing on standard 75°C-rated breaker lugs. But Romex (NM-B cable) must use the 60°C column no matter what's printed on the conductors, and #8 NM-B is only good for 40 A — so Romex needs #6. Sites that say "always #6" are being safe; sites that say "#8" are assuming conduit. Both are quoting real rows of the same table — check it yourself in the
entries.translation: 。规范按绝缘温度栏给每根导线定一个安培额定值。#8 铜线在 75°C 那一栏正好额定 50 A——用作导管内的 THHN、接到标准 75°C 额定的断路器接线端上，完全没问题。但 Romex（NM-B 电缆）无论导体上印着什么都必须用 60°C 那一栏，而 #8 NM-B 只够 40 A——所以 Romex 得用 #6。说“永远用 #6”的网站是在往保险的一边靠；说“#8”的网站是假设你走导管。两边引的都是同一张表里真实存在的行——自己去查一下
entries.backTranslation: . The code assigns each wire an ampere rating by insulation temperature column. #8 copper is rated exactly 50 A in the 75°C column — completely fine used as THHN in conduit, landing on standard 75°C-rated breaker terminals. But Romex (NM-B cable) must use the 60°C column no matter what is printed on the conductor, and #8 NM-B is only good for 40 A — so with Romex you need #6. Sites that say "always use #6" are erring on the safe side; sites that say "#8" are assuming you are running conduit. Both sides are citing rows that really exist in the same table — go look it up yourself

entries.original: welders get special treatment (their duty cycle legally allows smaller wire than the breaker suggests — genuinely counterintuitive), so don't panic if a welder manual specifies less.
entries.translation: 电焊机有特殊待遇（它的负载持续率在规范上允许用比断路器所暗示的更细的导线——确实反直觉），所以焊机说明书写的规格更小，也不用慌。
entries.backTranslation: Welders get special treatment (their duty cycle lets the code allow thinner wire than the breaker would imply — genuinely counterintuitive), so don't panic when the welder's manual specifies a smaller size.

entries.backTranslation: The same guides, written according to the Canadian Electrical Code — mandatory Rule 8-102, NMD90, measured in metres.

entries.original: CEC Tables 2 and 4 are numerically identical to NEC 310.16 in the 60/75/90°C columns at every shared size. The old “14 AWG copper is 20 A in Canada” difference was real in the 2012 edition. It was harmonized away around 2015–2018. Anyone repeating it is a decade out of date. But the free-air tables still differ. The harmonization is not total.
entries.translation: CEC Tables 2 and 4 在所有共有线规的 60/75/90°C 栏中，与 NEC 310.16 的数值完全相同。过去“加拿大 14 AWG 铜线是 20 A”的差异在 2012 年版中确实存在，但约在 2015–2018 年间已完成协调。今天仍重复这一说法，已经落后十年。不过，自由空气表仍然不同，协调并不全面。
entries.backTranslation: CEC Tables 2 and 4 are numerically identical to NEC 310.16 in the 60/75/90°C columns for all shared wire sizes. The old difference that “14 AWG copper is 20 A in Canada” really existed in the 2012 edition, but it was harmonized around 2015–2018. Anyone still repeating this claim today is a decade out of date. However, the free-air tables still differ, and harmonization is not complete.

entries.original: The common US convention is black = A, red = B, blue = C. The NEC does not mandate ungrounded conductor colours; it prohibits white, grey, and green. The US pattern is convention and job specification.
entries.translation: 美国常见惯例是黑色 = A，红色 = B，蓝色 = C。NEC 并未规定非接地导线的颜色，只禁止使用白色、灰色和绿色。美国的配色是行业惯例和工程规范。
entries.backTranslation: The common U.S. convention is black = A, red = B, blue = C. The NEC does not specify colours for ungrounded conductors; it only prohibits white, grey, and green. The U.S. colour scheme is an industry convention and an engineering specification.

entries.original: Canadian RW90 is unjacketed cross-linked polyethylene. American THHN has a nylon jacket and is thinner for the same copper. RW90 is roughly 14–43% larger in cross-section, depending on size. Canadian EMT is also slightly smaller inside than its US counterpart. The two differences compound.
entries.translation: 加拿大 RW90 是无护套交联聚乙烯导线。美国 THHN 带尼龙护套，在铜导体相同的情况下更细。RW90 的截面积视线规不同大约增加 14–43%。加拿大 EMT 的内部空间也比美国对应产品略小。这两项差异会叠加。
entries.backTranslation: Canadian RW90 is an unjacketed cross-linked polyethylene conductor. U.S. THHN has a nylon jacket and is thinner with the same copper conductor. RW90 has approximately 14–43% more cross-sectional area, depending on the wire size. Canadian EMT also has slightly less interior space than its U.S. counterpart. These two differences add up.

entries.backTranslation: In one common case, the permitted quantities differ by one-third. The Canadian tables give six, while we previously reported nine.

entries.backTranslation: For equipment rated under Rule 8-104, limit the conductor to 80% of its permitted ampacity.

entries.original: The NEC lets you increase ampacity below 30°C ambient. The CEC does not. Its single-point rows give no cool-ambient credit below 30°C. Bringing the US habit north silently allows more current than the CEC does.
entries.translation: 环境温度低于 30°C 时，NEC 允许提高载流量。CEC 不允许。它的单点行在 30°C 以下不提供低温增益。把美国习惯带到加拿大，会在不知不觉中允许超过 CEC 规定的电流。
entries.backTranslation: When the ambient temperature is below 30°C, the NEC allows ampacity to be increased. The CEC does not. Its single-point rows provide no low-temperature credit below 30°C. Taking the U.S. practice to Canada can unknowingly permit more current than the CEC allows.

entries.original: 3. Canada gives no credit for a cool room

entries.original: Nearly every online source we found cites Canadian colour rules as “Rule 4-038.” In the current 26th edition there is no Rule 4-038. Section 4 ends at Rule 4-036, “Busbar.” The colour rule was Rule 4-038 in the 2012 edition. It is Rule 4-032 now. Sources agreeing with each other is not verification when they are copying each other.
entries.translation: 我们找到的几乎所有网络资料都把加拿大导线颜色规则写成“Rule 4-038”。现行 26th 版中并不存在 Rule 4-038。Section 4 到 Rule 4-036“Busbar”即结束。2012 年版的颜色规则确实是 Rule 4-038，现在则是 Rule 4-032。多个来源说法一致，并不代表经过核实，因为它们可能只是在互相抄写。
entries.backTranslation: Almost every online source we found lists the Canadian conductor-colour rule as “Rule 4-038.” Rule 4-038 does not exist in the current 26th edition. Section 4 ends at Rule 4-036, “Busbar.” The colour rule really was Rule 4-038 in the 2012 edition. It is now Rule 4-032. Multiple sources saying the same thing does not mean it has been verified, because they may simply be copying one another.

entries.original: On a 4-wire delta, Canada puts the higher-voltage-to-ground conductor on phase A under Rule 4-032. NEC 408.3(E) puts the high leg on phase B, the centre bus. An electrician looking where their home code taught them finds the wrong conductor.

entries.backTranslation: In a 4-wire delta system, Canada places the conductor with the higher voltage to ground on phase A under Rule 4-032. NEC 408.3(E) places the high leg on phase B, which is the centre busbar. An electrician looking in the location taught by their home country’s code will find the wrong conductor.

entries.original: The circuit still works but delivers lower voltage at the far end: motors start hard and overheat, LEDs flicker, chargers and heaters underperform, and energy is wasted as heat in the wire. Fix it with thicker wire, a shorter route, or a higher voltage.
entries.translation: 电路仍然能用，但送到末端的电压偏低：电机启动吃力并过热，LED 闪烁，充电器和加热器功率不足，电能还会在导线里变成热量白白浪费。解决办法是换更粗的导线、走更短的路径，或者提高电压。
entries.backTranslation: The circuit still works, but the voltage delivered at the far end is low: motors struggle to start and overheat, LEDs flicker, chargers and heaters are underpowered, and the energy is wasted as heat in the wire.
