entries.original: Count every hot and neutral that enters the box — including any that pass straight through unbroken (those count too). Don't count ground wires here (next question), and don't count pigtails that start and end inside the box.
entries.translation: Comptez chaque conducteur de phase et neutre qui entre dans la boîte, y compris ceux qui la traversent sans être coupés. Ne comptez pas ici les conducteurs de mise à la terre ni les queues de cochon qui commencent et se terminent dans la boîte.
entries.backTranslation: Count each phase and neutral conductor that enters the box, including those that pass through it without being cut. Do not count grounding conductors here or pigtails that begin and end in the box.

entries.original: Cram too many wires into a box and connections get stressed, insulation gets nicked, and heat builds up. The Canadian Electrical Code (Rule 12-3034 with Table 22) assigns every insulated conductor a space allowance in millilitres, and the box must have at least that much room.
entries.translation: Une boîte trop remplie force les raccords, endommage l’isolant et accumule de la chaleur. Canadian Electrical Code (Rule 12-3034 avec Table 22) attribue un volume en millilitres à chaque conducteur isolé, et la boîte doit offrir au moins ce volume.
entries.backTranslation: An overfilled box strains connections, damages insulation, and accumulates heat. Canadian Electrical Code (Rule 12-3034 with Table 22) assigns a volume in millilitres to each insulated conductor, and the box must provide at least that volume.

entries.original: Do pass-through wires count toward box fill?
entries.translation: Les conducteurs qui traversent la boîte comptent-ils dans le remplissage de boîte?
entries.backTranslation: Do conductors that pass through the box count toward box fill?

entries.original: Canadian counting: each insulated conductor entering the box counts once; bare bond wires and cable clamps do not count. Each device counts twice. Every pair of insulated wire connectors (marrettes) counts once, using the largest conductor connected.
entries.translation: Comptage canadien : chaque conducteur isolé qui entre dans la boîte compte une fois; les conducteurs de continuité des masses nus et les serre-câbles ne comptent pas. Chaque dispositif compte deux fois. Chaque paire de connecteurs isolés (marrettes) compte une fois, selon le plus gros conducteur raccordé.
entries.backTranslation: Canadian count: each insulated conductor that enters the box counts once; bare bonding conductors and cable clamps do not count. Each device counts twice. Each pair of insulated connectors (marrettes) counts once, based on the largest conductor connected.

entries.original: Is your junction or device box big enough? Count what's in it, get a clear fits / doesn't-fit answer.
entries.translation: Votre boîte de jonction ou de dispositif est-elle assez grande? Comptez son contenu pour obtenir une réponse claire.
entries.backTranslation: Is your junction or device box large enough? Count its contents to get a clear answer.

entries.original: Add one row for each conductor size. Most homes use 14 AWG (15 A circuits) or 12 AWG (20 A circuits).
entries.translation: Ajoutez une ligne pour chaque calibre du conducteur. La plupart des habitations utilisent 14 AWG (circuits de 15 A) ou 12 AWG (circuits de 20 A).
entries.backTranslation: Add one row for each conductor size. Most homes use 14 AWG (15 A circuits) or 12 AWG (20 A circuits).

entries.original: CEC Rule 12-3034 and Table 22 assign each conductor size a volume allowance in millilitres. Count each insulated conductor once, each device twice, and every pair of insulated wire connectors once. Bare bond wires and cable clamps do not count. The required volume must not exceed the box volume.
entries.translation: CEC Rule 12-3034 et Table 22 attribuent un volume en millilitres à chaque calibre du conducteur. Comptez une fois chaque conducteur isolé, deux fois chaque dispositif et une fois chaque paire de connecteurs isolés. Les conducteurs de continuité des masses nus et les serre-câbles ne comptent pas. Le volume requis ne doit pas dépasser le volume de la boîte.
entries.backTranslation: CEC Rule 12-3034 and Table 22 assign a volume in millilitres to each conductor gauge. Count each insulated conductor once, each device twice, and each pair of insulated connectors once. Bare bonding conductors and cable clamps do not count. The required volume must not exceed the box volume.

entries.original: CEC Rule 8-102 sets a mandatory maximum: keep the voltage drop on a branch circuit or feeder at or under 3%, and the combined drop from the service to the farthest load at or under 5%. These are enforceable limits in Canada, not optional performance guidelines. Low-voltage systems like 12 V solar often need an even tighter design target because 3% of 12 V hurts much more than 3% of 240 V.
entries.translation: La CEC Rule 8-102 fixe un maximum obligatoire : la chute de tension d’un circuit de dérivation ou d’une artère doit être d’au plus 3%, et la chute combinée du branchement à la charge la plus éloignée doit être d’au plus 5%. Au Canada, ce sont des limites exécutoires, et non de simples recommandations de rendement. Les systèmes à basse tension, comme le solaire 12 V, exigent souvent une cible encore plus serrée, car 3% de 12 V a beaucoup plus d’effet que 3% de 240 V.
entries.backTranslation: CEC Rule 8-102 sets a mandatory maximum: the voltage drop of a branch circuit or feeder must be at most 3%, and the combined drop from the service to the farthest load must be at most 5%. In Canada, these are enforceable limits, not mere performance recommendations. Low-voltage systems, such as 12 V solar, often require an even tighter target because 3% of 12 V has a much greater effect than 3% of 240 V.

entries.original: Wire has resistance, so some voltage is lost as heat before reaching the device. CEC Rule 8-102 makes the limits enforceable: maximum 3% on a branch circuit or feeder and 5% combined from the service to the farthest load. Low-voltage systems like 12 V solar often need an even tighter design target.
entries.translation: Un conducteur a une résistance; une partie de la tension est donc perdue sous forme de chaleur avant d’atteindre l’appareil. La CEC Rule 8-102 rend les limites exécutoires : maximum de 3% sur un circuit de dérivation ou une artère et de 5% au total, du branchement à la charge la plus éloignée. Les systèmes à basse tension, comme le solaire 12 V, exigent souvent une cible encore plus serrée.
entries.backTranslation: A conductor has resistance; part of the voltage is therefore lost as heat before reaching the device. CEC Rule 8-102 makes the limits enforceable: a maximum of 3% on a branch circuit or feeder and 5% total, from the service to the farthest load. Low-voltage systems, such as 12 V solar, often require an even tighter target.

entries.original: For ordinary lighting and receptacle circuits in dwellings (up to 20 A, 120 V), the CEC even publishes precomputed maximum lengths (Rule 8-102(3) with Table 68) so electricians don't have to calculate at all — with a bonus: if the run from the service to your panel is short (under 20 m), the branch circuit may use the whole 5% budget itself. Dedicated circuits — fridge, kitchen, heating — don't get that shortcut and use the standard calculation, which is exactly what our tools do.

Les circuits dédiés — frigo, cuisine, chauffage — n’ont pas droit à ce raccourci et passent par le calcul standard, exactement ce que font nos outils.

entries.original: Physics doesn't care about borders: motors start hard and run hot, LEDs flicker, chargers crawl, and energy turns into heat in the wall. The Canadian difference is bureaucratic — an over-limit run can also fail inspection, since 8-102 is enforceable.

La différence canadienne est bureaucratique — un parcours au-dessus de la limite peut aussi échouer à l’inspection, puisque la 8-102 est applicable.
entries.backTranslation: Physics does not care about borders: motors start hard and overheat, LEDs flicker, chargers drag, and energy turns into heat in the wall. The Canadian difference is bureaucratic — a run above the limit can also fail inspection, since 8-102 is enforceable.

entries.translation: Les CEC Tables 2 and 4 sont numériquement identiques à NEC 310.16 dans les colonnes 60/75/90°C pour chaque calibre commun. L’ancienne différence voulant que « le cuivre 14 AWG soit à 20 A au Canada » était réelle dans l’édition de 2012. Elle a été harmonisée vers 2015–2018. La répéter aujourd’hui accuse dix ans de retard. Les tableaux à l’air libre diffèrent toutefois encore. L’harmonisation n’est pas totale.
entries.backTranslation: CEC Tables 2 and 4 are numerically identical to NEC 310.16 in the 60/75/90°C columns for every shared wire size. The old difference that “14 AWG copper is rated for 20 A in Canada” was real in the 2012 edition. It was harmonized around 2015–2018. Repeating it today puts you ten years out of date. However, the free-air tables still differ. Harmonization is not complete.

entries.original: 1. Ampacity: mostly harmonized
entries.translation: 1. Intensité admissible : surtout harmonisée
entries.backTranslation: 1. Ampacity: mostly harmonized

entries.original: Canada, three-phase where colour coding is required: red = A, black = B, blue = C.
entries.translation: Canada, triphasé lorsque le code de couleurs est exigé : rouge = A, noir = B, bleu = C.
entries.backTranslation: Canada, three-phase where colour coding is required: red = A, black = B, blue = C.

entries.original: A and B are effectively swapped across the border.
entries.translation: A et B sont effectivement inversées de part et d’autre de la frontière.
entries.backTranslation: A and B are effectively reversed on opposite sides of the border.

entries.original: 7. Conductor colour: the phases are not in the same order
entries.translation: 7. Couleur des conducteurs : les phases ne suivent pas le même ordre
entries.backTranslation: 7. Conductor colour: the phases do not follow the same order

entries.original: The common US convention is black = A, red = B, blue = C. The NEC does not mandate ungrounded conductor colours; it prohibits white, grey, and green. The US pattern is convention and job specification.
entries.translation: La convention américaine courante est noir = A, rouge = B, bleu = C. Le NEC n’impose pas de couleurs aux conducteurs non mis à la terre; il interdit le blanc, le gris et le vert. Le modèle américain relève de la convention et du devis du chantier.
entries.backTranslation: The common U.S. convention is black = A, red = B, blue = C. The NEC does not impose colours on ungrounded conductors; it prohibits white, grey, and green. The U.S. pattern is a matter of convention and the job specification.

entries.original: Canadian RW90 is unjacketed cross-linked polyethylene. American THHN has a nylon jacket and is thinner for the same copper. RW90 is roughly 14–43% larger in cross-section, depending on size. Canadian EMT is also slightly smaller inside than its US counterpart. The two differences compound.
entries.translation: Le RW90 canadien est en polyéthylène réticulé sans gaine. Le THHN américain a une gaine de nylon et est plus mince pour la même quantité de cuivre. La section du RW90 est environ 14–43% plus grande selon le calibre. L’intérieur de l’EMT canadien est aussi légèrement plus petit que celui de son équivalent américain. Les deux différences s’additionnent.
entries.backTranslation: Canadian RW90 is unjacketed cross-linked polyethylene. U.S. THHN has a nylon jacket and is thinner for the same amount of copper. RW90 has approximately 14–43% more cross-sectional area, depending on the wire size. Canadian EMT is also slightly smaller inside than its U.S. equivalent. The two differences add up.

entries.original: In one common case, the permitted count differs by a third. We reported nine conductors where the Canadian tables give six.
entries.translation: Dans un cas courant, le nombre permis diffère d’un tiers. Nous indiquions neuf conducteurs là où les tableaux canadiens en donnent six.
entries.backTranslation: In one common case, the permitted number differs by one-third. We listed nine conductors where the Canadian tables give six.

entries.original: 6. Conduit fill: the one that caught us
entries.translation: 6. Remplissage des conduits : l’erreur qui nous a rattrapés
entries.backTranslation: 6. Conduit fill: the error that caught up with us

entries.original: In the Rule 8-104 rated-equipment case, limit the conductor to 80% of its permitted ampacity.
entries.translation: Dans le cas d’équipement nominal visé par Rule 8-104, limitez le conducteur à 80% de son intensité admissible permise.
entries.backTranslation: For rated equipment covered by Rule 8-104, limit the conductor to 80% of its permitted ampacity.

entries.original: The results land close, but these are not the same operation. Show the operation the local code uses.
entries.translation: Les résultats sont proches, mais ce ne sont pas les mêmes opérations. Montrez l’opération utilisée par le code local.
entries.backTranslation: The results are close, but they are not the same calculations. Show the calculation used by the local code.

entries.original: 4. Continuous loads work in opposite directions
entries.translation: 4. Les charges continues fonctionnent en sens opposés
entries.backTranslation: 4. Continuous loads work in opposite directions

entries.original: Multiply the load by 125%.
entries.translation: Multipliez la charge par 125%.
entries.backTranslation: Multiply the load by 125%.

entries.original: The NEC lets you increase ampacity below 30°C ambient. The CEC does not. Its single-point rows give no cool-ambient credit below 30°C. Bringing the US habit north silently allows more current than the CEC does.
entries.translation: Le NEC permet d’augmenter l’intensité admissible sous une température ambiante de 30°C. Le CEC ne le permet pas. Ses lignes à valeur unique n’accordent aucun crédit pour une ambiance fraîche sous 30°C. Importer l’habitude américaine au Canada permet discrètement plus de courant que le CEC.
entries.backTranslation: The NEC allows ampacity to be increased below an ambient temperature of 30°C. The CEC does not. Its single-value rows give no credit for a cool ambient temperature below 30°C. Importing the U.S. practice into Canada quietly permits more current than the CEC does.

entries.original: 3. Canada gives no credit for a cool room
entries.translation: 3. Le Canada n’accorde aucun crédit pour une pièce fraîche
entries.backTranslation: 3. Canada gives no credit for a cool room

entries.original: Nearly every online source we found cites Canadian colour rules as “Rule 4-038.” In the current 26th edition there is no Rule 4-038. Section 4 ends at Rule 4-036, “Busbar.” The colour rule was Rule 4-038 in the 2012 edition. It is Rule 4-032 now. Sources agreeing with each other is not verification when they are copying each other.
entries.translation: Presque toutes les sources en ligne que nous avons trouvées citent les règles canadiennes de couleur sous « Rule 4-038 ». Dans la 26e édition actuelle, Rule 4-038 n’existe pas. Section 4 se termine à Rule 4-036, « Busbar ». La règle de couleur était Rule 4-038 dans l’édition de 2012. C’est maintenant Rule 4-032. Des sources qui s’accordent ne constituent pas une vérification lorsqu’elles se copient.
entries.backTranslation: Almost every online source we found cites the Canadian colour rules under “Rule 4-038.” Rule 4-038 does not exist in the current 26th edition. Section 4 ends at Rule 4-036, “Busbar.” The colour rule was Rule 4-038 in the 2012 edition. It is now Rule 4-032. Sources that agree do not constitute verification when they copy one another.

entries.translation: 9. Une référence morte depuis plus de dix ans
entries.backTranslation: 9. A reference that has been dead for more than ten years

entries.original: At ten current-carrying conductors, the NEC drops to 0.50. The CEC allows 0.70. Same bundle, different answer. This difference is current and easy to miss.
entries.translation: À dix conducteurs porteurs de courant, le NEC descend à 0.50. Le CEC permet 0.70. Même groupement, réponse différente. Cette différence est actuelle et facile à manquer.
entries.backTranslation: At ten current-carrying conductors, the NEC drops to 0.50. The CEC allows 0.70. Same grouping, different answer. This difference is current and easy to miss.

entries.translation: Constats vérifiés avec CSA C22.1:24, Canadian Electrical Code, Part I, 26e édition (2024), et NEC 2023 (NFPA 70). L’adoption est locale et les modifications locales peuvent changer le résultat.
entries.backTranslation: Findings verified with CSA C22.1:24, Canadian Electrical Code, Part I, 26th edition (2024), and NEC 2023 (NFPA 70). Adoption is local, and local amendments may change the result.

entries.original: Yes, for the shared sizes and the 60/75/90°C in-raceway columns. The current CEC Tables 2 and 4 match NEC 310.16. Free-air tables still differ.
entries.translation: Oui, pour les calibres communs et les colonnes 60/75/90°C en canalisation. Les CEC Tables 2 and 4 actuelles correspondent à NEC 310.16. Les tableaux à l’air libre diffèrent encore.
entries.backTranslation: Yes, for shared wire sizes and the 60/75/90°C columns in raceways. The current CEC Tables 2 and 4 match NEC 310.16. The free-air tables still differ.

entries.original: Are Canadian and US ampacity tables the same?
entries.translation: Les tableaux d’intensité admissible du Canada et des États-Unis sont-ils identiques?
entries.backTranslation: Are the Canadian and U.S. ampacity tables identical?

entries.original: No. RW90 is roughly 14–43% larger in cross-section than THHN, and Canadian EMT is slightly smaller inside. T90 lands within about 2% of THHN.
entries.translation: Non. La section du RW90 est environ 14–43% plus grande que celle du THHN, et l’EMT canadien est légèrement plus petit à l’intérieur. Le T90 se situe à environ 2% du THHN.
entries.backTranslation: No. RW90 has approximately 14–43% more cross-sectional area than THHN, and Canadian EMT is slightly smaller inside. T90 is within about 2% of THHN.

entries.original: Is conduit fill the same in Canada and the US?
entries.translation: Le remplissage des conduits est-il identique au Canada et aux États-Unis?
entries.backTranslation: Is conduit fill identical in Canada and the United States?

entries.original: Quick answers
entries.translation: Réponses rapides
entries.backTranslation: Quick answers

entries.original: Canada puts the higher-voltage-to-ground conductor on phase A under Rule 4-032. NEC 408.3(E) puts the high leg on phase B.
entries.translation: Le Canada place le conducteur ayant la tension à la terre la plus élevée sur la phase A selon Rule 4-032. NEC 408.3(E) place le conducteur à tension élevée sur la phase B.
entries.backTranslation: Canada places the conductor with the highest voltage to ground on phase A under Rule 4-032. NEC 408.3(E) places the high leg on phase B.

entries.original: Which phase carries the high leg?
entries.translation: Quelle phase porte le conducteur à tension élevée?
entries.backTranslation: Which phase carries the high leg?

entries.original: The 3% and 5% figures are recommendations in NEC Informational Notes. CEC Rule 8-102 makes voltage drop mandatory in Canada.
entries.translation: Les valeurs de 3% et 5% sont des recommandations dans les notes d’information du NEC. CEC Rule 8-102 rend la chute de tension obligatoire au Canada.
entries.backTranslation: The 3% and 5% values are recommendations in the NEC Informational Notes. CEC Rule 8-102 makes voltage drop mandatory in Canada.

entries.original: Is the 3% voltage-drop figure a requirement?
entries.translation: La valeur de chute de tension de 3% est-elle obligatoire?
entries.backTranslation: Is the 3% voltage-drop value mandatory?

entries.original: On a 4-wire delta, Canada puts the higher-voltage-to-ground conductor on phase A under Rule 4-032. NEC 408.3(E) puts the high leg on phase B, the centre bus. An electrician looking where their home code taught them finds the wrong conductor.
entries.translation: Dans un delta à 4 fils, le Canada place le conducteur ayant la tension à la terre la plus élevée sur la phase A selon Rule 4-032. NEC 408.3(E) place le conducteur à tension élevée sur la phase B, la barre centrale. Un électricien qui regarde à l’endroit appris dans son code d’origine trouve le mauvais conducteur.
entries.backTranslation: In a 4-wire delta, Canada places the conductor with the highest voltage to ground on phase A under Rule 4-032. NEC 408.3(E) places the high leg on phase B, the centre busbar. An electrician who looks in the location taught by their home code finds the wrong conductor.

entries.original: 8. The high leg is on a different phase
entries.translation: 8. Le conducteur à tension élevée se trouve sur une phase différente
entries.backTranslation: 8. The high leg is on a different phase

entries.translation: Confirmez l’édition en vigueur auprès de l’autorité d’inspection locale et utilisez un appareil de mesure avant de toucher un conducteur.
entries.backTranslation: Confirm the current edition with the local inspection authority and use a meter before touching a conductor.

entries.original: We shipped a Canadian conduit-fill calculator that used American conductor dimensions. It gave answers about 50% too permissive. We found it, fixed it, and went looking for what else differs. This is what we found.
entries.translation: Nous avons publié une calculatrice canadienne de remplissage des conduits qui utilisait des dimensions de conducteurs américaines. Ses réponses étaient environ 50% trop permissives. Nous avons trouvé l’erreur, nous l’avons corrigée, puis nous avons cherché les autres différences. Voici ce que nous avons trouvé.
entries.backTranslation: We published a Canadian conduit-fill calculator that used U.S. conductor dimensions. Its answers were approximately 50% too permissive. We found the error, corrected it, and then looked for the other differences. Here is what we found.

entries.original: We got this wrong ourselves
entries.translation: Nous nous sommes trompés nous-mêmes
entries.backTranslation: We got it wrong ourselves

entries.original: A verified map of the NEC and Canadian Electrical Code differences that change real answers.
entries.translation: Une carte vérifiée des différences entre le NEC et le Canadian Electrical Code qui changent les réponses réelles.
entries.backTranslation: A verified map of the differences between the NEC and the Canadian Electrical Code that change real answers.

entries.original: T90 nylon, by contrast, lands within about 2% of THHN. It is the Canadian THHN-equivalent. The conductor type matters more than the country.
entries.translation: Le nylon T90, par contre, se situe à environ 2% du THHN. C’est l’équivalent canadien du THHN. Le type de conducteur compte plus que le pays.
entries.backTranslation: Nylon T90, on the other hand, is within about 2% of THHN. It is the Canadian equivalent of THHN. Conductor type matters more than country.

entries.original: NEC vs CEC: 10 differences that change the answer
entries.translation: NEC vs CEC : 10 différences qui changent la réponse
entries.backTranslation: NEC vs CEC: 10 differences that change the answer

entries.original: Where a Canadian table has not passed our checks, the page says so. We do not borrow an American number and hide the source.
entries.translation: Lorsqu’un tableau canadien n’a pas réussi nos vérifications, la page le dit. Nous n’empruntons pas un nombre américain en cachant sa source.
entries.backTranslation: When a Canadian table has not passed our checks, the page says so. We do not borrow a U.S. number while hiding its source.

entries.original: 10. What we could not verify
entries.translation: 10. Ce que nous n’avons pas pu vérifier
entries.backTranslation: 10. What we could not verify

entries.original: The 3% and 5% figures live in NEC Informational Notes. They are not requirements. In Canada, Rule 8-102 makes voltage drop mandatory. The physics is the same. The legal status is completely different. This is the marquee difference on this list.
entries.translation: Les valeurs de 3% et 5% se trouvent dans les notes d’information du NEC. Ce ne sont pas des exigences. Au Canada, Rule 8-102 rend la chute de tension obligatoire. La physique est la même. Le statut juridique est complètement différent. C’est la différence principale de cette liste.
entries.backTranslation: The 3% and 5% values are found in the NEC Informational Notes. They are not requirements. In Canada, Rule 8-102 makes voltage drop mandatory. The physics is the same. The legal status is completely different. This is the main difference on this list.

entries.original: 5. Voltage drop: a suggestion in one country, a rule in the other
entries.translation: 5. Chute de tension : une suggestion dans un pays, une règle dans l’autre
entries.backTranslation: 5. Voltage drop: a suggestion in one country, a rule in the other

entries.original: In the CEC Rule 8-104 rated-equipment case, a 40 A conductor limit supports 32 A continuous: 40 A × 80% = 32 A. Confirm the charger's permitted setting and the installation's ampacity checks.
entries.translation: Dans le cas d’équipement coté selon la Rule 8-104 du CEC, un conducteur limité à 40 A supporte 32 A en continu : 40 A × 80% = 32 A. Confirmez le réglage permis de la borne de recharge et les vérifications du courant admissible de l’installation.
entries.backTranslation: For equipment rated under CEC Rule 8-104, a conductor limited to 40 A supports 32 A continuous: 40 A × 80% = 32 A. Confirm the charger's permitted setting and the installation's ampacity checks.

entries.original: A range is the classic 40 A circuit. In the CEC Rule 8-104 rated-equipment case, a 40 A conductor limit supports 32 A continuous because 40 A × 80% = 32 A; confirm the EV charger's setting and instructions.
entries.translation: Une cuisinière est le circuit classique de 40 A. Dans le cas d’équipement coté selon la Rule 8-104 du CEC, un conducteur limité à 40 A supporte 32 A en continu puisque 40 A × 80% = 32 A; confirmez le réglage et les instructions de la borne de recharge VÉ.
entries.backTranslation: A range is the classic 40 A circuit. For equipment rated under CEC Rule 8-104, a conductor limited to 40 A supports 32 A continuous since 40 A × 80% = 32 A; confirm the EV charger's setting and instructions.

entries.original: Minimum size at 240 V, sized at the full 40 A with 60°C terminations and kept at or under the mandatory 3% voltage-drop limit (one-way distance):
entries.translation: Calibre minimal à 240 V, dimensionné pour les 40 A au complet avec des bornes à 60°C, sans dépasser la limite obligatoire de chute de tension de 3% (distance à l’aller) :
entries.backTranslation: Minimum size at 240 V, sized for the full 40 A with 60°C terminations, without exceeding the mandatory 3% voltage-drop limit (one-way distance):

entries.original: NMD90 insulation does not by itself choose the termination column. The verified 60°C column rates #8 copper at exactly 40 A, so the conservative method our Canadian tables use has no extra ampacity headroom; check the equipment markings in the Canadian Ampacity Check tool.
entries.translation: L’isolant du NMD90 ne détermine pas à lui seul la colonne de température des bornes. La colonne vérifiée à 60°C accorde exactement 40 A au #8 en cuivre, donc la méthode prudente utilisée par nos tableaux canadiens n’a aucune marge supplémentaire de courant admissible; vérifiez les marquages de l’équipement dans l’outil canadien Vérification du courant admissible.
entries.backTranslation: NMD90's insulation does not by itself determine the termination temperature column. The verified 60°C column grants exactly 40 A to #8 copper, so the conservative method used by our Canadian tables has no extra ampacity margin; check the equipment markings in the Canadian Ampacity Check tool.

entries.original: NMD90 has 90°C insulation, but CEC Rule 4-006 still makes the termination rating part of the answer. The verified 60°C column gives #8 copper exactly 40 A under ordinary conditions.
entries.translation: Le NMD90 a un isolant 90°C, mais la Rule 4-006 du CEC fait quand même de la cote des bornes une partie de la réponse. La colonne vérifiée à 60°C donne exactement 40 A au #8 en cuivre dans des conditions normales.
entries.backTranslation: NMD90 has 90°C insulation, but CEC Rule 4-006 still makes the termination rating part of the answer. The verified 60°C column gives exactly 40 A to #8 copper under normal conditions.

entries.original: Our verified calculator selects #6 copper (26,240 circular mils): 2 × 12.9 × 40 × 150 ÷ 26,240 = 5.90 V, or 2.46% of 240 V. #8 passes ampacity but does not meet the mandatory 3% drop limit at this distance.
entries.translation: Notre calculateur vérifié choisit le #6 en cuivre (26,240 cmil) : 2 × 12.9 × 40 × 150 ÷ 26,240 = 5.90 V, soit 2.46% de 240 V. Le #8 passe le test du courant admissible, mais ne respecte pas la limite obligatoire de chute de 3% à cette distance.
entries.backTranslation: Our verified calculator selects #6 copper (26,240 cmil): 2 × 12.9 × 40 × 150 ÷ 26,240 = 5.90 V, or 2.46% of 240 V. #8 passes the ampacity test but does not meet the mandatory 3% drop limit at this distance.

entries.original: No verified Canadian equivalent is available on this site. The U.S. allowance should not be carried into a Canadian design.
entries.translation: Aucun équivalent canadien vérifié n’est disponible sur ce site. L’allocation américaine ne devrait pas être transposée dans une conception canadienne.
entries.backTranslation: No verified Canadian equivalent is available on this site. The U.S. allowance should not be carried over into a Canadian design.

entries.original: The U.S. version explains NEC 310.12 and its 83% dwelling-service method. The Canadian Electrical Code uses its own calculated-load rules in Section 8. This site has not verified those service rules well enough to publish a Canadian conductor size.
entries.translation: La version américaine explique le NEC 310.12 et sa méthode des 83% pour le branchement résidentiel. Le Canadian Electrical Code utilise ses propres règles de charge calculée à la Section 8. Ce site n’a pas vérifié ces règles de branchement assez rigoureusement pour publier un calibre de conducteur canadien.
entries.backTranslation: The U.S. version explains NEC 310.12 and its 83% method for the residential service. The Canadian Electrical Code uses its own calculated-load rules in Section 8. This site has not verified those service rules rigorously enough to publish a Canadian conductor size.

entries.original: Do not copy the U.S. 4 AWG copper or 2 AWG aluminum answer into a Canadian service design. Have the calculated load, service equipment, conductor method, and locally adopted requirements checked together.
entries.translation: Ne copiez pas la réponse américaine de cuivre 4 AWG ou d’aluminium 2 AWG dans une conception de branchement canadien. Faites vérifier ensemble la charge calculée, l’équipement de branchement, la méthode de calcul du conducteur et les exigences adoptées localement.
entries.backTranslation: Do not copy the U.S. answer of 4 AWG copper or 2 AWG aluminum into a Canadian service design. Have the calculated load, the service equipment, the conductor calculation method, and the locally adopted requirements verified together.

entries.original: The Canadian Ampacity Check tool can test a proposed conductor against the verified ampacity table. It does not replace the Section 8 service calculation. For a sub-panel or other feeder that does not supply the whole dwelling, use the Canadian sub-panel guide.
entries.translation: L’outil canadien Vérification du courant admissible peut tester un conducteur proposé par rapport au tableau vérifié du courant admissible. Il ne remplace pas le calcul de branchement de la Section 8. Pour un panneau secondaire ou une autre artère qui n’alimente pas l’ensemble du logement, utilisez le guide canadien du panneau secondaire.
entries.backTranslation: The Canadian Ampacity Check tool can test a proposed conductor against the verified ampacity table. It does not replace the Section 8 service calculation. For a subpanel or another feeder that does not supply the entire dwelling, use the Canadian subpanel guide.

entries.original: Not responsibly from the verified material available here. Use a qualified Canadian electrician or designer for the Section 8 service calculation and local approval.
entries.translation: Pas de façon responsable à partir du contenu vérifié disponible ici. Faites appel à un électricien ou concepteur canadien qualifié pour le calcul de branchement de la Section 8 et l’approbation locale.
entries.backTranslation: Not responsibly from the verified content available here. Engage a qualified Canadian electrician or designer for the Section 8 service calculation and local approval.

entries.original: In the CEC Rule 8-104 rated-equipment case, a 60 A conductor limit supports 48 A continuous: 60 A × 80% = 48 A. Confirm the charger's setting, equipment markings, and local requirements.
entries.translation: Dans le cas d’équipement coté selon la Rule 8-104 du CEC, un conducteur limité à 60 A supporte 48 A en continu : 60 A × 80% = 48 A. Confirmez le réglage de la borne de recharge, les marquages de l’équipement et les exigences locales.
entries.backTranslation: For equipment rated under CEC Rule 8-104, a conductor limited to 60 A supports 48 A continuous: 60 A × 80% = 48 A. Confirm the charger's setting, the equipment markings, and local requirements.

entries.original: In the CEC Rule 8-104 rated-equipment case, a 60 A conductor limit supports 48 A continuous because 60 A × 80% = 48 A. Other common jobs include sub-panel feeds and larger heat-pump or mini-split circuits; follow the equipment nameplate.
entries.translation: Dans le cas d’équipement coté selon la Rule 8-104 du CEC, un conducteur limité à 60 A supporte 48 A en continu puisque 60 A × 80% = 48 A. Les autres jobs courantes incluent les artères de panneau secondaire et les circuits de thermopompe ou de mini-split plus gros; suivez la plaque signalétique de l’équipement.
entries.backTranslation: For equipment rated under CEC Rule 8-104, a conductor limited to 60 A supports 48 A continuous since 60 A × 80% = 48 A. Other common jobs include subpanel feeders and larger heat-pump or mini-split circuits; follow the equipment nameplate.

entries.original: Under the conservative 60°C termination method our Canadian tables use, start with #4 copper NMD90 for 60 A; check the exact installation in the Ampacity Check tool before relying on a marked 75°C termination and #6 copper at 65 A.
entries.translation: Selon la méthode prudente à 60°C que nos tableaux canadiens utilisent pour les bornes, commencez avec du #4 en cuivre NMD90 pour 60 A; vérifiez l’installation exacte dans l’outil Vérification du courant admissible avant de vous fier à une borne marquée 75°C et au #6 en cuivre à 65 A.
entries.backTranslation: According to the conservative 60°C method that our Canadian tables use for terminals, start with #4 copper NMD90 for 60 A; verify the exact installation in the Ampacity Check tool before relying on a terminal marked 75°C and #6 copper at 65 A.

entries.original: The verified 60°C column gives #6 copper only 55 A, so that method selects #4 copper at 70 A. The verified 75°C column gives #6 copper 65 A. CEC Rule 4-006 and the equipment markings decide which termination limit applies.
entries.translation: La colonne vérifiée à 60°C ne donne que 55 A au #6 en cuivre, donc cette méthode sélectionne le #4 en cuivre à 70 A. La colonne vérifiée à 75°C donne 65 A au #6 en cuivre. La Rule 4-006 du CEC et les marquages de l’équipement déterminent quelle limite de température des bornes s’applique.
entries.backTranslation: The verified 60°C column gives only 55 A for #6 copper, so this method selects #4 copper at 70 A. The verified 75°C column gives 65 A for #6 copper. CEC Rule 4-006 and the equipment markings determine which terminal temperature limit applies.

entries.original: The #6-versus-#4 split comes from the termination column. #6 copper is 55 A in the verified 60°C column and 65 A in the verified 75°C column; the conservative method our Canadian tables use therefore starts at #4 copper for 60 A unless the installation supports the 75°C column.
entries.translation: La division entre le #6 et le #4 vient de la colonne de température des bornes. Le #6 en cuivre vaut 55 A dans la colonne vérifiée à 60°C et 65 A dans la colonne vérifiée à 75°C; la méthode prudente que nos tableaux canadiens utilisent commence donc au #4 en cuivre pour 60 A, à moins que l’installation ne supporte la colonne 75°C.
entries.backTranslation: The split between #6 and #4 comes from the terminal temperature column. #6 copper is worth 55 A in the verified 60°C column and 65 A in the verified 75°C column; the conservative method our Canadian tables use therefore starts at #4 copper for 60 A, unless the installation supports the 75°C column.

entries.original: Our verified calculator selects #4 copper (41,740 circular mils): 2 × 12.9 × 60 × 150 ÷ 41,740 = 5.56 V, or 2.32% of 240 V. The result passes ampacity and the mandatory 3% drop limit.
entries.translation: Notre calculateur vérifié choisit le #4 en cuivre (41,740 cmil) : 2 × 12.9 × 60 × 150 ÷ 41,740 = 5.56 V, soit 2.32% de 240 V. Le résultat passe le test du courant admissible et respecte la limite obligatoire de chute de 3%.
entries.backTranslation: Our verified calculator selects #4 copper (41,740 cmil): 2 × 12.9 × 60 × 150 ÷ 41,740 = 5.56 V, which is 2.32% of 240 V. The result passes the ampacity check and respects the mandatory 3% voltage-drop limit.

entries.original: A TT-30 RV receptacle is 120 V. Start with 10 AWG copper NMD90 at ordinary distances, then use the 120 V table or calculator for the actual one-way run.
entries.translation: Une prise TT-30 pour VR est en 120 V. Commencez avec du cuivre 10 AWG NMD90 aux distances ordinaires, puis utilisez le tableau de 120 V ou le calculateur pour le parcours réel à l’aller.
entries.backTranslation: A TT-30 receptacle for an RV is 120 V. Start with 10 AWG copper NMD90 at ordinary distances, then use the 120 V table or the calculator for the actual one-way run.

entries.original: The verified 60°C column supports #8 aluminum at 35 A, so aluminum is included. Confirm the conductor type, terminals, and equipment listing in the Canadian Ampacity Check tool.
entries.translation: La colonne vérifiée à 60°C accorde 35 A au #8 en aluminium, donc l’aluminium est inclus. Confirmez le type de conducteur, les bornes et l’homologation de l’équipement dans l’outil canadien Vérification du courant admissible.
entries.backTranslation: The verified 60°C column grants 35 A to #8 aluminum, so aluminum is included. Confirm the conductor type, the terminals, and the equipment certification in the Canadian Ampacity Check tool.

entries.original: No. CEC Rule 14-104 caps 12 AWG copper at a 20 A overcurrent device for ordinary circuits, so it does not pass a 30 A ampacity check.
entries.translation: Non. La Rule 14-104 du CEC plafonne le cuivre 12 AWG à un dispositif de protection contre les surintensités de 20 A pour les circuits ordinaires, donc il ne passe pas une vérification du courant admissible à 30 A.
entries.backTranslation: No. CEC Rule 14-104 caps 12 AWG copper at a 20 A overcurrent protection device for ordinary circuits, so it does not pass a 30 A ampacity check.

entries.original: Start with 10 AWG copper NMD90 for an ordinary 30 A circuit. A TT-30 RV receptacle is 120 V, while a typical dryer or water-heater circuit is 240 V; that voltage difference changes long-run sizing.
entries.translation: Commencez avec du cuivre 10 AWG NMD90 pour un circuit ordinaire de 30 A. Une prise TT-30 pour VR est en 120 V, tandis qu’un circuit typique de sécheuse ou de chauffe-eau est en 240 V; cette différence de tension change le dimensionnement sur les longs parcours.
entries.backTranslation: Start with 10 AWG copper NMD90 for an ordinary 30 A circuit. A TT-30 receptacle for an RV is 120 V, while a typical dryer or water-heater circuit is 240 V; this voltage difference changes the sizing on long runs.

entries.original: At 120 V, our verified calculator selects #6 copper (26,240 circular mils): 2 × 12.9 × 30 × 100 ÷ 26,240 = 2.95 V, or 2.46%. The 240 V table is smaller because the same volts lost are half the percentage.
entries.translation: À 120 V, notre calculateur vérifié choisit le #6 en cuivre (26,240 cmil) : 2 × 12.9 × 30 × 100 ÷ 26,240 = 2.95 V, soit 2.46%. Le tableau à 240 V est plus petit parce que les mêmes volts perdus représentent la moitié du pourcentage.
entries.backTranslation: At 120 V, our verified calculator selects #6 copper (26,240 cmil): 2 × 12.9 × 30 × 100 ÷ 26,240 = 2.95 V, which is 2.46%. The 240 V table is smaller because the same lost volts represent half the percentage.

entries.original: Use 12 AWG copper NMD90 for an ordinary 20 A branch circuit. CEC Rule 14-104 caps 14 AWG copper at 15 A, so it cannot be protected by a 20 A overcurrent device for this ordinary use.
entries.translation: Utilisez du cuivre 12 AWG NMD90 pour un circuit de dérivation ordinaire de 20 A. La Rule 14-104 du CEC plafonne le cuivre 14 AWG à 15 A, donc il ne peut pas être protégé par un dispositif de protection contre les surintensités de 20 A pour cet usage ordinaire.
entries.backTranslation: Use 12 AWG copper NMD90 for an ordinary 20 A branch circuit. CEC Rule 14-104 caps 14 AWG copper at 15 A, so it cannot be protected by a 20 A overcurrent protection device for this ordinary use.

entries.original: CEC Rule 14-104 caps 14 AWG copper at 15 A and 12 AWG copper at 20 A for ordinary circuits. NMD90's higher insulation rating does not erase the overcurrent-device cap.
entries.translation: La Rule 14-104 du CEC plafonne le cuivre 14 AWG à 15 A et le cuivre 12 AWG à 20 A pour les circuits ordinaires. La cote d’isolant supérieure du NMD90 n’efface pas le plafond du dispositif de protection contre les surintensités.
entries.backTranslation: CEC Rule 14-104 caps 14 AWG copper at 15 A and 12 AWG copper at 20 A for ordinary circuits. NMD90's higher insulation rating does not erase the overcurrent protection device cap.

entries.original: Our verified calculator selects #8 copper (16,510 circular mils): 2 × 12.9 × 20 × 100 ÷ 16,510 = 3.13 V, or 2.6% of 120 V. It passes ampacity and the mandatory 3% drop limit.
entries.translation: Notre calculateur vérifié choisit le #8 en cuivre (16,510 cmil) : 2 × 12.9 × 20 × 100 ÷ 16,510 = 3.13 V, soit 2.6% de 120 V. Il passe le test du courant admissible et respecte la limite obligatoire de chute de 3%.
entries.backTranslation: Our verified calculator selects #8 copper (16,510 cmil): 2 × 12.9 × 20 × 100 ÷ 16,510 = 3.13 V, which is 2.6% of 120 V. It passes the ampacity check and respects the mandatory 3% voltage-drop limit.

entries.original: No. This site has not verified a matching Canadian allowance, so the U.S. percentage method is not used as a Canadian sizing rule here.
entries.translation: Non. Ce site n’a pas vérifié d’allocation canadienne équivalente, donc la méthode américaine en pourcentage n’est pas utilisée ici comme règle de calibrage canadienne.
entries.backTranslation: No. This site has not verified an equivalent Canadian allowance, so the American percentage method is not used here as a Canadian sizing rule.

entries.original: The U.S. version reconciles 2/0 copper, 3/0 copper, and 4/0 aluminum under NEC methods. Canada sizes dwelling services through its own calculated-load rules in Section 8, which this site has not verified for a headline conductor answer.
entries.translation: La version américaine concilie le cuivre 2/0, le cuivre 3/0 et l’aluminium 4/0 selon les méthodes du NEC. Le Canada calibre les branchements résidentiels selon ses propres règles de charge calculée à la Section 8, que ce site n’a pas vérifiées pour en tirer un calibre de conducteur de référence.
entries.backTranslation: The American version reconciles 2/0 copper, 3/0 copper, and 4/0 aluminum according to NEC methods. Canada sizes residential services according to its own calculated-load rules in Section 8, which this site has not verified in order to derive a reference conductor size.

entries.original: A Canadian 200 A service needs a Canadian service calculation and local review. This page does not publish a conductor size from the U.S. NEC or invent a Canadian equivalent.
entries.translation: Un branchement canadien de 200 A exige un calcul de branchement canadien et une révision locale. Cette page ne publie pas de calibre de conducteur tiré du NEC américain et n’invente pas d’équivalent canadien.
entries.backTranslation: A Canadian 200 A service requires a Canadian service calculation and local review. This page does not publish a conductor size drawn from the American NEC and does not invent a Canadian equivalent.

entries.original: Use the Canadian Ampacity Check tool to test a proposed conductor against the verified ampacity table. Use the Canadian sub-panel guide for feeder work that does not supply the whole dwelling. Neither step replaces the Section 8 service calculation.
entries.translation: Utilisez l’outil canadien Vérification du courant admissible pour tester un conducteur proposé par rapport au tableau vérifié du courant admissible. Utilisez le guide canadien du panneau secondaire pour les artères qui n’alimentent pas l’ensemble du logement. Ni l’une ni l’autre de ces étapes ne remplace le calcul de branchement de la Section 8.
entries.backTranslation: Use the Canadian Ampacity Check tool to test a proposed conductor against the verified ampacity table. Use the Canadian subpanel guide for feeders that do not supply the entire dwelling. Neither of these steps replaces the Section 8 service calculation.

entries.original: Not from the verified material available here. A qualified Canadian electrician or designer must apply the Section 8 load calculation and locally adopted requirements.
entries.translation: Pas à partir du contenu vérifié disponible ici. Un électricien ou concepteur canadien qualifié doit appliquer le calcul de charge de la Section 8 et les exigences adoptées localement.
entries.backTranslation: Not from the verified content available here. A qualified Canadian electrician or designer must apply the Section 8 load calculation and the locally adopted requirements.

entries.original: After a table passes, we take a fingerprint of it and store that fingerprint in the repository. From then on, if a single digit in that table changes, the verification suite stops before the browser checks and reports the mismatch. Re-verifying the data and deliberately updating the fingerprint are separate human steps, not something the seal can enforce by itself.
entries.translation: Lorsqu’un tableau franchit la vérification, nous en calculons l’empreinte numérique et la conservons dans le dépôt. Dès lors, si un seul chiffre du tableau change, la suite de vérification s’arrête avant les essais dans le navigateur et signale l’écart. Revérifier les données et mettre volontairement à jour l’empreinte sont deux interventions humaines distinctes que le sceau ne peut pas imposer à lui seul.
entries.backTranslation: When a table passes verification, we calculate its digital fingerprint and store it in the repository. From then on, if a single digit in the table changes, the verification suite stops before the browser tests and reports the discrepancy. Rechecking the data and deliberately updating the fingerprint are two separate human actions that the seal cannot enforce on its own.

entries.original: Back-translation catches missing warnings and mangled meaning. It is a screen, not proof.
entries.translation: La rétrotraduction repère les avertissements manquants et les sens déformés. C’est un filtre, pas une preuve.
entries.backTranslation: Back translation identifies missing warnings and distorted meanings. It is a filter, not proof.

entries.original: The seal proves a number hasn't changed without somebody noticing. It doesn't prove the original was right. That's what the multi-source check is for. They're separate protections and they do separate jobs.
entries.translation: Le sceau prouve qu’un nombre n’a pas changé sans que quelqu’un le remarque. Il ne prouve pas que le nombre d’origine était juste. C’est le rôle de la vérification multisource. Ces protections sont distinctes et remplissent des fonctions distinctes.
entries.backTranslation: The seal proves that a number did not change without someone noticing. It does not prove that the original number was correct. That is the role of multiple-source verification. These protections are distinct and serve distinct functions.

entries.original: Codes are adopted locally and amended locally. The edition in force where you're standing may not be the one a table came from.
entries.translation: Les codes sont adoptés et modifiés localement. L’édition en vigueur à l’endroit où vous travaillez peut différer de celle dont provient un tableau.
entries.backTranslation: Codes are adopted and amended locally. The edition in effect where you work may differ from the one from which a table came.

entries.original: Canadian data reflects CSA C22.1:24 — Canadian Electrical Code, Part I, 26th edition (2024): Tables 2/4, 5A, 5C, 6A/6K, and 9A–9H, with Rules 4-004, 4-006, 8-104, 12-910, and 14-104. Provincial and municipal adoption varies; confirm the edition adopted locally.
entries.translation: Les données canadiennes reflètent CSA C22.1:24 — Canadian Electrical Code, Part I, 26th edition (2024) : Tables 2/4, 5A, 5C, 6A/6K et 9A–9H, avec Rules 4-004, 4-006, 8-104, 12-910 et 14-104. L’adoption varie selon la province et la municipalité; confirmez l’édition adoptée localement.
entries.backTranslation: The Canadian data reflects CSA C22.1:24 — Canadian Electrical Code, Part I, 26th edition (2024): Tables 2/4, 5A, 5C, 6A/6K and 9A–9H, with Rules 4-004, 4-006, 8-104, 12-910 and 14-104. Adoption varies by province and municipality; confirm the locally adopted edition.

entries.original: Every calculator is driven in all six editions, not just English, and the answer is checked against an expected value — hand-worked for the core voltage-drop cases, and derived from the sealed tables for the rest. We learned this one the hard way: a test run that drove only English once reported a clean pass while the main calculator was dead in four other editions.
entries.translation: Chaque calculateur est exécuté dans les six éditions, pas seulement en anglais, et sa réponse est comparée à une valeur attendue — calculée à la main pour les principaux cas de chute de tension et dérivée des tableaux scellés pour les autres. Nous l’avons appris à nos dépens : un essai limité à l’édition anglaise avait donné un résultat sans erreur alors que le calculateur principal ne fonctionnait plus dans quatre autres éditions.
entries.backTranslation: Each calculator is run in all six editions, not just in English, and its answer is compared with an expected value—calculated by hand for the main voltage drop cases and derived from the sealed tables for the others. We learned this the hard way: a test limited to the English edition produced an error-free result while the main calculator no longer worked in four other editions.

entries.original: The numeric-parity check covers the translated guides, the Terms page, and three newer pages, including this one. On those pages, every visible number is compared with its English twin, except for a value explicitly marked as a legitimate locale-specific difference.
entries.translation: Le contrôle de parité numérique couvre les guides traduits, la page Conditions d’utilisation et trois pages plus récentes, dont celle-ci. Sur ces pages, chaque nombre visible est comparé à celui de la page anglaise correspondante, sauf si une valeur est expressément marquée comme une différence locale légitime.
entries.backTranslation: The numerical parity check covers the translated guides, the Terms of Use page, and three more recent pages, including this one. On these pages, every visible number is compared with the one on the corresponding English page, unless a value is expressly marked as a legitimate local difference.

entries.original: So read the labels rather than assuming. Where the data behind a result hasn't passed for your country, the page tells you so in plain language instead of quietly presenting it as a verified answer.
entries.translation: Lisez donc les indications au lieu de tenir quoi que ce soit pour acquis. Lorsque les données derrière un résultat n’ont pas franchi la vérification pour votre pays, la page le dit en langage clair au lieu de présenter discrètement ce résultat comme une réponse vérifiée.
entries.backTranslation: So read the notices instead of taking anything for granted. When the data behind a result has not passed verification for your country, the page says so in plain language instead of quietly presenting that result as a verified answer.

entries.original: Your local inspection authority decides, not us. Confirm the result against the rules actually adopted in your area before you install anything.
entries.translation: Votre autorité d’inspection locale décide, pas nous. Avant toute installation, confirmez le résultat selon les règles réellement adoptées dans votre secteur.
entries.backTranslation: Your local inspection authority decides, not us. Before any installation, confirm the result according to the rules actually adopted in your area.

entries.original: No licensed electrician reviews or approves VoltDrop. Nobody here is holding a licence over this work. If a page ever claims otherwise, it's wrong — tell us.
entries.translation: Aucun électricien titulaire d’une licence ne révise ni n’approuve VoltDrop. Personne ici ne fait valoir une licence professionnelle pour cautionner ce travail. Si une page prétend le contraire, elle est fausse : dites-le-nous.
entries.backTranslation: No licensed electrician reviews or approves VoltDrop. No one here invokes a professional license to endorse this work. If a page claims otherwise, it is false: tell us.

entries.original: VoltDrop is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or approved by CSA. No calculator is “CEC certified,” including this one. That isn't a thing.
entries.translation: VoltDrop n’est ni affilié à CSA, ni appuyé ou approuvé par cet organisme. Aucun calculateur n’est « certifié CEC », y compris celui-ci. Une telle certification n’existe pas.
entries.backTranslation: VoltDrop is neither affiliated with CSA nor endorsed or approved by that organization. No calculator is “CEC certified,” including this one. No such certification exists.

entries.original: The Canadian conduit-fill page shows what happens when a gap closes. It used to carry a warning because its Canadian conductor and conduit tables had not passed the multi-source check. CSA C22.1:24 Tables 6A/6K and 9A–9H have now passed, so the warning is gone and the page computes from sealed Canadian data. We would rather leave a visible gap than fill it early, and remove the warning only when the evidence changes.
entries.translation: La page canadienne de remplissage de conduits montre ce qui se passe lorsqu’une lacune est comblée. Elle portait auparavant un avertissement parce que ses tableaux canadiens de conducteurs et de conduits n’avaient pas franchi la vérification multisource. CSA C22.1:24 Tables 6A/6K et 9A–9H l’ont maintenant franchie; l’avertissement a donc disparu et la page calcule avec des données canadiennes scellées. Nous préférons laisser une lacune visible plutôt que la combler trop tôt, et retirer l’avertissement seulement lorsque les preuves changent.
entries.backTranslation: The Canadian conduit fill page shows what happens when a gap is filled. It previously carried a warning because its Canadian conductor and conduit tables had not passed the multiple-source check. CSA C22.1:24 Tables 6A/6K and 9A–9H have now passed it; the warning has therefore disappeared and the page calculates with sealed Canadian data. We prefer to leave a gap visible rather than fill it too soon, and remove the warning only when the evidence changes.

entries.original: Results are planning estimates using simplified, normal-conditions methods. Real installations have conditions our inputs don't ask about.
entries.translation: Les résultats sont des estimations de planification fondées sur des méthodes simplifiées et des conditions normales. Les installations réelles présentent des conditions que nos champs ne demandent pas.
entries.backTranslation: The results are planning estimates based on simplified methods and normal conditions. Actual installations have conditions that our fields do not ask about.

entries.original: Terms that must never be translated — code names, wire types, and units — are checked for survival in every language.
entries.translation: Dans chaque langue, nous vérifions que les termes qui ne doivent jamais être traduits demeurent intacts : noms de codes, types de conducteurs et unités.
entries.backTranslation: In every language, we check that terms which must never be translated remain intact: code names, conductor types, and units.

entries.original: The easiest thing in the world would be to fill every gap with a plausible-looking number and say nothing about it. When a country-specific table has not passed, we label the boundary or refuse the answer in the place you would be about to rely on it.
entries.translation: Le plus facile au monde serait de remplir chaque vide avec un nombre qui semble plausible et de ne rien en dire. Lorsqu’un tableau propre à un pays n’a pas franchi la vérification, nous indiquons cette limite ou refusons la réponse à l’endroit même où vous seriez sur le point de vous y fier.
entries.backTranslation: The easiest thing in the world would be to fill every gap with a number that seems plausible and say nothing about it. When a country-specific table has not passed the check, we indicate that limit or refuse the answer at the very point where you would be about to rely on it.

entries.original: The English pages are compared byte-for-byte against the previous build, so nothing changes by accident.
entries.translation: Les pages anglaises sont comparées octet par octet à la génération précédente afin que rien ne change par accident.
entries.backTranslation: The English pages are compared byte for byte with the previous generation so that nothing changes accidentally.

entries.original: This is not theatre. One draft ampacity value in an early build disagreed between sources. The check caught it, the value was corrected before it shipped, and that is the whole reason the step exists.
entries.translation: Ce n’est pas du théâtre. Dans une première version, une valeur provisoire de courant admissible différait selon les sources. La vérification l’a repérée, la valeur a été corrigée avant la publication, et c’est exactement pourquoi cette étape existe.
entries.backTranslation: This is not theater. In an early version, a provisional ampacity value differed between sources. The verification caught it, the value was corrected before publication, and that is exactly why this step exists.

entries.original: VoltDrop doesn't type numbers in from memory. Every electrical table built into these calculators is compared against at least two independently produced reproductions of the published table before it goes live, row by row. They all have to agree, on every cell, or it doesn't ship.
entries.translation: VoltDrop ne saisit aucun nombre de mémoire. Avant sa publication, chaque tableau électrique intégré aux calculateurs est comparé, cellule par cellule, à au moins deux reproductions du tableau publié produites indépendamment. Elles doivent toutes concorder dans chaque cellule, sinon le tableau n’est pas publié.
entries.backTranslation: VoltDrop does not enter any numbers from memory. Before publication, every electrical table built into the calculators is compared, cell by cell, with at least two independently produced reproductions of the published table. They must all match in every cell, or the table is not published.

entries.original: VoltDrop ships in six editions across four languages. A safety warning that quietly loses its meaning in translation is a real hazard, so we screen for it: the translated text is turned back into English on its own, without the original in view, and the result is compared against what we actually meant.
entries.translation: VoltDrop existe en six éditions et quatre langues. Un avertissement de sécurité qui perd discrètement son sens pendant la traduction constitue un vrai danger. Nous le vérifions donc ainsi : le texte traduit est reconverti en anglais de façon autonome, sans que l’original soit visible, puis le résultat est comparé au sens voulu.
entries.backTranslation: VoltDrop exists in six editions and four languages. A safety warning that quietly loses its meaning during translation is a real danger. We therefore check it as follows: the translated text is independently converted back into English, without the original being visible, and then the result is compared with the intended meaning.

entries.original: We also watch the screen itself. An early version of this check reported almost everything as perfect because the English original had leaked into the process and was simply being echoed back. That run was thrown out. The check was rebuilt so the source is sealed out of it. Runs that show signs of leakage are rejected rather than trusted.
entries.translation: Nous surveillons aussi le processus lui-même. Une première version de cette vérification déclarait presque tout parfait parce que l’original anglais s’était infiltré dans le processus et était simplement répété. Cet essai a été rejeté. La vérification a été reconstruite pour tenir la source à l’écart. Les essais qui montrent des signes d’infiltration sont rejetés plutôt que crus.
entries.backTranslation: We also monitor the process itself. An early version of this check declared almost everything perfect because the English original had leaked into the process and was simply repeated. That test was rejected. The check was rebuilt to keep the source out. Tests showing signs of leakage are rejected rather than believed.

entries.original: We've tested that the seal fires on a one-digit edit.
entries.translation: Nous avons confirmé que le sceau réagit à la modification d’un seul chiffre.
entries.backTranslation: We have confirmed that the seal responds to a change in a single digit.

entries.original: You're about to size a conductor from a number on a screen. Here's exactly where that number came from, and what we do to stop it being wrong.
entries.translation: Vous allez choisir le calibre d’un conducteur à partir d’un nombre affiché à l’écran. Voici exactement d’où vient ce nombre et ce que nous faisons pour éviter qu’il soit faux.
entries.backTranslation: You are about to choose a conductor size based on a number displayed on the screen. Here is exactly where that number comes from and what we do to prevent it from being false.

entries.original: Ohm's law describes a circuit; it does not size a conductor. Wire size depends on ampacity (heat) and voltage drop (distance), neither of which is in this equation. For those, use
entries.translation: La loi d’Ohm décrit un circuit; elle ne dimensionne pas un conducteur. Le calibre dépend du courant admissible (chaleur) et de la chute de tension (distance), deux éléments absents de cette équation. Pour ces questions, utilisez
entries.backTranslation: Ohm’s law describes a circuit; it does not size a conductor. The size depends on allowable current (heat) and voltage drop (distance), two elements absent from this equation. For these questions, use

entries.original: Ask for ohms on a three-phase circuit and this calculator declines, on purpose. A single resistance figure depends on whether the load is wye or delta connected, and that changes the answer. This form does not ask, and many people wiring a motor do not know off the top of their head. Printing a number anyway would be a guess dressed up as a result.
entries.translation: Demandez les ohms d’un circuit triphasé et ce calculateur refuse, volontairement. Une seule valeur de résistance dépend du raccordement de la charge en étoile ou en triangle, ce qui change la réponse. Le formulaire ne pose pas la question, et bien des personnes qui câblent un moteur ne connaissent pas ce détail de mémoire. Afficher quand même un nombre serait une supposition déguisée en résultat.
entries.backTranslation: Ask for the ohms of a three-phase circuit and this calculator deliberately refuses. A single resistance value depends on whether the load is connected in star or delta, which changes the answer. The form does not ask the question, and many people wiring a motor do not know this detail from memory. Displaying a number anyway would be a guess disguised as a result.

entries.original: Verified Canadian wire ampacity chart from CSA C22.1:24 CEC Table 2 and Table 4, with 60/75/90°C columns, Rule 4-006 termination guidance, and Rule 14-104 caps.
entries.translation: Tableau canadien vérifié du courant admissible tiré de CSA C22.1:24 CEC Table 2 et Table 4, avec les colonnes 60/75/90°C, les bornes de Rule 4-006 et les plafonds de Rule 14-104.
entries.backTranslation: Verified Canadian conductor ampacity table from CSA C22.1:24 CEC Table 2 and Table 4, with 60/75/90°C columns, Rule 4-006 terminations, and Rule 14-104 caps.

entries.original: Wire Ampacity Chart Canada — CEC Table 2 & Table 4 | VoltDrop
entries.translation: Tableau du courant admissible des conducteurs Canada — CEC Table 2 & Table 4 | VoltDrop
entries.backTranslation: Canada conductor ampacity table — CEC Table 2 & Table 4 | VoltDrop

entries.original: The Canadian 50-amp answer: #6 NMD90 vs #8 T90 in conduit under CEC termination rules, with a verified distance table and hot tub / EV / RV framings.
entries.translation: La réponse canadienne pour 50 ampères : #6 NMD90 contre #8 T90 en conduit selon les règles du CEC sur la température des bornes, avec un tableau de distances vérifié et les cas du spa, du VÉ et du VR.
entries.backTranslation: The Canadian answer for 50 amps: #6 NMD90 versus #8 T90 in conduit, following the CEC rules on terminal temperature, with a verified distance table and the hot tub, EV, and RV cases.

entries.original: Plain-English Canadian wiring guides written to the CEC: sub-panel wire size, 50 amp circuits, ampacity tables, run-length limits, and the mandatory Rule 8-102 voltage-drop rules.
entries.translation: Guides de câblage canadiens en langage clair, rédigés selon le CEC : calibre de conducteur pour panneau secondaire, circuits de 50 ampères, tableaux de courant admissible, limites de longueur de parcours et les règles obligatoires de chute de tension de la Rule 8-102.
entries.backTranslation: Plain-language Canadian wiring guides, written to the CEC: conductor size for a sub-panel, 50-amp circuits, ampacity tables, run-length limits, and the mandatory voltage drop rules of Rule 8-102.

entries.original: Ten verified NEC and Canadian Electrical Code differences: ampacity, derating, continuous loads, voltage drop, conduit fill, conductor colours, and the high leg.
entries.translation: Dix différences vérifiées entre le NEC et le Canadian Electrical Code : intensité admissible, correction, charges continues, chute de tension, conduits, couleurs et conducteur à tension élevée.
entries.backTranslation: Ten verified differences between the NEC and the Canadian Electrical Code: ampacity, adjustment, continuous loads, voltage drop, conduits, colours, and the high leg.

entries.original: NEC vs CEC — 10 Electrical Code Differences That Change the Answer | VoltDrop
entries.translation: NEC vs CEC — 10 différences du code électrique qui changent la réponse | VoltDrop

entries.original: Watts (kW) measure real usable power, while kVA measures the apparent power the wiring must carry. For heaters and simple loads they are equal; for motors and electronics kVA can be higher, and the ratio between them is the power factor.
entries.translation: Les watts (kW) mesurent la puissance réelle utilisable, tandis que kVA mesure la puissance apparente que le câblage doit transporter. Pour les appareils de chauffage et les charges simples, les deux sont égales; pour les moteurs et l’électronique, kVA peut être supérieur. Leur rapport est le facteur de puissance.
entries.backTranslation: Watts (kW) measure actual usable power, while kVA measures the apparent power that the wiring must carry. For heaters and simple loads, the two are equal; for motors and electronics, kVA may be higher. Their ratio is the power factor.

entries.original: Canadian counting (Rule 12-3034): each insulated wire entering the box counts once at its own size. Bare bond wires are NOT counted. Each device counts twice. Every PAIR of insulated wire connectors (marrettes) counts once. Devices and marrette pairs use the largest listed conductor. Cable clamps get NO allowance in Canada. Pigtails that live entirely inside the box are free.
entries.translation: Comptage canadien (Rule 12-3034) : chaque conducteur isolé entrant dans la boîte compte une fois selon son propre calibre. Les conducteurs de continuité des masses nus NE comptent PAS. Chaque dispositif compte deux fois. Chaque PAIRE de connecteurs isolés (marrettes) compte une fois. Les dispositifs et les paires de marrettes utilisent le plus gros conducteur indiqué. Les serre-câbles ne reçoivent AUCUN volume au Canada. Les queues de cochon internes ne comptent pas.
entries.backTranslation: Canadian counting (Rule 12-3034): each insulated conductor entering the box counts once at its own size. Bare bonding conductors do NOT count. Each device counts twice. Each PAIR of insulated connectors (marrettes) counts once. Devices and marrette pairs use the largest listed conductor. Clamps receive NO volume in Canada. Internal pigtails do not count.

entries.original: Canadian fine print: bare bond wires and cable clamps get no allowance (unlike the US); marrettes count one allowance per pair, sized by the largest wire in them (we use your selected size — pick the largest present to be safe); devices deeper than 2.54 cm need an extra deduction of 32 mL per cm of depth, which this simple check doesn't include.
entries.translation: Détail canadien : les conducteurs de continuité des masses nus et les serre-câbles ne reçoivent aucun volume; chaque paire de marrettes reçoit un volume selon le plus gros conducteur raccordé (nous utilisons le calibre sélectionné; par sécurité, choisissez le plus gros conducteur présent). Les dispositifs de plus de 2.54 cm de profondeur exigent une déduction supplémentaire de 32 mL par cm de profondeur, que cette vérification simple n’inclut pas.
entries.backTranslation: Canadian detail: bare bonding conductors and cable clamps receive no volume; each pair of marrettes receives a volume based on the largest conductor connected (we use the selected gauge; for safety, choose the largest conductor present). Devices more than 2.54 cm deep require an additional deduction of 32 mL per cm of depth, which this simple check does not include.

entries.original: Cram too many wires into a box and connections get stressed, insulation gets nicked, and heat builds up — a classic cause of failed inspections and flickering circuits. The U.S. electrical code (NEC 314.16) assigns every wire a space allowance based on its size, and the box must have at least that much room.
entries.translation: Une boîte trop remplie force les raccords, endommage l’isolant et accumule de la chaleur. C’est une cause fréquente d’échec à l’inspection et de circuits intermittents. NEC 314.16 attribue un volume à chaque calibre du conducteur, et la boîte doit offrir au moins ce volume.
entries.backTranslation: An overfilled box strains connections, damages insulation, and accumulates heat. It is a frequent cause of inspection failure and intermittent circuits. NEC 314.16 assigns a volume to each conductor gauge, and the box must provide at least that volume.

entries.original: Each hot or neutral entering the box counts at its own size — including wires that pass straight through unbroken. Each device (switch/outlet) counts twice at the allowance of its largest connected conductor. All ground wires together count once at the largest ground size. Built-in cable clamps count once at the largest conductor in the box. Pigtails that live entirely inside the box are free.
entries.translation: Chaque conducteur de phase ou neutre qui entre dans la boîte compte selon son propre calibre, y compris un conducteur qui la traverse sans être coupé. Chaque dispositif compte deux fois selon le volume de son plus gros conducteur raccordé. Tous les conducteurs de mise à la terre comptent ensemble une fois selon le plus gros. Les serre-câbles internes comptent une fois selon le plus gros conducteur de la boîte. Les queues de cochon internes ne comptent pas.
entries.backTranslation: Each hot or neutral conductor entering the box counts at its own size, including conductors that pass through unbroken. Each device counts twice using the volume of its largest connected conductor. All grounds together count once using the largest ground. Internal clamps count once using the largest conductor in the box. Internal pigtails do not count.

entries.original: Fine print: pigtails that stay entirely inside the box don't count, but a wire passing through unbroken DOES count once — include it above. If more than four ground wires enter the box, each one beyond four adds a ¼ count (2020 code rule) — add roughly one extra wire to be safe. Mixed wire sizes deserve the full by-size calculation (coming soon); until then, picking your largest size is the safe way to use this tool.
entries.translation: Détail : les queues de cochon entièrement dans la boîte ne comptent pas, mais un conducteur qui la traverse sans être coupé compte UNE fois. Au-delà de quatre conducteurs de mise à la terre, chacun ajoute ¼ selon les règles de 2020. Si plusieurs calibres sont présents, choisissez le plus gros pour garder une marge sécuritaire.
entries.backTranslation: Detail: pigtails entirely inside the box do not count, but a conductor that passes through it without being cut counts ONCE. Beyond four grounding conductors, each one adds ¼ under the 2020 rules. If several gauges are present, choose the largest to maintain a safety margin.

entries.backTranslation: Different table ranges: Voltage drop alone permits {dropSize}, but the ampacity table starts at {floorSize} for {material}. {dropSize} is not treated as compliant with ampacity.

entries.original: Smallest-size proof: {size} passes and is the smallest size this ampacity table supports for {material}. The engine makes no claim about smaller sizes.
entries.translation: Preuve du plus petit calibre : {size} réussit et constitue le plus petit calibre pris en charge par ce tableau pour {material}. Le moteur ne se prononce pas sur les calibres inférieurs.

entries.backTranslation: Distance did not increase the conductor: zero listed sizes. Ampacity increased it from size {dropSize}, permitted by distance alone, to {finalSize}.

entries.original: Smallest-size proof: {size} passes. The next smaller supported size, {smallerSize}, fails the entered {load} A under the applied load rule.
entries.translation: Preuve du plus petit calibre : {size} réussit. Le calibre inférieur suivant pris en charge, {smallerSize}, échoue pour la charge saisie de {load} A selon la règle de charge appliquée.
entries.backTranslation: Smallest-size proof: {size} passes. The next smaller supported size, {smallerSize}, fails for the entered load of {load} A under the applied load rule.

entries.original: Distance did not raise the conductor beyond ampacity — zero listed sizes. Both constraints select {finalSize}; this is a normal tie.
entries.translation: La distance n’a pas augmenté le conducteur au-delà du courant admissible : zéro calibre répertorié. Les deux contraintes choisissent {finalSize}; cette égalité est normale.
entries.backTranslation: Distance did not increase the conductor beyond ampacity: zero listed sizes. Both constraints select {finalSize}; this tie is normal.

entries.original:
Continuous-load step — CEC Rule 8-104 rated-equipment case

Permitted ampacity: {permitted} A × {factor}% = {after} A available for continuous load {load} A entered load ≤ {after} A → passes

The conductor is limited to 80% of its permitted ampacity. The switch treats the entire entered load as continuous; it does not model a mixed load.

Le conducteur est limité à 80% de son courant admissible. Le sélecteur traite toute la charge saisie comme continue; il ne modélise pas une charge mixte.

entries.original: The drop targets this tool uses are starting points from common solar practice, not code requirements. There is no code rule that says 2%. Your equipment manufacturer may specify something tighter, and their number wins. The tool shows the target it used so you can change it knowingly rather than inherit it silently.
entries.translation: Les cibles de chute utilisées par cet outil sont des points de départ issus de la pratique solaire courante, non des exigences du code. Aucune règle du code n’impose 2%. Le fabricant de votre équipement peut exiger une valeur plus serrée, et sa valeur l’emporte. L’outil affiche la cible utilisée pour que vous puissiez la modifier en connaissance de cause plutôt que de l’accepter sans le savoir.
entries.backTranslation: The drop targets used by this tool are starting points from common solar practice, not code requirements. No code rule requires 2%. Your equipment manufacturer may require a tighter value, and its value takes precedence. The tool displays the target used so that you can change it knowingly rather than accept it without realizing it.

entries.original: Always verify calculations independently, follow your local electrical code and permit requirements, and hire a licensed professional where required by law or common sense.
entries.translation: Vérifiez toujours les calculs indépendamment, respectez le code de l’électricité et les permis locaux, et engagez un professionnel autorisé lorsque la loi ou la prudence l’exige.
entries.backTranslation: Always verify calculations independently, comply with local electrical code and permits, and hire a licensed professional when the law or prudence requires it.
