entries.original: For Canadian code-based calculations, VoltDrop implements CSA C22.1:24 — Canadian Electrical Code, Part I, 26th edition (2024): Tables 2, 4, 5A, 5C, and 22, and Rules 4-004, 4-006, 8-102, 8-104, 12-3034, and 14-104.
entries.translation: Pour les calculs fondés sur le code canadien, VoltDrop met en œuvre CSA C22.1:24 — Canadian Electrical Code, Part I, 26th edition (2024) : Tables 2, 4, 5A, 5C et 22, ainsi que Rules 4-004, 4-006, 8-102, 8-104, 12-3034 et 14-104.
entries.backTranslation: For calculations based on the Canadian code, VoltDrop implements CSA C22.1:24 — Canadian Electrical Code, Part I, 26th edition (2024): Tables 2, 4, 5A, 5C, and 22, as well as Rules 4-004, 4-006, 8-102, 8-104, 12-3034, and 14-104.

entries.original: For U.S. code-based calculations, VoltDrop implements the 2023 edition of NFPA 70 — National Electrical Code (NEC): Table 310.16, Tables 310.15(B)(1) and 310.15(C)(1), 240.4(D), and 110.14(C). Its conduit-fill and box-fill tools also use NEC Chapter 9 Tables 4 and 5 and NEC 314.16, including Tables 314.16(A) and 314.16(B).
entries.translation: Pour les calculs fondés sur le code américain, VoltDrop met en œuvre l’édition 2023 de NFPA 70 — National Electrical Code (NEC) : Table 310.16, Tables 310.15(B)(1) et 310.15(C)(1), 240.4(D) et 110.14(C). Ses outils de remplissage de conduit et de boîte utilisent aussi NEC Chapter 9 Tables 4 et 5 ainsi que NEC 314.16, y compris Tables 314.16(A) et 314.16(B).
entries.backTranslation: For calculations based on the U.S. code, VoltDrop implements the 2023 edition of NFPA 70 — National Electrical Code (NEC): Table 310.16, Tables 310.15(B)(1) and 310.15(C)(1), 240.4(D), and 110.14(C). Its conduit-fill and box-fill tools also use NEC Chapter 9 Tables 4 and 5 and NEC 314.16, including Tables 314.16(A) and 314.16(B).

entries.original: Results are simplified estimates for normal conditions. They do not account for every real-world factor (temperature, bundling, derating, continuous loads, local code amendments, equipment listings, and more). The Service is not a substitute for a licensed electrician or professional engineer, and using it does not create any professional relationship.
entries.translation: Les résultats sont des estimations simplifiées pour des conditions normales. Ils ne tiennent pas compte de tous les facteurs réels (température, regroupement, réduction du courant admissible, charges continues, modifications locales au code, homologations d’équipement et autres). Le Service ne remplace pas un électricien autorisé ni un ingénieur professionnel, et son utilisation ne crée aucune relation professionnelle.
entries.backTranslation: The results are simplified estimates for normal conditions. They do not account for all real-world factors (temperature, grouping, ampacity reduction, continuous loads, local code modifications, equipment approvals, and others). The Service does not replace a licensed electrician or professional engineer, and its use creates no professional relationship.

entries.original: States, provinces, and municipalities adopt codes on different schedules and may add local amendments. A result that is correct under the edition VoltDrop implements can be wrong where an earlier edition or local amendment applies. You must confirm the edition adopted by your own authority.
entries.translation: Les États, les provinces et les municipalités adoptent les codes selon des calendriers différents et peuvent y ajouter des modifications locales. Un résultat exact selon l’édition mise en œuvre par VoltDrop peut être erroné là où une édition antérieure ou une modification locale s’applique. Vous devez confirmer l’édition adoptée par votre propre autorité compétente.
entries.backTranslation: States, provinces, and municipalities adopt codes on different schedules and may add local amendments. A result that is accurate under the edition implemented by VoltDrop may be wrong where an earlier edition or local amendment applies. You must confirm the edition adopted by your own competent authority.

entries.original: VoltDrop sometimes uses a simplified or conservative method. For example, CEC Rule 4-006 limits the termination-temperature requirement to the first 1.2 m of conductor and permits a compliant transition beyond it. VoltDrop does not model that split; it applies the lower of the conductor and termination temperature ratings to the entire run. This is conservative, but it is not the full Code procedure.
entries.translation: VoltDrop emploie parfois une méthode simplifiée ou prudente. Par exemple, CEC Rule 4-006 limite l’exigence de température aux terminaisons aux premiers 1.2 m du conducteur et permet ensuite une transition conforme au Code. VoltDrop ne modélise pas cette division; il applique la plus basse des températures nominales du conducteur et de la terminaison à toute la longueur. Cette méthode est prudente, mais elle ne constitue pas la procédure complète du Code.
entries.backTranslation: VoltDrop sometimes uses a simplified or cautious method. For example, CEC Rule 4-006 limits the termination-temperature requirement to the first 1.2 m of the conductor and then permits a code-compliant transition. VoltDrop does not model this division; it applies the lower of the conductor and termination temperature ratings to the entire length. This method is cautious, but it is not the Code’s complete procedure.

entries.original: Where a Code does not expressly answer an implementation detail, VoltDrop may make a conservative choice that your local inspector or authority may not share. For example, CEC Rule 4-004 does not expressly address installed spare power or lighting conductors; VoltDrop counts them toward Table 5C.
entries.translation: Lorsqu’un Code ne règle pas expressément un détail de mise en œuvre, VoltDrop peut faire un choix prudent que votre inspecteur ou votre autorité locale peut ne pas partager. Par exemple, CEC Rule 4-004 ne traite pas expressément des conducteurs de réserve installés pour la puissance ou l’éclairage; VoltDrop les compte aux fins de Table 5C.
entries.backTranslation: When a Code does not expressly settle an implementation detail, VoltDrop may make a cautious choice that your local inspector or authority may not share. For example, CEC Rule 4-004 does not expressly address installed spare conductors for power or lighting; VoltDrop counts them for purposes of Table 5C.

entries.original: Green or green with yellow stripes under CEC Rule 4-032. Those colours are reserved for grounding and bonding.
entries.translation: Vert ou vert avec des rayures jaunes selon CEC Rule 4-032. Ces couleurs sont réservées à la mise à la terre et à la continuité des masses.
entries.backTranslation: Green or green with yellow stripes, in accordance with CEC Rule 4-032. These colors are reserved for grounding and bonding.

entries.original: Use green or green with yellow stripes. Larger than #2 AWG may be permanently marked at each end and accessible point; these colours are reserved for grounding and bonding.
entries.translation: Utilisez le vert ou le vert avec des rayures jaunes. Au-dessus de #2 AWG, un marquage permanent est permis à chaque extrémité et point accessible; ces couleurs sont réservées à la mise à la terre et à la continuité des masses.
entries.backTranslation: Use green or green with yellow stripes. Above #2 AWG, permanent marking is permitted at each end and accessible point; these colors are reserved for grounding and bonding.

entries.original: On a standard three-phase panelboard, circuits 1 and 2 are phase A, 3 and 4 are B, 5 and 6 are C, then the pattern repeats.
entries.translation: Dans un panneau triphasé standard, les circuits 1 et 2 sont sur la phase A, 3 et 4 sur B, 5 et 6 sur C, puis la séquence se répète.
entries.backTranslation: In a standard three-phase panel, circuits 1 and 2 are on phase A, 3 and 4 on B, 5 and 6 on C, and then the sequence repeats.

entries.original: Use this for new work; the actual bus is a meter question. Verify with a meter before touching anything.
entries.translation: Utilisez ceci pour les travaux neufs; la barre réelle se confirme au multimètre. Vérifiez au multimètre avant de toucher quoi que ce soit.
entries.backTranslation: Use this for new work; confirm the actual bus with a multimeter. Check with a multimeter before touching anything.

entries.original: CEC Rule 4-032 uses black and red for single-phase conductors, adds white where a neutral is required, and sets three-phase as A red, B black, C blue. Green and green/yellow are reserved for grounding and bonding.
entries.translation: CEC Rule 4-032 utilise le noir et le rouge pour les conducteurs monophasés, ajoute le blanc lorsqu’un neutre est requis et fixe le triphasé à A rouge, B noir, C bleu. Le vert et le vert/jaune sont réservés à la mise à la terre et à la continuité des masses.
entries.backTranslation: CEC Rule 4-032 uses black and red for single-phase conductors, adds white when a neutral is required, and sets three-phase colors as A red, B black, C blue. Green and green/yellow are reserved for grounding and bonding.

entries.original: Where colour-coded circuits are required, CEC Rule 4-032 sets these colours.
entries.translation: Lorsque le codage par couleur est exigé, CEC Rule 4-032 fixe ces couleurs.
entries.backTranslation: When color coding is required, CEC Rule 4-032 specifies these colors.

entries.original: No. Colour tells you what should be installed; it does not prove what an existing conductor is.
entries.translation: Non. La couleur indique ce qui devrait être installé; elle ne prouve pas la fonction d’un conducteur existant.
entries.backTranslation: No. Color indicates what should be installed; it does not prove the function of an existing conductor.

entries.original: Canada puts the higher-voltage-to-ground conductor on phase A. The NEC puts the high leg on phase B.
entries.translation: Le Canada place le conducteur ayant la tension la plus élevée par rapport à la terre sur la phase A. Le NEC place la branche haute sur la phase B.
entries.backTranslation: Canada places the conductor with the higher voltage to ground on phase A. The NEC places the high leg on phase B.

entries.original: In a Canadian 4-wire delta system, phase A is the conductor with the higher voltage to ground. The NEC puts the high leg on phase B.
entries.translation: Dans un réseau delta canadien à 4 fils, la phase A est le conducteur ayant la tension la plus élevée par rapport à la terre. Le NEC place la branche haute sur la phase B.
entries.backTranslation: In a Canadian 4-wire delta system, phase A is the conductor with the higher voltage to ground. The NEC places the high leg on phase B.

entries.original: Phase A is the high leg and remains red in the three-phase colour sequence.
entries.translation: La phase A est la branche haute et demeure rouge dans la séquence triphasée.
entries.backTranslation: Phase A is the high leg and remains red in the three-phase sequence.

entries.original: This tool answers what to install on new work. Legacy wiring, faded insulation and earlier mistakes make colour unreliable as an identification method.
entries.translation: Cet outil indique quoi installer dans des travaux neufs. Le câblage ancien, l’isolant décoloré et les erreurs passées rendent la couleur peu fiable pour l’identification.
entries.backTranslation: This tool indicates what to install in new work. Old wiring, discolored insulation, and past errors make color unreliable for identification.

entries.original: Enter a whole circuit number of 1 or higher.
entries.translation: Entrez un numéro de circuit entier de 1 ou plus.
entries.backTranslation: Enter a whole-number circuit number of 1 or greater.

entries.original: White where a neutral is required under CEC Rule 4-032; Rule 4-024 covers permitted white-with-coloured-stripe identification.
entries.translation: Blanc lorsqu’un neutre est requis selon CEC Rule 4-032; Rule 4-024 traite de l’identification permise en blanc avec une rayure de couleur.
entries.backTranslation: White when a neutral is required, in accordance with CEC Rule 4-032; Rule 4-024 covers permitted identification using white with a colored stripe.

entries.original: Use white where a neutral is required. Rule 4-024 also covers permitted white-with-coloured-stripe identification.
entries.translation: Utilisez le blanc lorsqu’un neutre est requis. Rule 4-024 traite aussi de l’identification permise en blanc avec une rayure de couleur.
entries.backTranslation: Use white when a neutral is required. Rule 4-024 also covers permitted identification using white with a colored stripe.

entries.original: Standard three-phase panel rows follow A, B, C in repeating pairs. For a 4-wire delta system, the Canadian rule makes phase A the higher-voltage-to-ground conductor; do not carry the U.S. phase-B position across the border.
entries.translation: Les rangées d’un panneau triphasé standard suivent A, B, C par paires répétées. Dans un réseau delta à 4 fils, la règle canadienne fait de la phase A le conducteur ayant la tension la plus élevée par rapport à la terre; ne transposez pas la position américaine sur la phase B.
entries.backTranslation: The rows of a standard three-phase panel follow A, B, C in repeating pairs. In a 4-wire delta system, the Canadian rule makes phase A the conductor with the higher voltage to ground; do not transfer the U.S. phase B position.

entries.original: This is the prescribed colour for the selected conductor.
entries.translation: Il s’agit de la couleur prescrite pour le conducteur sélectionné.
entries.backTranslation: This is the prescribed color for the selected conductor.

entries.original: This tells you what to install on new work. What is already in the wall is a meter question—verify with a meter before touching anything.
entries.translation: Ceci indique quoi installer dans des travaux neufs. Ce qui est déjà dans le mur se vérifie au multimètre — vérifiez au multimètre avant de toucher quoi que ce soit.
entries.backTranslation: This indicates what to install in new work. What is already in the wall must be checked with a multimeter—check with a multimeter before touching anything.

entries.backTranslation: The Canadian answer for 40 A: 8 AWG NMD90 copper per the 60°C method, with a verified distance table and range and EV examples.

entries.original: For an in-between temperature, the next higher listed row is used; never interpolation or rounding down.
entries.translation: 对于介于两点之间的温度，采用下一个更高的已列行；绝不插值或向下取整。
entries.backTranslation: For a temperature between two points, use the next higher listed row; never interpolate or round down.

entries.original: CEC Table 5A lists single ambient points only above 30°C. At or below 30°C the factor is 1.00, with no cool-ambient credit. Between listed points, this calculator uses the next higher row; it never interpolates or rounds down.
entries.translation: CEC Table 5A仅列出30°C以上的单点环境温度。30°C或以下采用1.00，不给予低温增容。输入位于两个列出温度之间时，本计算器采用下一个更高温度行；绝不插值或向下取整。
entries.backTranslation: CEC Table 5A lists only single ambient-temperature points above 30°C. At 30°C or below, use 1.00, with no cooler-temperature credit. When the input falls between two listed temperatures, this calculator uses the next higher temperature row; it never interpolates or rounds down.

entries.original: Ampacity is the maximum current a conductor can carry under stated conditions without overheating. This Canadian calculator uses CSA C22.1:24 — Canadian Electrical Code, Part I, 26th edition (2024): Tables 2/4, 5A, and 5C, with Rules 4-004, 4-006, 8-104, and 14-104.
entries.translation: 载流量是导体在规定条件下不过热时可承载的最大电流。本加拿大计算器采用CSA C22.1:24 — Canadian Electrical Code, Part I, 26th edition (2024)中的Tables 2/4、5A和5C，以及Rules 4-004、4-006、8-104和14-104。
entries.backTranslation: Ampacity is the maximum current a conductor can carry under stated conditions without overheating. This Canadian calculator uses CSA C22.1:24 — Canadian Electrical Code, Part I, 26th edition (2024), Tables 2/4, 5A and 5C, and Rules 4-004, 4-006, 8-104 and 14-104.

entries.original: Apply the Canadian ambient and conductor-count factors, then see which CEC safety limit controls.
entries.translation: 应用加拿大环境温度和导体数量系数，然后查看哪项CEC安全上限起决定作用。

entries.original: CEC Rule 8-104 limits a continuous load to 80% of corrected ampacity for standard 80%-rated equipment. This is a separate check, not a derating multiplier.
entries.translation: 对于标准80%额定设备，CEC Rule 8-104将连续负载限制为校正载流量的80%。这是独立检查，不是降容系数。

entries.original: Continuous-load limit (corrected ampacity × 80%)
entries.translation: 连续负载上限（校正载流量 × 80%）

entries.original: Continuous-load sizing and conductor derating answer different questions. CEC Rule 8-104 checks that the continuous load is no more than 80% of corrected ampacity for standard 80%-rated equipment. It is never combined with a 125% multiplier.
entries.translation: 连续负载选型与导体降容回答不同问题。对于标准80%额定设备，CEC Rule 8-104检查连续负载是否不超过校正载流量的80%。该检查绝不与125%乘数同时使用。
entries.backTranslation: Continuous-load sizing and conductor derating answer different questions. For standard 80%-rated equipment, CEC Rule 8-104 checks whether the continuous load is no more than 80% of corrected ampacity. This check is never used together with a 125% multiplier.

entries.translation: 加拿大数据来源：CSA C22.1:24 — Canadian Electrical Code, Part I, 26th edition (2024)。本计算器采用Tables 2/4、5A和5C，以及Rules 4-004、4-006、8-104和14-104。各省采用时间和修订内容不同；请确认当地采用的版本。
entries.backTranslation: Canadian data source:CSA C22.1:24 — Canadian Electrical Code, Part I, 26th edition (2024). This calculator uses Tables 2/4, 5A and 5C, and Rules 4-004, 4-006, 8-104 and 14-104. Provincial adoption dates and amendments differ; confirm the version adopted locally.

entries.original: Count insulated power and lighting conductors. A bonding conductor never counts. Do not count control or signal conductors, or a neutral carrying only unbalanced current in a normally balanced circuit. Count a neutral carrying current comparable to the phase conductors or significant harmonic current from non-linear loads. The Code is silent on spares; VoltDrop counts installed power or lighting spares by default as a conservative reading, not a Code quotation. Your local authority may differ.
entries.translation: 计算绝缘功率及照明导体。接地跨接导体永远不计。控制和信号导体不计；正常平衡电路中仅承载不平衡电流的中性线也不计。承载与相导体相当电流的中性线，或承载非线性负载显著谐波电流的中性线应计。Code未说明备用导体；VoltDrop默认计入已安装的功率或照明备用导体，作为保守解释而非Code原文。当地主管机构可能有不同意见。
entries.backTranslation: Count insulated power and lighting conductors. A bonding conductor never counts. Control and signal conductors do not count; a neutral in a normally balanced circuit that carries only unbalanced current also does not count. Count a neutral carrying current comparable to the phase conductors, or significant harmonic current from nonlinear loads. The Code does not address spare conductors; VoltDrop counts installed power or lighting spares by default as a conservative interpretation, not as Code text. The local authority may hold a different view.

The Code is silent on spares, so VoltDrop counts installed power or lighting spares by default as a conservative reading, not a Code quotation; your local authority may differ.
entries.translation: 根据CEC Rule 4-004，计算绝缘功率及照明导体。接地跨接导体永远不计。控制和信号导体不计。正常平衡电路中仅承载不平衡电流的中性线不计；承载与各相相当电流或非线性负载显著谐波电流的中性线应计。Code未说明备用导体，因此VoltDrop默认计入已安装的功率或照明备用导体，作为保守解释而非Code原文；当地主管机构可能有不同意见。

entries.backTranslation: This Canadian edition uses base ampacity from CSA C22.1:24 Tables 2/4, ambient factors from Table 5A, conductor factors from Table 5C, counting under Rule 4-004, a conservative simplified Rule 4-006 termination check, Rule 14-104 small-conductor caps, and a separate Rule 8-104 continuous-load check.

entries.original: Use the conductor insulation rating for the starting column. Under CEC Rule 4-006, marked equipment uses its marked termination temperature. For unmarked equipment, use 60°C when it is rated not more than 100 A or marked for #1 AWG and smaller, and 75°C above that. The rule applies to the first 1.2 m from a termination and permits a transition beyond it. VoltDrop conservatively applies the lower termination limit throughout as a simplified method.
entries.translation: 起始温度栏采用导体绝缘额定温度。根据CEC Rule 4-006，有标记设备采用其标明的端子温度。无标记设备若额定不超过100 A或标明适用于#1 AWG及更小导体，则采用60°C；超过该范围采用75°C。该规则适用于端子起的前1.2 m，并允许在其后转换。VoltDrop采用保守的简化方法，在全长范围内应用较低的端子上限。
entries.backTranslation: Use the conductor insulation rating as the starting temperature column. Under CEC Rule 4-006, marked equipment uses its marked termination temperature. For unmarked equipment rated no more than 100 A or marked for #1 AWG and smaller conductors, use 60°C; above that range use 75°C. The rule applies to the first 1.2 m from the termination and permits a transition afterward. VoltDrop uses a conservative simplified method and applies the lower termination cap for the full length.

entries.backTranslation: According to CEC Rule 12-3034, bare bonding conductors do not count.

entries.original: Canadian rule: every pair of insulated wire connectors counts as one conductor's worth of space. This aggregate input uses the largest conductor listed above.

entries.backTranslation: Canadian rule: each pair of insulated wire connectors counts as one conductor allowance. This aggregate input uses the largest conductor listed above.

entries.original: Cable clamps receive no volume allowance under the Canadian counting rule.
entries.translation: 根据加拿大计数规则，电缆夹不预留容积。
entries.backTranslation: Under the Canadian counting rule, cable clamps do not reserve volume.

entries.original: Count every hot and neutral that enters the box — including any that pass straight through unbroken (those count too). Don't count ground wires here (next question), and don't count pigtails that start and end inside the box.
entries.translation: 请计算进入接线盒的每根相线和中性线，包括未断开而穿过接线盒的导线。此处不要计算接地导体，也不要计算始终留在盒内的引出短线。
entries.backTranslation: Count every phase conductor and neutral conductor entering the junction box, including conductors that pass through the box without being cut. Do not count grounding conductors here, and do not count pigtails that remain entirely inside the box.

entries.original: Cram too many wires into a box and connections get stressed, insulation gets nicked, and heat builds up. The Canadian Electrical Code (Rule 12-3034 with Table 22) assigns every insulated conductor a space allowance in millilitres, and the box must have at least that much room.
entries.translation: 接线盒过满会使连接点受力、损伤绝缘层并积聚热量。Canadian Electrical Code（Rule 12-3034和Table 22）按毫升为每根绝缘导线规定空间，接线盒必须至少提供该容积。
entries.backTranslation: An overfilled junction box puts stress on connections, damages insulation, and accumulates heat. Canadian Electrical Code (Rule 12-3034 and Table 22) specifies space in millilitres for each insulated wire, and the junction box must provide at least that volume.

entries.original: Do pass-through wires count toward box fill?
entries.translation: 未断开而穿过接线盒的导线是否计入接线盒填充？
entries.backTranslation: Do conductors that pass through the junction box uncut count toward junction-box fill?

entries.original: Canadian counting: each insulated conductor entering the box counts once; bare bond wires and cable clamps do not count. Each device counts twice. Every pair of insulated wire connectors (marrettes) counts once, using the largest conductor connected.
entries.translation: 加拿大计数规则：每根进入接线盒的绝缘导体计一次；裸露的接地跨接导体和电缆夹不计。每个器件计两次。每对绝缘导线连接器（marrettes）计一次，并按其中最大的导体计算。
entries.backTranslation: Canadian counting rule: each insulated conductor entering the junction box is counted once; bare bonding conductors and cable clamps do not count. Each device is counted twice. Each pair of insulated wire connectors (marrettes) is counted once, calculated according to the largest conductor among them.

entries.original: Is your junction or device box big enough? Count what's in it, get a clear fits / doesn't-fit answer.
entries.translation: 接线盒或器件盒是否足够大？请计算盒内项目，即可获得明确结果。
entries.backTranslation: Is the junction box or device box large enough? Count the items in the box to obtain a clear result.

entries.original: Add one row for each conductor size. Most homes use 14 AWG (15 A circuits) or 12 AWG (20 A circuits).
entries.translation: 每种导线规格（线规）使用一行。住宅中最常见的是14 AWG（15 A电路）或12 AWG（20 A电路）。
entries.backTranslation: Add one row for each conductor size. Most homes use 14 AWG (15 A circuits) or 12 AWG (20 A circuits).

entries.original: CEC Rule 12-3034 and Table 22 assign each conductor size a volume allowance in millilitres. Count each insulated conductor once, each device twice, and every pair of insulated wire connectors once. Bare bond wires and cable clamps do not count. The required volume must not exceed the box volume.
entries.translation: CEC Rule 12-3034和Table 22按毫升为每种导线规格（线规）规定容积。每根绝缘导线计一次，每个器件计两次，每对绝缘导线连接器计一次。裸露的接地跨接导体和电缆夹不计。所需容积不得超过接线盒容积。
entries.backTranslation: CEC Rule 12-3034 and Table 22 specify a volume in millilitres for each conductor size (wire gauge). Count each insulated wire once, each device twice, and each pair of insulated wire connectors once. Bare bonding conductors and cable clamps do not count. The required volume must not exceed the junction-box volume.

entries.original: This result sizes the conductor for ampacity (heat) and voltage drop (distance). It does not size the whole circuit.
entries.translation: 本结果仅按载流量（热量）和电压降（距离）确定导线规格，并不确定整个电路的规格。
entries.backTranslation: This result sizes the conductor only by ampacity (heat) and voltage drop (distance). It does not size the complete circuit.

entries.original: The yes/no choice treats the entire entered load as continuous or noncontinuous. It does not model a mix of the two.
entries.translation: 此是/否选项会把全部输入负载视为连续或非连续负载，不会计算两者混合的情况。
entries.backTranslation: This yes/no option treats the entire entered load as continuous or noncontinuous. It does not calculate a combination of both.

entries.original: CEC Rule 8-102 sets a mandatory maximum: keep the voltage drop on a branch circuit or feeder at or under 3%, and the combined drop from the service to the farthest load at or under 5%. These are enforceable limits in Canada, not optional performance guidelines. Low-voltage systems like 12 V solar often need an even tighter design target because 3% of 12 V hurts much more than 3% of 240 V.
entries.translation: CEC Rule 8-102 规定了强制最大值：分支电路或馈线的电压降必须不高于3%，从供电进线到最远负载的组合电压降必须不高于5%。在加拿大，这些是可执行的限值，而不是可选的性能建议。12 V 太阳能等低压系统通常还需要更严格的设计目标，因为12 V的3%比240 V的3%影响大得多。
entries.backTranslation: CEC Rule 8-102 specifies mandatory maximums: voltage drop for a branch circuit or feeder must be no higher than 3%, and combined voltage drop from the service entrance to the farthest load must be no higher than 5%. In Canada, these are enforceable limits, not optional performance recommendations. Low-voltage systems such as 12 V solar usually need an even stricter design target because 3% of 12 V has a much greater effect than 3% of 240 V.

entries.original: Conduit fill counts every conductor in the raceway, including the neutral and bond, and also needs the conduit type. That is a different count from current-carrying conductors.
entries.translation: 导管填充必须计算管道中的每一根导体，包括中性线和接地跨接导体，并且还需要导管类型。这与载流导体数量是不同的计数。
entries.backTranslation: Conduit fill must count every conductor in the raceway, including the neutral and bonding conductor, and also requires the conduit type. This is a different count from the number of current-carrying conductors.

entries.original: Wire has resistance, so some voltage is lost as heat before reaching the device. CEC Rule 8-102 makes the limits enforceable: maximum 3% on a branch circuit or feeder and 5% combined from the service to the farthest load. Low-voltage systems like 12 V solar often need an even tighter design target.
entries.translation: 导线具有电阻，因此一部分电压会在到达设备前以热量形式损失。CEC Rule 8-102 使限值具有强制性：分支电路或馈线最大3%，从供电进线到最远负载的组合路径最大5%。12 V太阳能等低压系统通常需要更严格的设计目标。
entries.backTranslation: A conductor has resistance, so part of the voltage is lost as heat before reaching the device. CEC Rule 8-102 makes the limits mandatory: a maximum of 3% for a branch circuit or feeder, and a maximum of 5% for the combined path from the service entrance to the farthest load. Low-voltage systems such as 12 V solar usually need a stricter design target.

entries.original: (CEC Rule 4-006). Wire insulation may be rated 90°C — NMD90 and T90 both are. Marked equipment uses its marked termination temperature. For unmarked equipment, use 60°C when rated not more than 100 A or marked for #1 AWG and smaller, and 75°C above that. entries.translation: 对住宅里普通的照明和插座电路（不超过 20 A、120 V），CEC 甚至直接给出了预先算好的最大长度（Rule 8-102(3) 配合 Table 68），电工完全不用自己算——还有个额外的好处：如果从供电进线到你家配电盘这一段很短（不到 20 m），分支电路可以自己把 5% 的额度全部用掉。专用电路——冰箱、厨房、供暖——享受不到这个捷径，要走标准计算，而这正是我们的工具在做的事。

entries.original: Physics doesn't care about borders: motors start hard and run hot, LEDs flicker, chargers crawl, and energy turns into heat in the wall. The Canadian difference is bureaucratic — an over-limit run can also fail inspection, since 8-102 is enforceable.
entries.translation: 物理规律不认国界：电机启动吃力、运行发烫，LED 闪烁，充电器变慢，电能还在墙里变成热量白白浪费。加拿大这边的区别在于行政层面——超出限值的线路还可能通不过检验，因为 8-102 是可强制执行的。
entries.backTranslation: Physics does not recognize borders: motors strain to start and run hot, LEDs flicker, chargers slow down, and electricity is wasted as heat inside the walls. The difference on the Canadian side is administrative — a run over the limit can also fail inspection, because 8-102 is enforceable.

entries.original: Yes — for dwelling lighting and general-use receptacle circuits up to 20 A at 120 V, Rule 8-102(3) with Table 68 gives precomputed maximum lengths. Dedicated circuits like kitchen, fridge, and heating use the standard voltage-drop calculation instead.
entries.translation: 有——对住宅照明和一般用途插座电路，在 120 V、不超过 20 A 的情况下，Rule 8-102(3) 配合 Table 68 给出了预先算好的最大长度。厨房、冰箱、供暖这类专用电路则要用标准的电压降计算。
entries.backTranslation: Yes — for residential lighting and general-purpose receptacle circuits at 120 V and no more than 20 A, Rule 8-102(3) together with Table 68 gives pre-calculated maximum lengths. Dedicated circuits such as kitchen, fridge, and heating must use the standard voltage drop calculation.

entries.original: A lookup table of precomputed maximum circuit lengths for dwelling lighting and general-use receptacle circuits up to 20 A at 120 V, provided by Rule 8-102(3) so routine residential circuits don't need a manual calculation. Dedicated circuits are excluded and use the standard method.
entries.translation: 它是一张查询表，列出住宅照明和一般用途插座电路（120 V、不超过 20 A）预先算好的最大电路长度，由 Rule 8-102(3) 提供，让常规住宅电路不必手算。专用电路不在其中，要用标准方法。
entries.backTranslation: It is a lookup table listing pre-calculated maximum circuit lengths for residential lighting and general-purpose receptacle circuits (120 V, no more than 20 A), provided by Rule 8-102(3), so ordinary residential circuits need no hand calculation. Dedicated circuits are not included and must use the standard method.

entries.original: For ordinary 120 V lighting and receptacle circuits up to 20 A in homes, the CEC provides precomputed maximum lengths (Rule 8-102(3), Table 68) — and where the service-to-panel run is under 20 m, the branch circuit may consume the full 5% by itself. Dedicated circuits (kitchen, fridge, heating) are excluded from the shortcut and use the standard calculation.
entries.translation: 对住宅里普通的 120 V 照明和插座电路（不超过 20 A），CEC 给出了预先算好的最大长度（Rule 8-102(3)、Table 68）——而且如果从供电进线到配电盘这一段不到 20 m，分支电路可以自己把 5% 全部用掉。专用电路（厨房、冰箱、供暖）不适用这个捷径，要走标准计算。
entries.backTranslation: For ordinary 120 V residential lighting and receptacle circuits (no more than 20 A), the CEC gives pre-calculated maximum lengths (Rule 8-102(3), Table 68) — and if the stretch from the service entrance to the panel is under 20 m, the branch circuit can use up the whole 5% by itself. Dedicated circuits (kitchen, fridge, heating) don't get this shortcut and must use the standard calculation.

entries.original: Is the 3% voltage drop rule mandatory in Canada?
entries.translation: 在加拿大，3% 电压降规则是强制的吗？
entries.backTranslation: In Canada, is the 3% voltage drop rule mandatory?

entries.original: : maximum 3% on a branch circuit, 3% on the feeder (including the consumer's service), and 5% combined from the service to the farthest point. An inspector can fail an over-limit run. If you remember one cross-border fact about voltage drop, make it this one.
entries.translation: ：分支电路最多 3%，馈线 3%（包括用户的供电进线），从供电进线到最远点合计 5%。检验员可以判超出限值的线路不合格。关于电压降，如果你只记住一条跨境差别，就记这一条。
entries.backTranslation: : branch circuits 3% maximum, feeders 3% (including the consumer's service entrance), 5% total from the service entrance to the farthest point. An inspector can fail a run that exceeds the limit. If you remember only one cross-border difference about voltage drop, make it this one.

entries.original: (2024 CEC). This settles the argument that splits every calculator forum. Computing at 100% of the breaker — as our conservative tables do — is always acceptable and leaves margin.
entries.translation: （2024 版 CEC）。这就了结了各大计算器论坛上争执不下的那个问题。按断路器的 100% 计算——就像我们那些偏保守的表格那样——任何时候都可以接受，而且还留有余量。
entries.backTranslation: (2024 CEC). That settles the question argued endlessly on the calculator forums. Calculating at 100% of the breaker — as our conservative tables do — is acceptable at any time, and still leaves margin.

entries.original: . Over the mandatory limit — upsize to #10 (3.3%) or shorten the run.
entries.translation: 。超出强制限值——加粗到 #10（3.3%），或者缩短线路。
entries.backTranslation: . Over the mandatory limit — go up to #10 (3.3%), or shorten the run.

entries.original: shorten the route
entries.translation: 缩短走线路径
entries.backTranslation: shorten the routing

entries.original: The formula, worked examples — and the big Canadian difference: here, the limit is the law.
entries.translation: 公式、算例——以及加拿大最大的不同：在这里，这个限值就是法规。
entries.backTranslation: The formula, worked examples — and Canada's biggest difference: here, this limit is the law.

entries.original: The 2024 CEC specifies the connected load if known, otherwise 80% of the overcurrent device rating. Calculating at the full breaker rating is a conservative, always-acceptable choice.
entries.translation: 2024 版 CEC 规定：已知时用已连接负载，否则取过电流保护装置额定值的 80%。按断路器的满额定值计算是偏保守的做法，任何时候都可以接受。
entries.backTranslation: The 2024 CEC specifies: use the connected load when it is known, otherwise take 80% of the overcurrent device's rating. Calculating at the breaker's full rating is the conservative approach and is acceptable at any time.

entries.original: (three-phase uses √3 instead of 2). K is the material constant — 12.9 for copper, 21.2 for aluminum. Circular mils is the wire's cross-section (#12 = 6,530; #6 = 26,240). Measure distance
entries.translation: （三相用 √3 代替 2）。K 是材料常数——铜为 12.9，铝为 21.2。圆密耳是导线的截面积（#12 = 6,530；#6 = 26,240）。量距离时只取
entries.backTranslation: (for three-phase, use √3 instead of 2). K is the material constant — 12.9 for copper, 21.2 for aluminum. Circular mils is the conductor's cross-sectional area (#12 = 6,530; #6 = 26,240). When measuring distance, take only

entries.original: What load do I use to calculate voltage drop under the CEC?
entries.translation: 按 CEC 算电压降时，该用哪个负载？
entries.backTranslation: When calculating voltage drop under the CEC, which load should be used?

entries.original: Yes. CEC Rule 8-102 is enforceable code: maximum 3% on a branch circuit, 3% on the feeder, 5% combined. This differs from the US, where the same figures are only an informational recommendation.
entries.translation: 是的。CEC Rule 8-102 是可强制执行的规范：分支电路最多 3%，馈线 3%，合计 5%。这一点和美国不同，在美国同样的数字只是资料性的建议。
entries.backTranslation: Yes. CEC Rule 8-102 is enforceable code: a maximum of 3% for branch circuits, 3% for feeders, 5% combined. This is different from the US, where the same numbers are only informational recommendations.

entries.original: CEC Tables 2 and 4 are numerically identical to NEC 310.16 in the 60/75/90°C columns at every shared size. The old “14 AWG copper is 20 A in Canada” difference was real in the 2012 edition. It was harmonized away around 2015–2018. Anyone repeating it is a decade out of date. But the free-air tables still differ. The harmonization is not total.
entries.translation: CEC Tables 2 and 4 在所有共有线规的 60/75/90°C 栏中，与 NEC 310.16 的数值完全相同。过去“加拿大 14 AWG 铜线是 20 A”的差异在 2012 年版中确实存在，但约在 2015–2018 年间已完成协调。今天仍重复这一说法，已经落后十年。不过，自由空气表仍然不同，协调并不全面。
entries.backTranslation: CEC Tables 2 and 4 are numerically identical to NEC 310.16 in the 60/75/90°C columns for all shared wire sizes. The old difference that “14 AWG copper is 20 A in Canada” really existed in the 2012 edition, but it was harmonized around 2015–2018. Anyone still repeating this claim today is a decade out of date. However, the free-air tables still differ, and harmonization is not complete.

entries.original: 1. Ampacity: mostly harmonized
entries.translation: 1. 载流量：大部分已经协调
entries.backTranslation: 1. Ampacity: mostly harmonized

entries.original: CEC:
entries.translation: CEC：
entries.backTranslation: CEC:

entries.original: Canada, three-phase where colour coding is required: red = A, black = B, blue = C.
entries.translation: 加拿大，在要求颜色编码的三相系统中：红色 = A，黑色 = B，蓝色 = C。
entries.backTranslation: Canada, in three-phase systems where colour coding is required: red = A, black = B, blue = C.

entries.original: A and B are effectively swapped across the border.
entries.translation: 跨过边境后，A 相和 B 相实际上对调了。
entries.backTranslation: After crossing the border, phases A and B are effectively swapped.

entries.original: 7. Conductor colour: the phases are not in the same order
entries.translation: 7. 导线颜色：相序并不相同
entries.backTranslation: 7. Conductor colours: the phase order is not the same

entries.original: The common US convention is black = A, red = B, blue = C. The NEC does not mandate ungrounded conductor colours; it prohibits white, grey, and green. The US pattern is convention and job specification.
entries.translation: 美国常见惯例是黑色 = A，红色 = B，蓝色 = C。NEC 并未规定非接地导线的颜色，只禁止使用白色、灰色和绿色。美国的配色是行业惯例和工程规范。
entries.backTranslation: The common U.S. convention is black = A, red = B, blue = C. The NEC does not specify colours for ungrounded conductors; it only prohibits white, grey, and green. The U.S. colour scheme is an industry convention and an engineering specification.

entries.original: Canadian RW90 is unjacketed cross-linked polyethylene. American THHN has a nylon jacket and is thinner for the same copper. RW90 is roughly 14–43% larger in cross-section, depending on size. Canadian EMT is also slightly smaller inside than its US counterpart. The two differences compound.
entries.translation: 加拿大 RW90 是无护套交联聚乙烯导线。美国 THHN 带尼龙护套，在铜导体相同的情况下更细。RW90 的截面积视线规不同大约增加 14–43%。加拿大 EMT 的内部空间也比美国对应产品略小。这两项差异会叠加。
entries.backTranslation: Canadian RW90 is an unjacketed cross-linked polyethylene conductor. U.S. THHN has a nylon jacket and is thinner with the same copper conductor. RW90 has approximately 14–43% more cross-sectional area, depending on the wire size. Canadian EMT also has slightly less interior space than its U.S. counterpart. These two differences add up.

entries.original: In one common case, the permitted count differs by a third. We reported nine conductors where the Canadian tables give six.
entries.translation: 在一个常见案例中，允许数量相差三分之一。加拿大表格给出六根，而我们曾报告九根。
entries.backTranslation: In one common case, the permitted quantities differ by one-third. The Canadian tables give six, while we previously reported nine.

entries.original: 6. Conduit fill: the one that caught us
entries.translation: 6. 导管填充：让我们栽跟头的差异
entries.backTranslation: 6. Conduit fill: the difference that tripped us up

entries.original: In the Rule 8-104 rated-equipment case, limit the conductor to 80% of its permitted ampacity.
entries.translation: 在 Rule 8-104 的额定设备情形下，将导线限制为其允许载流量的 80%。
entries.backTranslation: For equipment rated under Rule 8-104, limit the conductor to 80% of its permitted ampacity.

entries.original: The results land close, but these are not the same operation. Show the operation the local code uses.
entries.translation: 两种结果接近，但运算并不相同。应展示当地规范所采用的运算。
entries.backTranslation: The two results are close, but the calculations are not the same. Show the calculation used by the local code.

entries.original: 4. Continuous loads work in opposite directions
entries.translation: 4. 连续负载的处理方向相反
entries.backTranslation: 4. Continuous loads are handled in opposite directions

entries.original: Multiply the load by 125%.
entries.translation: 将负载乘以 125%。
entries.backTranslation: Multiply the load by 125%.

entries.original: The NEC lets you increase ampacity below 30°C ambient. The CEC does not. Its single-point rows give no cool-ambient credit below 30°C. Bringing the US habit north silently allows more current than the CEC does.
entries.translation: 环境温度低于 30°C 时，NEC 允许提高载流量。CEC 不允许。它的单点行在 30°C 以下不提供低温增益。把美国习惯带到加拿大，会在不知不觉中允许超过 CEC 规定的电流。
entries.backTranslation: When the ambient temperature is below 30°C, the NEC allows ampacity to be increased. The CEC does not. Its single-point rows provide no low-temperature credit below 30°C. Taking the U.S. practice to Canada can unknowingly permit more current than the CEC allows.

entries.original: 3. Canada gives no credit for a cool room
entries.translation: 3. 加拿大不给凉爽房间增加载流量
entries.backTranslation: 3. Canada gives no ampacity increase for a cool room

entries.original: Nearly every online source we found cites Canadian colour rules as “Rule 4-038.” In the current 26th edition there is no Rule 4-038. Section 4 ends at Rule 4-036, “Busbar.” The colour rule was Rule 4-038 in the 2012 edition. It is Rule 4-032 now. Sources agreeing with each other is not verification when they are copying each other.
entries.translation: 我们找到的几乎所有网络资料都把加拿大导线颜色规则写成“Rule 4-038”。现行 26th 版中并不存在 Rule 4-038。Section 4 到 Rule 4-036“Busbar”即结束。2012 年版的颜色规则确实是 Rule 4-038，现在则是 Rule 4-032。多个来源说法一致，并不代表经过核实，因为它们可能只是在互相抄写。
entries.backTranslation: Almost every online source we found lists the Canadian conductor-colour rule as “Rule 4-038.” Rule 4-038 does not exist in the current 26th edition. Section 4 ends at Rule 4-036, “Busbar.” The colour rule really was Rule 4-038 in the 2012 edition. It is now Rule 4-032. Multiple sources saying the same thing does not mean it has been verified, because they may simply be copying one another.

entries.original: 9. A citation that has been dead for over a decade
entries.translation: 9. 一条失效超过十年的引用
entries.backTranslation: 9. A citation that has been obsolete for more than a decade

entries.original: At ten current-carrying conductors, the NEC drops to 0.50. The CEC allows 0.70. Same bundle, different answer. This difference is current and easy to miss.
entries.translation: 当有十根载流导线时，NEC 降到 0.50，CEC 允许 0.70。同一组导线，答案不同。这项差异仍然有效，也很容易漏掉。
entries.backTranslation: With ten current-carrying conductors, the NEC drops to 0.50, while the CEC allows 0.70. The same group of conductors gives a different answer. This difference is still valid and easy to miss.

entries.original: 2. Conductor-count derating: a live difference
entries.translation: 2. 按导线数量降额：仍然存在的差异
entries.backTranslation: 2. Adjustment by conductor count: a difference that still exists

entries.original: Findings checked against CSA C22.1:24, Canadian Electrical Code, Part I, 26th edition (2024), and NEC 2023 (NFPA 70). Adoption is local and local amendments can change the result.
entries.translation: 这些发现依据 CSA C22.1:24、Canadian Electrical Code, Part I 26th 版（2024）以及 NEC 2023 (NFPA 70) 核实。各地采用时间不同，当地修订也可能改变结果。
entries.backTranslation: These findings were verified against CSA C22.1:24, Canadian Electrical Code, Part I, 26th edition (2024), and NEC 2023 (NFPA 70). Adoption timing varies by location, and local amendments may also change the result.

entries.original: Edition checked
entries.translation: 核实的版本
entries.backTranslation: Verified edition

entries.original: Yes, for the shared sizes and the 60/75/90°C in-raceway columns. The current CEC Tables 2 and 4 match NEC 310.16. Free-air tables still differ.
entries.translation: 是，但仅限共有线规以及导管内 60/75/90°C 栏。现行 CEC Tables 2 and 4 与 NEC 310.16 相同。自由空气表仍然不同。
entries.backTranslation: Yes, but only for shared wire sizes and the 60/75/90°C columns in raceways. The current CEC Tables 2 and 4 match NEC 310.16. The free-air tables still differ.

entries.original: Are Canadian and US ampacity tables the same?
entries.translation: 加拿大与美国的载流量表相同吗？
entries.backTranslation: Are Canadian and U.S. ampacity tables the same?

entries.original: No. RW90 is roughly 14–43% larger in cross-section than THHN, and Canadian EMT is slightly smaller inside. T90 lands within about 2% of THHN.
entries.translation: 不同。RW90 的截面积比 THHN 大约增加 14–43%，加拿大 EMT 的内部空间也略小。T90 与 THHN 的差距约在 2% 以内。
entries.backTranslation: No. RW90 has approximately 14–43% more cross-sectional area than THHN, and Canadian EMT also has slightly less interior space. T90 is within about 2% of THHN.

entries.original: Is conduit fill the same in Canada and the US?
entries.translation: 加拿大和美国的导管填充相同吗？
entries.backTranslation: Is conduit fill the same in Canada and the U.S.?

entries.original: Quick answers
entries.translation: 快速答案
entries.backTranslation: Quick answers

entries.original: Canada puts the higher-voltage-to-ground conductor on phase A under Rule 4-032. NEC 408.3(E) puts the high leg on phase B.
entries.translation: 根据 Rule 4-032，加拿大把对地电压较高的导线放在 A 相。NEC 408.3(E) 把高脚放在 B 相。
entries.backTranslation: Under Rule 4-032, Canada places the conductor with the higher voltage to ground on phase A. NEC 408.3(E) places the high leg on phase B.

entries.original: Which phase carries the high leg?
entries.translation: 哪一相是高脚？
entries.backTranslation: Which phase is the high leg?

entries.original: The 3% and 5% figures are recommendations in NEC Informational Notes. CEC Rule 8-102 makes voltage drop mandatory in Canada.
entries.translation: 3% 和 5% 在 NEC 信息性说明中是建议值。CEC Rule 8-102 在加拿大把电压降规定为强制要求。
entries.backTranslation: 3% and 5% are recommended values in the NEC Informational Notes. CEC Rule 8-102 makes voltage drop mandatory in Canada.

entries.original: Is the 3% voltage-drop figure a requirement?
entries.translation: 3% 电压降是强制要求吗？
entries.backTranslation: Is 3% voltage drop mandatory?

entries.original: On a 4-wire delta, Canada puts the higher-voltage-to-ground conductor on phase A under Rule 4-032. NEC 408.3(E) puts the high leg on phase B, the centre bus. An electrician looking where their home code taught them finds the wrong conductor.
entries.translation: 在 4 线三角形系统中，根据 Rule 4-032，加拿大把对地电压较高的导线放在 A 相。NEC 408.3(E) 把高脚放在 B 相，也就是中间母线。电工若按本国规范教的位置寻找，就会找到错误的导线。
entries.backTranslation: In a 4-wire delta system, Canada places the conductor with the higher voltage to ground on phase A under Rule 4-032. NEC 408.3(E) places the high leg on phase B, which is the centre busbar. An electrician looking in the location taught by their home country’s code will find the wrong conductor.

entries.original: 8. The high leg is on a different phase
entries.translation: 8. 高脚位于不同的相
entries.backTranslation: 8. The high leg is on a different phase

entries.original: Read how VoltDrop checks its numbers.
entries.translation: 了解 VoltDrop 如何核查数据。
entries.backTranslation: Learn how VoltDrop checks its data.

entries.original: Confirm the edition in force with the local inspection authority, and use a meter before touching any conductor.
entries.translation: 请向当地检查主管机构确认现行版本，并在接触任何导线前使用仪表测量。
entries.backTranslation: Confirm the current edition with the local inspection authority, and use a meter before touching any conductor.
